signals.title: [FEATURE]: Add font customization support to opencode.json config
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request I would like to request the ability to configure custom fonts (font family, size, and weight) through the opencode.json configuration file, similar to how VS Code handles editor.fontFamily in its settings. Proposed implementation: Add new optional fields to the config schema: ``` { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "editor": { "fontFamily": "Fira Code, JetBrains Mono, monospace", "fontSize": 14, "fontWeight": 400, "fontLigatures": true } } ``` Alternatively, this could be part of the tui configuration: ``` { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "tui": { "scroll_speed": 3, "diff_style": "auto", "fontFamily": "Fira Code, monospace", "fontSize": 14, "fontLigatures": true } } ``` What are the benefits of implementing this? 1. Enhanced developer experience: Programming-optimized fonts like Fira Code, JetBrains Mono, Cascadia Code, and Monaspace dramatically improve code readability with ligatures and better character distinction (0 vs O, 1 vs l vs I) Developers can match OpenCode's font with their other editors for consistency 2. Accessibility: Some developers need larger font sizes for visibility Dyslexia-friendly fonts like OpenDyslexic or Lexend can be configured Font weight adjustments help with eye strain and contrast preferences 3. Branding and theming: Organizations and teams can enforce brand-consistent typography Custom themes could include recommended fonts as part of the complete visual identity Professional recording/streaming setups benefit from carefully chosen fonts 4. Cross-platform consistency: Currently, font rendering depends on terminal configuration, which varies across iTerm2, Warp, Windows Terminal, Alacritty, etc. Having font config in OpenCode ensures consistent appearance regardless of terminal choice 5. Integration with existing workflow: Config-based font management aligns with OpenCode's philosophy of JSON-driven configuration Could be combined with theme selection for complete visual customization Would complement the existing theme option perfectly Additional considerations: Font fallback chains ensure compatibility across systems fontLigatures toggle allows users to enable/disable programming ligatures Config could validate against installed system fonts or provide helpful warnings Could support both global (~/.config/opencode/opencode.json) and per-project settings Example use case: A developer working on a BrandX-branded project could ship an opencode.json with: ``` { "theme": "brandx", "editor": { "fontFamily": "Fira Code, monospace", "fontSize": 13, "fontLigatures": true } } ``` This ensures every contributor sees the codebase with optimal, consistent typography that complements the custom theme. References: VS Code: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/settings#_font Popular coding fonts: [Fira Code](https://github.com/tonsky/FiraCode), [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/), [Cascadia Code](https://github.com/microsoft/cascadia-code)

signals.title: [FEATURE]: configuration profiles (per‑context setups)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request I’d like profiles for full configuration sets, not just auth. Specifically, I have multiple ‎`oh-my-opencode` configs that I currently swap manually, and I want to switch between them as profiles. What I want ￼ - Named profiles (e.g. Personal, Work, Client‑A, Client‑B) that each define: 1. Active configuration files / directories. 2. Enabled plugins / subagents / tools. 3. Default models and providers. 4. Per‑profile environment (env vars, project roots, workspace layout). - A fast way to switch profiles: 1. From the UI (visible selector). 2. Via a command / keybinding. - A clear indicator of the current profile so I don’t accidentally run the wrong config. Why this is useful ￼ - Different contexts (personal, work, different clients) need very different configurations and constraints. - Today, I have to: 1. Manually swap configuration folders / files. 2. Restart or reload things to pick up the new setup. 3. Remember which config is currently active, which is error‑prone. - Profiles would: 1. Make context switching fast and safe. 2. Keep work and personal / client setups clearly separated. 3. Encourage focused, minimal configs instead of one huge, overloaded configuration. Example use case ￼ - One profile for personal hacking (my own tools, models, repos). - One profile per client / employer (their tools, providers, repos, security rules). - For example, I currently maintain multiple configurations (including ‎`oh-my-opencode`‑based setups) and have to juggle them manually; profiles would let me encode these as first‑class switches inside OpenCode itself. Possible implementation ￼ - Introduce a Profile abstraction that: - Points to a config root and optional overrides (models, tools, env). - Is persisted and selectable from the UI and command palette. - Reload active configuration when the profile changes, without needing manual file juggling.

signals.title: Missing {file:} reference causes entire agent config to fail
signals.text: ## Summary When an `opencode.json` contains a `{file:./path}` reference that doesn't exist on disk, OpenCode rejects the **entire** agent configuration with a hard error: ``` Error: Configuration is invalid at /var/www/extrachill.com/opencode.json: bad file reference: "{file:./AGENTS.md}" /var/www/extrachill.com/AGENTS.md does not exist ``` This means no agent files get loaded at all — including the ones that DO exist. ## Expected Behavior A missing `{file:}` reference should either: 1. Be treated as a soft warning (skip the missing file, load the rest) 2. Resolve to empty string with a logged warning The current behavior silently breaks the entire agent context because one optional file is missing. ## Reproduction 1. Create `opencode.json` with multiple `{file:}` references in `agent.build.prompt` 2. Ensure one of the referenced files doesn't exist 3. Run `opencode agent list` or start a session ## Context This came up in a wp-opencode setup where `AGENTS.md` wasn't created (setup script crashed before that phase), but the DM agent files (SOUL.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md) all existed. The single missing file caused none of them to be injected.

signals.title: Multiple local clones of same repo share one project identity, breaking file change tracking
signals.text: ## Summary When you have multiple local clones of the same git repository (same remote origin URL), OpenCode treats them all as a single project. This breaks file change tracking and causes visual issues in the project selector. ## Environment - OpenCode version: 1.1.53 - OS: Linux (Ubuntu) - Three local clones of the same repo in separate directories: - `/home/user/Projects/project` - `/home/user/Projects/project-8000` - `/home/user/Projects/project-8080` - All three have the same git remote: `git@github.com:org/repo.git` ## Problem OpenCode generates the project ID from the git remote origin URL rather than the local directory path. This means all three clones resolve to the same project ID (e.g. `5ca09febb1b87758aeeb2c8949774a8bbafc6c8f`), sharing a single project record and a single snapshot directory. ### Consequences 1. **File change tracking breaks** — The snapshot git config's `worktree` can only point to one directory at a time. Whichever clone was opened last overwrites the worktree path, so file changes are not detected in the other clones. In my case, the snapshot pointed to `project-8080` while I was working in `project-8000`, so session file diffs were always empty. 2. **Project selector shows wrong colors** — On the project selection screen, each clone initially has a distinct icon color. But once you select any one of them, all three switch to the same color because they share the same project record and `icon.color` value. 3. **Only one project record exists** — There is a single JSON file in `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/project/` for all three directories, with only one `worktree` value. ## Expected Behavior Each local directory should be treated as a separate project, even if they share the same git remote URL. The project ID should incorporate the local worktree path (or some other disambiguator) so that: - Each clone gets its own snapshot directory with the correct `worktree` path - File change tracking works independently in each clone - Each clone can have its own icon color and name in the project selector ## Workaround Manually deleting the snapshot directory (`~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<project_id>`) and restarting OpenCode causes it to recreate the snapshot with the correct worktree for the currently active clone — but this only fixes one clone at a time and the underlying identity collision remains.

signals.title: [FEATURE]:Frontend UI extensibility for plugins (Custom Settings & Dialogs)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Currently, the @opencode-ai/plugin architecture is exclusively backend-focused (Node/Bun). While it provides excellent support for intercepting lifecycle hooks, registering commands/tools, and modifying configurations, it completely lacks mechanisms for frontend UI extensibility. A concrete example of this limitation arises when attempting to refactor the built-in experimental war agent into a standalone plugin to clean up the core codebase. The backend logic and prompts can be successfully migrated via the config hook. However, the plugin loses its dedicated settings UI (dialog-war-config.tsx) and specific trigger buttons (prompt-input.tsx) because plugins cannot currently inject custom SolidJS components or HTML into the frontend. The only workaround right now is hardcoding agent-specific UI logic directly into the core packages/app repository. This tightly couples the code and defeats the purpose of having a modular plugin system. Furthermore, while MCP (Model Context Protocol) is fantastic for exposing tools and context, it does not address these client-side UI rendering limitations. ### Describe the solution you'd like I would love to see a frontend extensibility mechanism introduced into the plugin architecture. Here are a few potential approaches, ranging from highly flexible to highly secure: Micro-frontend / Dynamic Component Loading: Allow plugins to bundle a ui.js module that exports standard SolidJS components or Web Components. The core app could dynamically import() these and provide specific mounting points (e.g., registerSettingsTab, registerAgentConfigDialog). Iframe / WebView Injection (Safest & Simplest): Allow plugins to expose an endpoint or a static HTML file. The frontend could provide a hook like registerWebviewPanel(id, url) and render an <iframe> within the settings dialog or side panel. This ensures complete decoupling and sandbox security. Schema-driven UI Generation: If running arbitrary third-party code on the frontend is a security concern, plugins could return a JSON Schema describing their required configuration fields (e.g., dropdowns for commanderModel, editModel). The frontend could then dynamically render a generic, native-looking form based on this schema. ### Describe alternatives you've considered Modifying .opencode.json directly: Users have to manually edit the JSON file to change plugin-specific settings. This offers a significantly poorer user experience compared to native UI dropdowns and toggles. Tool-based configuration: Exposing a configure_agent tool and asking the AI to change the settings for the user. While functional, it is much slower and less deterministic than a simple UI interaction. Forking the repository: Maintaining a hardcoded fork of packages/app strictly to preserve custom UI components for proprietary or experimental agents. ### Additional context Frontend UI extensibility is the missing piece for a truly modular Opencode ecosystem. Implementing this would empower developers to build rich, interactive plugins—such as custom agent dashboards, specialized workflow visualizations, and seamless third-party integrations—without perpetually bloating the core application repository.

signals.title: bug: mouse escape sequences garbled after TUI exit
signals.text: ## Description After exiting the opencode TUI (via quit, Ctrl+C, or process stop), mouse escape sequences appear as garbled text in the terminal: ``` 35;89;19M35;84;20M35;76;22M35;71;23M35;67;23M35;67;24M35;67;25M35... ``` This is a separate issue from in-session mouse garbling (#3199 / PR #19520). The in-session bug is about fragmented SGR sequences leaking through StdinParser timeouts during active use. This bug occurs **after** the TUI has exited. ## Root Cause This is an upstream bug in `@opentui/core`'s `cleanupBeforeDestroy()` method. During renderer destruction, `stdin.setRawMode(false)` is called (re-enabling terminal ECHO) **before** mouse tracking is disabled. Any mouse events arriving during this window get echoed as raw escape sequence bytes. The correct ordering already exists in `@opentui/core`'s `suspend()` method, which calls `disableMouse()` before `setRawMode(false)`. **Upstream issue:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/issues/904 **Upstream fix PR:** https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/905 ## Reproduction 1. Run `opencode` 2. Move the mouse while the TUI is active 3. Exit the TUI (quit or Ctrl+C) 4. Move the mouse in the shell immediately after exit 5. Garbled escape sequences appear ## Workaround A `patchedDependencies` patch for `@opentui/core` can fix this by adding `disableMouse()` + stdin drain before `setRawMode(false)` in `cleanupBeforeDestroy()`. A PR with this patch is forthcoming. ## Environment - macOS / Linux - Affects `@opentui/core@0.1.90` and `@opentui/core@0.1.95`

signals.title: Memory Megathread
signals.text: We have scattered reports of memory issues so we are going to tackle them all in a central place. PLEASE DO NOT RUN YOUR LLM AND SUGGEST SOLUTIONS IT IS ALWAYS WRONG What we need help with is collecting heap snapshots. There are two ways to do that. Manual snapshot flow - run opencode (terminal not desktop) - use it until memory has grown (we don't need crazy numbers, once it hits 1-2gb it should help) - press ctrl+p and select heap snapshot - ui will freeze while it is generated - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit Automatic snapshot flow - run opencode with `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1`, for example `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode` - use it until memory grows past around 2gb - opencode checks memory once a minute and automatically writes a heap snapshot when rss is above 2gb - snapshots are written to the log directory as `.heapsnapshot` files - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit and mention that you used the automatic flow If you follow this we can almost always trace the issue and fix it

signals.title: Session title agent generates title from injected memory/system context rather than actual user message
signals.text:
### Description ## Description When automatic session title generation runs, it passes the full rendered message history to the title model via `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect`. If a memory MCP server injects prior conversation summaries or facts into the system prompt or as synthetic message parts, the title model receives that injected content and generates a title based on it rather than the actual user message. ## Expected Behaviour The title should reflect the content of the current user message only. ## Actual Behaviour The title reflects injected memory context from prior sessions. Starting a session with "hi" produced: > "Discussion on Workaround and GitHub Issue Regarding Roampal Data Location Setup and Patching cli.py" — an accurate summary of the *previous* session's content, surfaced via memory context injection. ## Root Cause In `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, the title generation constructs its payload as: ```ts const context = input.history.slice(0, idx + 1) messages: [ { role: "user", content: "Generate a title for this conversation:
" }, ...yield* MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect(context, mdl) ] ``` `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect` renders the full message including injected memory/system content. The title model then titles based on that rather than the actual user message. ## Suggested Fix Pass only the raw text of the first real user message to the title model: ```ts const userText = firstUser.parts .filter(p => p.type === "text") .map(p => p.text) .join("
") messages: [ { role: "user", content: "Generate a title for this conversation:
" + userText } ] ``` This strips all synthetic/injected parts before passing to the title model. ### Plugins roampal-core ### OpenCode version 1.4.6 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a memory MCP server that injects prior session context into the conversation (e.g. Roampal, mem0, or similar). 2. Start a new session with a short or unrelated message (e.g. "hi"). 3. Observe that the generated session title reflects content from a *previous* session rather than the current one. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windwos 11 ### Terminal PWSH

signals.title: opencode upgrade fails with 403 (doesn't respect GITHUB_TOKEN)
signals.text: ### Describe the bug When running `opencode upgrade` from behind a proxy/VPN, the command frequently fails with a 403 error due to GitHub API rate limiting for unauthenticated requests (60 requests/hour/IP). The command appears to make an anonymous request to `https://api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode/releases/latest`. Even if the user has a valid `GITHUB_TOKEN` exported in their environment, or is authenticated via the GitHub CLI (`gh auth login`), `opencode` does not seem to utilize these credentials to authenticate the API request. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Connect to a shared proxy/VPN (to simulate an IP with exhausted unauthenticated GitHub API limits). 2. Export a valid `GITHUB_TOKEN` or authenticate with `gh auth login`. 3. Run `opencode upgrade` 4. See error: ``` Error: Unexpected error, check log file... StatusCode: non 2xx status code (403 GET https://api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode/releases/latest) ``` ### Expected behavior `opencode upgrade` should check for the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable and use it to authenticate the request to the GitHub API. This would increase the rate limit to 5000/hour and prevent rate limiting for users behind shared proxies. ### Environment - OS: Linux - OpenCode Version: 1.14.18

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Plan mode should allow planning-related CLI tools (gh, glab, ticket management, diagrams)
signals.text: - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request **Problem** Plan mode's system prompt uses absolute language that prevents ALL bash commands except read/inspect operations. This blocks legitimate planning activities like: - Creating/updating GitHub issues via `gh issue create`, `gh pr create` - Creating/updating GitLab issues via `glab issue create`, `glab mr create` - Generating and committing planning diagrams or documentation artifacts This forces users into build mode for these activities, which often leads to the agent executing code changes prematurely before planning is complete. **Problematic responses in plan mode** When asked to create a GitHub issue or GitLab ticket in plan mode, the agent responds with variations of: > "I'm in plan mode and cannot execute commands. I can only read and analyze. Please switch to build mode to create the issue." > "Plan mode restricts me to read-only operations. Creating a GitHub issue requires running `gh issue create`, which I cannot do in this mode." This happens because the system prompt (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/plan.txt`) states: ``` STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: ANY file edits, modifications, or system changes. Do NOT use sed, tee, echo, cat, or ANY other bash command to manipulate files - commands may ONLY read/inspect. ...ZERO exceptions. ``` And the `## Important` section reinforces: ``` you MUST NOT make any edits, run any non-readonly tools (including changing configs or making commits), or otherwise make any changes to the system. ``` The experimental plan prompt (`prompt.ts:279`) has the same restriction: *"run any non-readonly tools (including changing configs or making commits)"* **Root cause** The plan agent's bash tool is NOT hard-denied in the permission config (`agent.ts:124-146`) — it inherits `"allow"` from defaults. The model's refusal is caused entirely by the system prompt's absolutist language, which makes no distinction between "modifying source code" and "managing project tickets." **Recommended fix** (3 files, ~35 lines changed) 1. **`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/plan.txt`** — Reframe restrictions from "ALL commands" to "source code modifications." Add an explicit "Allowed planning activities" section listing issue/ticket management (`gh`, `glab`), PR/MR management, documentation artifacts, and project queries. 2. **`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`** (experimental plan prompt) — Same distinction: restrict source code edits, explicitly permit planning CLI tools. 3. **`packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts`** — Add explicit `bash: { "gh *": "allow", "glab *": "allow" }` permission rules to the plan agent config, making the intent unambiguous at the permission layer (not just prompt). **Benefits** - Users can stay in plan mode for the entire planning workflow (research → create tickets → write specs → create PR) without being forced into build mode - Source code is still fully protected from modification - The permission system and the system prompt are aligned in intent **OpenCode version:** v1.14.21 **OS:** macOS (Darwin) **Terminal:** Ghostty

signals.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro via zen/go: reasoning_content inconsistency causes "must be passed back to the API" error in multi-turn tool calls
signals.text: ## Description When using DeepSeek V4 Pro via the `opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` endpoint, multi-turn conversations with tool calls fail intermittently with: ``` Error from provider (DeepSeek): The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. ``` ## Root Cause DeepSeek V4 Pro's thinking mode is **all-or-nothing**: once ANY assistant message in the conversation history includes `reasoning_content`, ALL subsequent assistant messages MUST also include it. If even one message lacks it (e.g., a `tool_calls` message where reasoning was omitted), the API rejects the entire request. ## Reproduction (minimal) **FAILS** — first assistant has `reasoning_content`, second (tool_calls) does NOT: ```json { "model": "deepseek-v4-pro", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "帮我查下文件"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "好的，我来帮你查。", "reasoning_content": "用户需要查文件，我应该用工具。"}, {"role": "user", "content": "读SOUL.md"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [{"id":"c1","type":"function","function":{"name":"read","arguments":"{\"path\":\"SOUL.md\"}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "SOUL内容"}, {"role": "user", "content": "写个总结"} ], "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"read","description":"read","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}}}}} ], "max_tokens": 20 } ``` → Returns: `"The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API."` **PASSES** — ALL assistant messages consistently have `reasoning_content`: ```json { "model": "deepseek-v4-pro", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "读SOUL.md"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [{"id":"c1","type":"function","function":{"name":"read","arguments":"{\"path\":\"SOUL.md\"}"}}], "reasoning_content": "需要读文件，调用read工具。"}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "# SOUL\n我是时崎狂三"}, {"role": "user", "content": "总结"} ], "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"read","description":"read","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}}}}} ], "max_tokens": 30 } ``` → Works fine (200 OK). ## Impact - Any multi-turn conversation using DeepSeek V4 Pro with tool calls (e.g., OpenClaw, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) will fail after the first tool call - The zen/go proxy appears to sometimes omit `reasoning_content` from tool_calls responses, creating the inconsistency - This is the typical pattern for coding agents where model generates text → calls tools → continues conversation ## Suggested Fix The zen/go proxy should either: 1. Ensure `reasoning_content` is consistently included in ALL assistant messages when thinking mode is active, including tool call messages, OR 2. Strip `reasoning_content` from ALL messages in the history before forwarding to DeepSeek if consistency cannot be guaranteed ## Environment - Endpoint: `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` - Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` - Timestamp: 2026-04-30 03:30 UTC

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Support Multiple Skills in a Single Prompt — Critical for Multi-Framework Workflows
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Description Currently, OpenCode does not support specifying multiple skills simultaneously in a single prompt. When I input multiple skill commands such as `/vue3 /vue-router-v4`, only the first skill (`/vue3`) is loaded and activated. The second skill (`/vue-router-v4`) is incorrectly treated as plain user input rather than being parsed and loaded as an additional skill. ## Current Behavior - **Input:** `/vue3 /vue-router-v4` - **Actual Result:** Only the `/vue3` skill is loaded. `/vue-router-v4` is passed as raw text to the model without skill activation. ## Expected Behavior Both `/vue3` and `/vue-router-v4` skills should be parsed, loaded, and activated concurrently, allowing the model to leverage the context and capabilities from multiple skills simultaneously within the same session. ## Use Case & Importance In real-world development, projects rarely rely on a single technology in isolation. For example: - A Vue 3 project almost always uses **Vue Router** alongside it. - A React project frequently requires both **React** and **React Router** context. - Full-stack tasks often involve both **frontend** and **backend** skills at the same time. Without support for multiple skills, users are forced to: 1. Choose only one skill and lose critical context from others. 2. Manually paste documentation or context for secondary technologies. 3. Break a single coherent task into multiple fragmented sessions. This limitation significantly reduces OpenCode's effectiveness for complex, multi-framework workflows and negatively impacts the overall developer experience. ## Request I would greatly appreciate it if the team could consider implementing multi-skill activation in a single prompt. This enhancement would be incredibly valuable for handling realistic development scenarios where multiple technologies intersect, and it would make OpenCode substantially more powerful for everyday use. Thank you for your time and for maintaining such a promising tool!
signals.author: pengln

signals.title: Regression: plugin provider.models() hook no longer populates custom providers (post #25167)
signals.text: ## Summary After PR #25167 (commit `560baae`, merged April 30 2026, shipped in v1.14.x), the plugin `provider.models()` hook can no longer populate models for **custom providers** — i.e. providers declared by the user in `opencode.jsonc` whose `id` is not present in the public models.dev catalog. This is a regression: the same plugin code worked on versions shipped before April 30. ## Root cause (located in `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`) The PR moved the plugin hook iteration from running *after* config processing to *before*, and switched the lookup from the live `providers` map to the pre-config `database` map: **Before (worked):** ```ts // ran AFTER configProviders were merged into providers for (const hook of plugins) { ... const provider = providers[providerID] // live map, includes user-config providers if (!provider) continue provider.models = await models(provider, ...) } ``` **After PR #25167 (broken for custom providers):** ```ts // runs BEFORE configProviders loop for (const hook of plugins) { ... const provider = database[providerID] // models.dev catalog only if (!provider) continue // ← skips any custom provider provider.models = await models(provider, ...) } ``` `database` is built from `modelsDev` (the public models.dev catalog at `~/.cache/opencode/models.json`). Any provider declared exclusively in user config — e.g. a local proxy, a self-hosted endpoint, or any other non-catalog provider — is not in `database`, so `if (!provider) continue` short-circuits the hook entirely. The PR's stated intent (\"ensure user config takes precedence over plugin hooks\") is reasonable, but the implementation also removed the ability for plugins to register models for non-catalog providers. ## Reproduction 1. Declare a custom provider in `opencode.jsonc` not present in models.dev (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible local proxy): ```jsonc { \"provider\": { \"my-custom-proxy\": { \"npm\": \"@ai-sdk/openai-compatible\", \"name\": \"My Custom Proxy\", \"options\": { \"baseURL\": \"http://localhost:9090/v1\", \"apiKey\": \"unused\" } } } } ``` 2. Write a plugin that exposes the v2 `provider.models()` hook: ```js export default { id: \"my-custom-proxy\", server: async () => ({ provider: { id: \"my-custom-proxy\", models: async () => ({ \"some-model\": { id: \"some-model\", providerID: \"my-custom-proxy\", api: { id: \"some-model\", url: \"http://localhost:9090/v1\", npm: \"@ai-sdk/openai-compatible\" }, name: \"Some Model\", capabilities: { /* ... */ }, cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cache: { read: 0, write: 0 } }, limit: { context: 200000, output: 64000 }, status: \"active\", options: {}, headers: {} } }), }, }), }; ``` 3. **Expected**: The provider appears with the model the hook returned. 4. **Actual on v1.14.x**: The provider is registered (because the static config block exists), but the plugin hook is skipped entirely. No models from the hook appear; only models defined statically in `opencode.jsonc` show up. Adding the provider's id to the static models.dev catalog isn't user-facing, so users with self-hosted/proxy providers cannot rely on dynamic model discovery via plugins anymore. ## Impact This breaks any plugin that augments a non-catalog provider with dynamically discovered models — e.g. local LLM proxies that expose `/v1/models`, internal corporate gateways, OpenAI-compatible self-hosted servers. Users now have to hardcode every model in `opencode.jsonc` and update it manually whenever the upstream catalog changes. ## Suggested fix Move the plugin hook iteration back to run *after* `configProviders` are merged into `providers`, and look up `providers[providerID]` instead of `database[providerID]`. The original ordering supported both catalog and custom providers. To preserve PR #25167's intent (user config taking precedence over plugin hooks), apply config models on top of plugin-supplied models in a final reconciliation pass, rather than by reordering the hooks. ## Environment - OpenCode `v1.14.33` - macOS (Apple Silicon) - Plugin SDK `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.4.7`

signals.title: LLM response headers are discarded, preventing plugins from accessing proxy routing metadata
signals.text: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Current behavior When using a LiteLLM proxy with an auto router (complexity router, semantic router), the actual model selected by the router is returned in HTTP response headers like `x-litellm-model-api-base` and `llm_provider-x-ms-deployment-name`. The AI SDK captures these headers on the `finish-step` stream event (`value.response.headers`), but `processor.ts` only reads `value.usage`, `value.providerMetadata`, and `value.finishReason` — `value.response` is discarded entirely. This means plugins cannot determine which model actually served a request when using proxy-based routing. ### Expected behavior Response headers from LLM provider HTTP responses should be available on the assistant message so plugins can access proxy routing metadata and other provider-specific response headers. ### How to reproduce 1. Configure OpenCode with a LiteLLM proxy using a complexity/semantic router 2. Send a message through the router 3. Write a plugin listening for `message.updated` events 4. Observe that `msg.responseHeaders` does not exist — the plugin can only see the router alias in `msg.modelID` ### OpenCode version dev (latest) ### Platform macOS ### Additional context The `APIError` schema in the same file already has a `responseHeaders` field for error responses. This change extends the same pattern to successful responses. Example plugin that would use this: https://github.com/jtbnz/opencode-routed-model
signals.author: jtbnz

signals.title: Husky pre-push hook may fail to find Bun due to minimal PATH in Git hooks
signals.text: ### Description Git runs hook scripts with a **minimal environment**. In practice, `PATH` inside hooks often does **not** include directories that interactive shells add from profile scripts (for example `~/.bun/bin` after the default Bun install). The root `.husky/pre-push` hook invokes `bun` directly (version check followed by `bun typecheck`). Contributors can end up with **Bun working in their normal terminal** but **`git push` failing** inside the hook with errors such as `bun: command not found`, even though the repository expects Bun via `packageManager` in `package.json`. ### Expected behavior Pre-push hooks should reliably find `bun` for typical local setups (including default Bun install location), or the contribution docs should prominently state required PATH customization for hooks. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install Bun using the standard installer so the binary lives under `~/.bun/bin` and your shell PATH is updated via rc files. 2. Ensure `bun` is **not** on the PATH Git uses when running hooks without those rc files (common on Linux desktops / minimal hook env). 3. Clone the repo, make a commit, run `git push` to trigger `.husky/pre-push`. 4. Observe the hook fail when `bun` is not resolved. ### Suggested direction (optional) Prepend Bun’s bin directory inside the hook, e.g. `export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"`, before calling `bun`, so the hook environment matches typical developer setups. ### Environment - **OS**: Linux (also likely affects environments where GUI Git clients invoke hooks with restricted PATH). - **OpenCode**: `dev` / current mainline (hook content subject to drift). _No plugins / runtime version applicable beyond the husky/Git hook._
signals.author: JackLuguibin

signals.title: Windows auto-update stopped preserving custom install directory and reinstalls to %LocalAppData%\\Programs
signals.text: ### Description On Windows, OpenCode desktop auto-update no longer preserves the original custom install directory. My original installation was a machine-wide install at: `D:\OpenCode` This worked correctly for earlier updates. But in the last few days, auto-update started launching the downloaded installer and installing a new copy under: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop` As a result, I now have two installs: - old install: `D:\OpenCode` - new per-user install: `%LocalAppData%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop` The new desktop/start-menu shortcuts were also recreated to point to the `%LocalAppData%` install. ### Expected behavior Auto-update should preserve the existing install location (`D:\OpenCode`), or at minimum preserve the existing installation mode/location instead of silently switching from machine-wide/custom-dir install to per-user install in `%LocalAppData%\Programs`. ### Actual behavior Recent updates are performed by running the cached installer, and the install location switches to `%LocalAppData%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop`. ### Timeline My local evidence suggests this regression started between May 10 and May 11, 2026. #### Previously working - `2026-05-08 15:19` - `D:\OpenCode` was updated successfully - version became `1.14.41` #### First signs of failure On `2026-05-10`, updater attempted to install `1.14.46` multiple times: - `2026-05-10 19:52:15` - `2026-05-10 20:18:21` - `2026-05-10 20:23:23` But after restart, app still reported: - `version: 1.14.41` #### Wrong-location install actually happens On `2026-05-11 13:18:17`, updater executed: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\@opencode-aidesktop-updater\pending\opencode-desktop-win-x64.exe --updated --force-run` After that: - `%LocalAppData%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop\OpenCode.exe` became `1.14.48` - `D:\OpenCode\OpenCode.exe` remained `1.14.41` - desktop/start-menu shortcuts for current user were recreated and now point to `%LocalAppData%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop` ### Relevant logs `main.log` repeatedly shows: - `disableWebInstaller is set to false` - `Install on explicit quitAndInstall` - `Executing: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\@opencode-aidesktop-updater\pending\opencode-desktop-win-x64.exe with args: --updated,--force-run` Example from `2026-05-11`: ```text [2026-05-11 13:18:11.977] [info] installing downloaded update { version: '1.14.48' } [2026-05-11 13:18:17.980] [info] Install on explicit quitAndInstall [2026-05-11 13:18:17.982] [info] Executing: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\@opencode-aidesktop-updater\pending\opencode-desktop-win-x64.exe with args: --updated,--force-run ``` ### Additional context I checked the public Electron builder config in the repo and noticed Windows uses NSIS with: - `oneClick: false` - `allowToChangeInstallationDirectory: true` I did not see obvious logic to force reuse of the previous machine-wide/custom install path during auto-update. This looks like a regression where auto-update now switches installation mode/location instead of preserving the existing install. ### Environment - OS: Windows - Original install location: `D:\OpenCode` - New unexpected install location: `%LocalAppData%\Programs\@opencode-aidesktop`

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Agent Activity Panel -- sidebar view for monitoring running background agents
signals.text: ## Summary When orchestrating multiple background agents in parallel (e.g., `explore`, `librarian`, `oracle`), there's currently no way to monitor their status without calling `background_output()` manually. A dedicated sidebar/panel showing live agent activity would greatly improve visibility into multi-agent workflows. ## Problem Right now, when agents are spawned with `run_in_background=true`, the user has zero visibility into: - **How many agents** are currently running - **What each agent is doing** (task description / current step) - **Their status** (running / completed / failed) - **Their partial output** (live progress) The only way to check is to wait for a system notification and then call `background_output(task_id="...")` -- which is a pull-based, reactive model with no live visibility. ## Proposed Solution Add an **Agent Activity Panel** in the sidebar (similar to a CI/CD pipeline view) that shows all background agents with their real-time status. ### Mockup ``` +- Agents ──────────────────────────────+ | | | 🟡 explore "Find auth patterns…" | <- click to expand | 🟡 librarian "JWT security docs…" | <- click to expand | ✅ oracle "Architecture review" | <- click to see output | ❌ explore "Find error handlers" | <- click to see error | | +───────────────────────────────────────+ ``` ### Clicking an agent entry expands to show: - Full task description / prompt - Live streaming output (if still running) - Final result (if completed) - Error details (if failed) - Start time + elapsed duration ## User Story > As a power user running complex multi-agent workflows, I want to see all active background agents in the sidebar at a glance, so I can monitor their progress and click into any agent to view real-time output -- without having to wait for completion notifications. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Sidebar panel lists all background agents spawned in the current session - [ ] Each entry shows: agent type, task description snippet, status icon (running / done / failed) - [ ] Clicking an entry opens a detail view with full output - [ ] Running agents show live/streaming output as it arrives - [ ] Panel updates in real-time (no manual refresh needed) - [ ] Completed/failed agents remain visible (dismissible) ## Context This is especially valuable for workflows where 3-5 agents run in parallel (e.g., parallel codebase exploration + external docs research + architecture consultation). Currently the UX feels like "fire and forget" with no control panel. Related to the overall goal of making multi-agent orchestration more transparent and manageable from the UI.
signals.author: zh-zimoer

signals.title: [Bug] OpenCode leaks temporary .so files in /tmp, consuming hundreds of GB over time
signals.text: ### Description ## Title: [Bug] OpenCode leaks temporary .so files in /tmp, consuming hundreds of GB over time ### Environment - OS: CentOS 7 / Linux x86_64 - OpenCode: latest (running May 2026) - Shell: bash ### Summary OpenCode generates temporary ELF shared object (`.so`) files in `/tmp` and **never cleans them up**. Over time, this accumulates into hundreds of gigabytes of disk space consumed by orphaned files. ### Reproducible Steps 1. Run OpenCode CLI for an extended period (days/weeks) 2. Observe `/tmp` directory ### Observed Behavior - OpenCode creates hidden `.so` files in `/tmp` with naming pattern: - `.5fff*-00000000.so` (4.3 MB each) - `.7bef*-00000000.so` (4.5 MB each) - `.fbff*-00000000.so` (4.5 MB each) - These are ELF 64-bit LSB shared objects (`file` output: "ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, not stripped") - New files are generated continuously (creation timestamps within seconds of current time) - **Old files are never deleted** — they accumulate indefinitely ### Impact On one system running OpenCode: | Metric | Before Cleanup | After Cleanup | |--------|---------------|---------------| | `/tmp` size | 728 GB | 252 MB | | `.so` file count | ~154,000 | 0 | | Disk usage | 1.8T / 1.9T (99%) | 1.1T / 1.9T (60%) | The system was running at 99% disk capacity, leaving only 30 GB free on a 1.9 TB disk. ### Root Cause Analysis Using `lsof`, confirmed that running `.opencode` processes hold these files as memory-mapped regions: ``` .opencode 15606 root mem REG ... /tmp/.7befcfab9d7f5ff9-00000000.so .opencode 27137 root mem REG ... /tmp/.7bef5fffbdff7fbf-00000000.so .opencode 72378 root mem REG ... /tmp/.5fffa7f6acff5fe7-00000000.so ... ``` This suggests OpenCode is generating JIT-compiled or dynamically-loaded shared libraries (possibly from V8 code caching or WASM compilation) but lacks any cleanup mechanism — no tmpwatch integration, no file rotation, no cleanup on process exit. ### Expected Behavior - Temporary files should be cleaned up when the process exits - Or at minimum, a bounded number of files should be retained (e.g., LRU eviction) - Or use a dedicated temp directory (e.g. `/tmp/opencode/`) that is cleaned on startup ### Workaround Added a cron job to clean old `.so` files daily: ``` 0 2 * * * find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name ".*.so" -type f -mtime +1 -delete ``` ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_
signals.author: a1667834841

signals.title: Renderer crashes with STATUS_BREAKPOINT when workspace path contains CJK characters
signals.text: ### Description Environment - OpenCode Desktop: v1.15.7 - OS: Windows 11 Home China 10.0.26200 - Electron: 41.2.1 / Chromium 146.0.7680.188 Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a workspace directory with CJK (Chinese) characters in the path, e.g. D:\插件与编程研发\智能体工作区\my-project\ 2. Place an AGENTS.md or OPENCLAW_RESTART_PROMPT.md in a parent or sibling directory that references large data assets (e.g., ~90MB of ChromaDB vectors, JSON files) 3. Open the workspace in OpenCode Desktop Expected Behavior Workspace opens normally, no crash. Actual Behavior 1. Memory spikes to ~5000MB within 30-60 seconds 2. Renderer process crashes with exitCode: -2147483645 (0x80000003, STATUS_BREAKPOINT) 3. Window goes white and becomes unresponsive In v1.15.6, the crash manifested as a JavaScript error instead: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'keys') at MessageTimeline.createMemo.equals Additional Findings 1. Config file scanning scope: OpenCode appears to scan not only ancestor directories but also sibling directories for AGENTS.md, .opencode/, and .claude/ config files. In my case, D:\插件与编程研发\opencode\AGENTS.md (in a separate project) was being picked up when opening D:\插件与编程研發\智能体工作区\PAA_v3. 2. CJK path trigger: The identical project directory copied to a pure ASCII path (D:\test_parent\PAA_v3) works without issues. The crash only occurs when the path contains CJK characters, suggesting a Dawn/WebGPU or Chromium file-path handling issue in the renderer. 3. OPENCLAW_RESTART_PROMPT.md amplification: When this file references large data directories, OpenCode attempts to load/index all of them at startup, causing the memory spike that triggers the crash. 4. Persistent crash loop: opencode.global.dat saves server.lastProject pointing to the crashing workspace, causing the crash to repeat on every subsequent launch until the key is manually cleaned. Workaround - Move the workspace to a pure ASCII path (e.g., D:\PAA_v3) - Rename OPENCLAW_RESTART_PROMPT.md and AGENTS.md to .bak to prevent auto-scanning - Clean opencode.global.dat to remove references to the crashing workspace ### Plugins NO ### OpenCode version v.1.15.7 ### Steps to reproduce The software crashed directly without any relevant error reports. We only noticed abnormal memory usage, interface lag and extremely slow token generation before the white screen appeared. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: Infinite retry loop on consistent provider failure
signals.text: ### Description The fallback system can spin in an infinite retry loop when a provider consistently fails. We should cap retry attempts (e.g. at 5) so the fallback system can proceed to the next configured model instead of spinning indefinitely. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Observe the session logs showing an infinite retry loop without proceeding to the next configured model. ### Expected Behavior The retry loop should be capped at a reasonable limit (e.g., 5 attempts). Once the limit is reached, it should return an exhaustion status so the system can proceed to the next fallback model. ### Environment - **OS**: Any - **OpenCode version**: dev - **Provider/model**: Any consistently failing provider

signals.title: Feature request: Config option to always expand reasoning/thinking blocks by default
signals.text: ### Problem When using reasoning models (e.g., Claude, o3, DeepSeek, etc.), the thinking/reasoning blocks in the TUI are collapsed by default. The user has to manually expand them (press Enter or click) every single time the model outputs a reasoning block. This gets tedious quickly, especially during long sessions where reasoning is the primary interaction mode. ### Proposed Solution Add a configuration option in `opencode.json` to control the default visibility of reasoning/thinking blocks. **Suggested config shape:** ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "expand_thinking": true } ``` Or, more generally, a `display` / `ui` section: ```json { "ui": { "expand_reasoning": true } } ``` ### Use Case Developers who rely heavily on reasoning models need to constantly review the model's thought process to verify correctness, understand decisions, or debug unexpected behavior. Having to expand every block manually is a significant friction point that interrupts flow. ### Alternatives Considered - **Keyboard shortcut:** A global keybind to expand/collapse all thinking blocks in the current session could be a partial workaround, but it still requires an action per session. - **Environment variable:** e.g., `OPENCODE_EXPAND_THINKING=1`, but this is less discoverable than a config file option. ### Additional Context This feature would be especially valuable for: - Users on models with explicit reasoning tokens (Claude, o3, DeepSeek-R1, etc.) - Educational/debugging scenarios where understanding the model's chain of thought is critical - Accessibility: users who may have difficulty with repeated fine-motor interactions (clicking/pressing to expand) --- Thank you for considering this! OpenCode is an amazing tool and this small UX improvement would make reasoning-heavy workflows much smoother.

signals.title: Desktop app merges separate directories of the same Git repo into one project
signals.text: ### Description When adding projects in the desktop app, two different local directories that point to the same Git repository are merged into a single project. One directory becomes the main project worktree, and the other directory is shown/treated as a sandbox. This is unexpected. In the desktop app, each added directory should appear as an independent project, even if both directories use the same Git remote or represent different branches of the same repository. ### Plugins ### OpenCode version 1.15.12 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Clone the same Git repository into two different local directories. 2. Checkout a different branch in each directory. 3. Open the desktop app. 4. Add the first directory as a project. 5. Add the second directory as another project. ### Actual Behavior The desktop app merges both directories into one project. The first added directory becomes the main project, while the second directory is treated as a sandbox of that project. ### Expected Behavior The desktop app should show both directories as separate projects. Projects in the desktop app should be distinguished by their local directory path, not only by Git repository identity, remote URL, or shared Git metadata. ### Why This Matters It is common to keep multiple checkouts of the same repository in different directories, especially when working on multiple branches at the same time. Treating one checkout as a sandbox makes it harder to manage them independently in the desktop app. ### Suggested Fix The app could use `git worktree list` to distinguish linked Git worktrees from separate clones/checkouts. Proposed behavior: - If two directories are part of the same `git worktree` setup, merging them into one project with sandboxes makes sense. - If two directories are separate clones or separate local checkouts of the same remote repository, they should be shown as two independent projects. - In other words, sharing the same Git remote should not be enough to merge projects. The merge should only happen when Git reports the directories as linked worktrees of the same repository. This would preserve the current sandbox behavior for real Git worktrees while avoiding accidental merging of unrelated local directories. ### Screenshot and/or share link ### Operating System window 10 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signals.title: [BUG] plugin package.json drifts from config: stale deps never cleaned, missing deps cause slow startup
signals.text: ## Description OpenCode manages plugins through two paths that are poorly synchronized: **Path 1: `opencode plugin install --global`** — Uses `@npmcli/arborist` reify with `save: true` to append the plugin to `package.json`. This is **append-only**: it never removes entries for plugins that were previously installed but are no longer in config. **Path 2: Direct config edit + restart** — Users edit `opencode.json`/`tui.json` directly and restart. On startup, `Loader.resolve()` calls `Npm.add()` for each plugin individually, which calls `reify()` per-plugin (no batch). If `node_modules` is missing or stale, each plugin triggers a separate npm resolve+install. Over time, `package.json` drifts from the actual plugin declarations in config: 1. **Stale deps remain** — e.g. replacing `@tarquinen/opencode-dcp` with `open-mem` in config leaves the old entry in `package.json` forever 2. **Missing deps** — plugins added directly to config JSON are never added to `package.json`; startup must resolve them from scratch each time 3. **Slow startup** — each plugin calls `Npm.add()` → individual `reify()`, N plugins = N sequential npm operations instead of one batch install 4. **No `plugin remove` command** — there is no way to cleanly uninstall a plugin from both config and `package.json` ## Reproduction ### Scenario A (CLI path — stale entries): 1. `opencode plugin install --global some-plugin@1.0.0` → `package.json` gets `{"some-plugin": "1.0.0"}` 2. `opencode plugin install --global replacement@2.0.0` → config is updated, but `some-plugin` stays in `package.json` 3. Repeat → `package.json` accumulates orphaned deps ### Scenario B (config edit path — missing entries + slow startup): 1. Edit `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: add `"new-plugin@^1.0.0"` to `plugin` array 2. Delete `node_modules` (or start fresh) 3. Restart opencode → startup takes seconds as each plugin is resolved individually via `Npm.add()` → `reify()` 4. After startup, `package.json` may still not reflect all declared plugins (only the ones that needed install) ## Root Cause (source analysis) | File | Behavior | |---|---| | `packages/core/src/npm.ts` L78-108 | `reify()` uses `save: true, saveType: "prod"` — append-only, no prune | | `packages/core/src/npm.ts` L138-186 | `install()` checks declared vs locked but never removes stale entries | | `packages/opencode/src/plugin/install.ts` | `patchPluginList()` only modifies config JSON (opencode.json/tui.json), never `package.json` | | `packages/opencode/src/plugin/loader.ts` L94 | Each plugin calls `resolvePluginTarget()` → `Npm.add()` → individual `reify()` | | `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/plug.ts` | No `remove`/`uninstall` subcommand for plugins | ## Suggested Fix **A. Sync `package.json` from config on startup** — Before the per-plugin resolve loop, rebuild `package.json` dependencies to match the union of all plugin specifiers in `opencode.json` + `tui.json`, then run a single batch `reify()`. This would: - Remove stale entries - Add missing entries - Replace N individual reify calls with one batch install **B. Add `opencode plugin remove <module>` command** — Removes plugin from config JSON and prunes `package.json` entry. Gives users explicit control. ## Workaround Users experiencing long **"loading plugins"** delays on startup can manually clean up: ```bash # Regenerate package.json from config, then batch install (eliminates the slow per-plugin resolve) cd ~/.config/opencode rm -rf node_modules package.json package-lock.json # Restart opencode — it will regenerate from config declarations ``` ## Environment - OpenCode: v1.15.13 - OS: macOS - Config: global (opencode.json + tui.json) - 8 plugins across opencode.json + tui.json

signals.title: ProviderModelNotFoundError: subagents fail on tool-using tasks across all categories
signals.text: ## Bug Description Subagents (Sisyphus-Junior) fail with `ProviderModelNotFoundError` when executing tasks that require tool calls (write, read, websearch). Text-only ping tests succeed on some categories, but any real work task fails immediately. ## Environment - **OpenCode version**: 1.16.0 - **Platform**: macOS (darwin) - **Shell**: zsh - **Config file**: `~/.config/opencode/oh-my-openagent.json` ## Error Message ``` ProviderModelNotFoundError: at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-zdvbgwzc.js:668:62221) at SessionPrompt.getModel (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1067:1879) at SessionPrompt.getModel (definition) (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1066:1056) at SessionPrompt.run (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1068:1367) at SessionPrompt.run (definition) (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1067:929) at SessionRunState.ensureRunning (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1068:1338) at SessionRunState.ensureRunning (definition) (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:933:5264) at SessionPrompt.loop (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1067:653) at SessionPrompt.loop (definition) (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1068:1274) at SessionPrompt.prompt (/$bunfs/root/chunk-ech9cm9d.js:3:14109) at SessionPrompt.prompt (definition) (/$bunfs/root/chunk-m71nm5wk.js:1067:272) ``` ## Category Model Configuration ``` === CATEGORIES === visual-engineering: model=opencode/minimax-m2.5, fallbacks=[deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-free, opencode/nemotron-3-super-free, opencode/mimo-v2.5-free, opencode/big-pickle] ultrabrain: model=opencode/glm-5.1, fallbacks=[opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-free, opencode/nemotron-3-super-free, opencode/big-pickle] deep: model=opencode/minimax-m2.5, fallbacks=[opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-free, opencode/nemotron-3-super-free, opencode/mimo-v2.5-free, opencode/big-pickle] artistry: model=opencode/glm-5.1, fallbacks=[opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-free, opencode/nemotron-3-super-free, opencode/big-pickle] writing: model=opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus, fallbacks=[deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-free, opencode/nemotron-3-super-free, opencode/mimo-v2.5-free, opencode/big-pickle] unspecified-high: model=opencode/minimax-m2.5, fallbacks=[deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-free, opencode/nemotron-3-super-free, opencode/mimo-v2.5-free, opencode/big-pickle] quick: (not configured — uses default) === AGENTS === sisyphus: model=opencode/minimax-m2.5 oracle: model=opencode/glm-5.1 prometheus: model=opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus metis: model=opencode/glm-5.1 momus: model=opencode/glm-5.1 explore: model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-free librarian: model=opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus sisyphus-junior: model=opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus ``` ## Test Results ### Text-only ping tests (no tool calls) | Category | Configured Model | Ping Result | Actual Model Used | |----------|-----------------|-------------|-------------------| | writing | opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus | ✅ OK | opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus | | deep | opencode/minimax-m2.5 | ✅ OK | opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus (fell back) | | visual-engineering | opencode/minimax-m2.5 | ✅ OK | opencode/mimo-v2.5-free (fell back) | | ultrabrain | opencode/glm-5.1 | ✅ OK | opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus (fell back) | | artistry | opencode/glm-5.1 | ✅ OK | opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus (fell back) | | unspecified-high | opencode/minimax-m2.5 | ✅ OK | opencode/mimo-v2.5-free (fell back) | | quick | (default) | ❌ ProviderModelNotFoundError | N/A | ### Tool-using tasks (write/read/websearch) | Category | Task | Result | |----------|------|--------| | writing | Write Chapter 1 (research + write file) | ❌ ProviderModelNotFoundError | | deep | Write 100-word summary to file | ❌ ProviderModelNotFoundError | | deep | Write test file | ❌ ProviderModelNotFoundError | | unspecified-high | Write Chapter 1 (research + write file) | ❌ ProviderModelNotFoundError | | quick | Write "test" to file | ❌ ProviderModelNotFoundError | ## Key Observations 1. **Ping tests pass but actual tasks fail** — subagents can initialize and respond to text-only prompts, but crash when they need to use tools. 2. **Model fallback routing is broken** — categories configured with `opencode/minimax-m2.5` or `opencode/glm-5.1` are falling back to `opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus` or `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` instead of using the configured primary model. 3. **The error occurs at `SessionPrompt.getModel`** — suggesting the model resolution fails when the subagent session tries to actually execute, not during initialization. 4. **Main session works fine** — the parent session (running on `opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus`) can use all tools without error. Only subagent spawning is affected. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure categories in `~/.config/opencode/oh-my-openagent.json` with model mappings 2. Call `task(category="writing", prompt="Write a file", subagent_type="Sisyphus-Junior")` 3. Observe `ProviderModelNotFoundError` ## Expected Behavior Subagents should be able to execute tool calls (write, read, websearch, etc.) using their configured model or a working fallback. ## Actual Behavior Subagents crash with `ProviderModelNotFoundError` when attempting any task that requires tool execution. ## Workaround Parent agent (Sisyphus) performs all work directly without delegation. This defeats the purpose of the subagent system.

signals.title: Duplicate overlapping LLM streams in one session after background task result injection
signals.text: ### Description A real `opencode web` session produced overlapping LLM/provider turns for the same session and the same parent user message. This is not a UI-only duplicate and does not look like an upstream provider retry: the duplicated requests are persisted as distinct assistant messages/parts in OpenCode's SQLite DB and appear as distinct provider usage rows. This appears to be the same bug family as #30809 and #28202, but with additional evidence from provider usage IDs and exact local `session.processor` / `llm.stream` overlap. ### Environment - OpenCode repo/runtime under investigation: `anomalyco/opencode` - Observed runtime version in logs: `1.15.11` - Entry point: `opencode web --port 4096 --hostname 0.0.0.0` - Session: `ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og` - Session directory: redacted user workspace - Model/provider: `openai/gpt-5.5` ### Evidence Two provider usage rows that looked like duplicate requests were confirmed to be real separate requests from the same OpenCode session: - `286185bd-a0c6-4686-a141-43addecd3a61` - OpenCode assistant message: `msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g` - Created: `2026-06-09T08:47:55.397Z` - Finish: `stop` - Tokens: input `861`, cache read `142848`, output `268` - `f9c8faeb-bcba-47a5-8246-1e650d3dd2ea` - OpenCode assistant message: `msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn` - Created: `2026-06-09T08:47:58.850Z` - Finish: `stop` - Tokens: input `629`, cache read `143360`, output `241` Both provider usage rows had: - `request_metadata.client_family = opencode` - session affinity `session=ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og` The local OpenCode DB shows these were not display duplicates. Both assistant messages have real persisted `step-start`, `text`, and `step-finish` parts. Around the same window, several terminal assistant siblings were created under the same parent user message: ```text parent user: msg_eab868be5001ubwGod5Cy16qZo 2026-06-09T08:47:15.458Z msg_eab908402001hktb8SNT9BxEqC finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:24.649Z msg_eab90a7e9001DSqtZTlAxWliH0 finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:35.881Z msg_eab90d3c9001KMOve81qFwnJKU finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:38.347Z msg_eab90dd6b001WlltSckBE8CgPd finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:45.650Z msg_eab90f9f200113JhjG3UT9rB6N finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:55.397Z msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g finish=stop 2026-06-09T08:47:58.850Z msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn finish=stop ``` The step parts show actual overlap, not just sequential duplicate output: ```text 2026-06-09T08:47:59.889Z step-start msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g 2026-06-09T08:48:03.334Z step-start msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn 2026-06-09T08:48:07.877Z step-finish msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g 2026-06-09T08:48:10.535Z step-finish msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn ``` The service log confirms two prompt-loop sequences were interleaved for the same session: ```text 2026-06-09T08:47:55 service=session.prompt step=40 loop 2026-06-09T08:47:55 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab912005001e49cCKuQJXd50g process 2026-06-09T08:47:55 service=llm ... session.id=ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og ... stream 2026-06-09T08:47:58 service=session.prompt step=39 loop 2026-06-09T08:47:58 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab912d82001CgJE4JVOu2WYdn process 2026-06-09T08:47:58 service=llm ... session.id=ses_154d13caaffebBjbwxDhuBP7og ... stream ``` There is an even earlier local log line where the same assistant message ID entered `session.processor process` twice and triggered two `llm` streams: ```text 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=session.prompt step=34 loop 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab90029a001uMQVb8UIKHQtcR process 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=llm ... stream 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=session.processor messageID=msg_eab90029a001uMQVb8UIKHQtcR process 2026-06-09T08:46:42 service=llm ... stream ``` ### Trigger shape The parent user message was a synthetic background-task completion reminder. The actual project/task content is intentionally redacted, but the structural marker was: ```text <system-reminder> [ALL BACKGROUND TASKS COMPLETE] ... redacted project/task content ... ``` This matches the background result injection path in `TaskTool.injectBackgroundResult`, which forks a parent-session `ops.prompt(...)` when a background task completes. ### Source-path notes Relevant paths in current source: - `packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts` - `TaskTool.injectBackgroundResult` calls parent-session `ops.prompt(...)` and forks it. - `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` - `SessionPrompt.prompt()` persists a user message and calls `loop(...)`. - `runLoop()` creates an assistant message and eventually calls `handle.process(...)`. - `loop()` relies on `state.ensureRunning(sessionID, ...)` for same-session serialization. - `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts` - `SessionProcessor.process()` logs `process` and calls `llm.stream(streamInput)`. - `packages/opencode/src/session/run-state.ts` - The runner map is an in-memory `Map<SessionID, Runner>` scoped by `InstanceState`. The intended invariant appears to be "one active runner per session", but the evidence above shows that invariant was not held in this session. One likely contributing issue is that `SessionRunState` is not durable; it only protects one in-memory `SessionRunState` instance. If multiple Effect runtime/layer instances or prompt entry points acquire different `SessionRunState` instances for the same session, they can both enter `runLoop()`. The HTTP/server layer also provides `SessionPrompt.defaultLayer` and `SessionRunState.defaultLayer`, while `SessionPrompt.defaultLayer` itself provides a private `SessionRunState.defaultLayer`, which is worth auditing to ensure all prompt paths share the same run-state instance. ### Expected behavior For one session and one parent user/system-reminder message, OpenCode should not run overlapping provider turns or persist multiple terminal assistant siblings unless that is explicitly modeled as separate queued activities. Background task result injection should either coalesce into the active session drain or enqueue a future turn behind a durable/session-owned execution claim. ### Actual behavior Multiple `llm.stream(...)` calls were active for the same session, producing multiple terminal assistant messages under the same parent. This multiplied provider usage and polluted session history. ### Related issues - #30809: very closely related; same-parent duplicate assistant replies around background task result injection. - #28202: closely related; overlapping async/plugin prompts and Web `prompt_async` can create same-parent assistant siblings. - #29478: related duplicate final answers due to fragile prompt-loop completion checks. - #24773: related user-message side of the concurrency gate problem. - #26526: related `promptAsync` fork/context issue; may be relevant if different prompt paths get different instance/run-state context. ### Suggested direction The robust fix should make the session execution claim durable/session-owned rather than only an in-memory `Map` inside one `SessionRunState` instance. At minimum: 1. Audit layer composition so all legacy prompt paths for the same process and instance share exactly one `SessionRunState`. 2. Add regression coverage that simulates background result injection while a parent session drain is active and asserts there is only one provider turn at a time for a session. 3. Consider a DB-backed/session-owned execution lease for legacy sessions, or migrate this path to the V2 durable inbox/coalescing model.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Support drag-and-drop / paste of images in the question tool UI
signals.text: ### Description When the agent invokes the `question` tool (MCQ / structured question UI), there is currently no way to attach images or screenshots while answering. Drag-and-drop and clipboard paste work (or are planned) for the main chat prompt, but the question interface appears to be text/selection-only. This is a common workflow gap: the agent asks a clarifying question, and the user wants to respond with a screenshot (e.g. "which layout do you mean?" → drop a UI screenshot) without dismissing the question modal or switching back to the main prompt. ### Expected behavior While the question tool UI is open, users should be able to: - Drag and drop image files (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP) into the question interface - Paste screenshots from the clipboard (Cmd/Ctrl+V) - See attached images as thumbnails/previews before submitting answers - Have attached images included in the question response sent back to the agent ### Actual behavior - Dropping images onto the question UI does nothing (no dropzone, no attachment) - Pasting a screenshot while focused on the question UI does not attach it - Users must dismiss or work around the question flow and attach images via the main prompt instead ### Motivation / use cases 1. Agent asks "Which error screen are you seeing?" → user drops a screenshot inline 2. Agent asks "Which of these UI variants should we match?" → user attaches reference images 3. Debugging sessions where visual context is faster than describing UI state in text ### Related issues These cover image attach for the **main prompt**, but not the **question tool** UI specifically: - #906 — Feature request: Paste to attach image - #26111 — Windows desktop Ctrl+V + drag-drop - #26780 — TUI drag-and-drop support - #20169 — TUI attach button when drag-drop fails - #18143 — Desktop dropped files in prompt Question tool UI issues (layout/behavior, not image attach): - #31383 — Question Tool popup doesn't appear casually - #11367 — Long question tool makes opencode unusable - #6330 — Generic UI Intent Channel (broader cross-client question UI architecture) ### Suggested implementation notes - Reuse existing prompt attachment / dropzone infrastructure where possible (`prompt.dropzone.label` i18n strings already exist for desktop/web) - Extend the question tool response schema to support optional image attachments per answer or as freeform context - Ensure parity across Desktop, Web, and TUI clients (or document platform limitations) ### OpenCode version Latest (observed June 2026) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a session where the agent invokes the `question` tool 2. When the question UI appears, try dragging a PNG/JPG screenshot onto it 3. Alternatively, copy a screenshot to clipboard and press Cmd/Ctrl+V while the question UI is focused 4. Observe that no image is attached and the answer can only be text/selection-based ### Operating System macOS (likely affects Desktop/Web/TUI generally) ### Terminal N/A (Desktop app / question modal)

signals.title: [FEATURE]: add SSH remote directory references
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Add a new SSH remote directory reference type to opencode's references system. Currently references support local paths and Git repositories only — there is no way to reference files on a remote server without manually copying them or setting up a Git repo. The proposed reference would sync a remote directory via rsync over SSH and make it available as a project reference, following the same async materialization pattern as Git references. #### Proposed config schema: ```jsonc { "references": { "infra": { "host": "devint-229", "remotePath": "/home/devint/infra", "user": "devint", "description": "Infrastructure server" } } } ``` Optional fields: `user`, `port`, `identityFile`, `description`, `hidden`. #### Why rsync? rsync provides incremental sync, delete propagation, and uses the user's existing SSH config (`~/.ssh/config`, ssh-agent) without additional native dependencies (compared to ssh2). #### Implementation status A draft PR with a complete implementation is available: **https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/31900** The implementation includes: - `SshSource` as a new variant in the `Source` tagged union - `ConfigSsh` config schema class - rsync-based cache service with EffectFlock locking - Input validation and non-interactive SSH host key handling - Tests and documentation

signals.title: [BUG]: Skill discovery logs false "duplicate skill name" warnings when .claude/skills is a symlink to .agents/skills
signals.text: ## Description A common multi-agent convention is to keep one canonical skills directory and symlink the agent-specific paths to it, e.g.: ``` .agents/skills/ # canonical, shared by Claude Code / Codex / opencode .claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills ``` opencode scans both `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, does not resolve symlinks to a real path, and therefore discovers every skill twice — logging a `WARN duplicate skill name` per skill on every startup: ``` timestamp=2026-06-12T02:16:25.049Z level=WARN run=1285e688 message="duplicate skill name" name=demo-skill existing=/tmp/oc-symlink-repro/.claude/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md duplicate=/tmp/oc-symlink-repro/.agents/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md ``` In a project with ~30 skills this produces ~30 warnings per session start, drowning out real log signal. Note this is **not** the case fixed in #26709 — there the `existing` and `duplicate` paths were *identical strings*. Here the paths are different strings pointing at the same physical file through a symlinked directory, so the string-equality skip does not apply. #17219 reports the same root cause (no realpath dedup) in the permission scanner. ## Steps to reproduce ```bash mkdir -p repro/.agents/skills/demo-skill repro/.claude cat > repro/.agents/skills/demo-skill/SKILL.md <<'SKILL' --- name: demo-skill description: Demo skill for symlink dedup repro --- Demo body. SKILL ln -s ../.agents/skills repro/.claude/skills cd repro && git init -q opencode run 'hi' # then check the log: grep 'duplicate skill name' ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log | grep demo-skill ``` ## Expected behavior Skill files reachable through more than one scan path should be deduplicated by resolved real path (`fs.realpath`) and produce no warning. Alternatively (or additionally) a config option to restrict skill discovery directories (#23035) would let users opt out of scanning one of the locations. ## Environment - opencode 1.17.3 (also reproduced on earlier 1.17.x) - Linux x86_64 (NixOS), opencode installed via nix

signals.title: CJK characters garbled when copying text via OSC52 clipboard (WSL2 + VSCode terminal)
signals.text: ## Bug Description When copying text containing CJK characters (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) from opencode running in VSCode integrated terminal on WSL2, the pasted result is garbled/mojibake. ASCII text copies correctly. This is a known issue in the upstream OpenTUI framework's OSC52 clipboard implementation. The same bug was reported and fixed in charmbracelet/crush (see related issues below). ## Environment - opencode: v1.17.4 - OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows 11 - Terminal: VSCode integrated terminal v1.124.0 - LANG: C.UTF-8 (WSL), zh_CN.UTF-8 (VSCode terminal env) - TERM_PROGRAM: vscode ## Reproduction 1. Start opencode in VSCode integrated terminal on WSL2 2. Use `Ctrl+↑` / `Ctrl+↓` to navigate to a message containing Chinese text 3. Press `Ctrl+X Y` to copy the message 4. Paste elsewhere → garbled text ## Root Cause opencode's TUI framework (OpenTUI `@opentui/core@0.3.4`) uses `copyToClipboardOSC52` which sends `\033]52;c;<base64>\007` to the terminal. The OSC52 implementation has a bug handling multi-byte UTF-8 characters — likely truncating at byte boundaries instead of character boundaries during base64 encoding. Evidence from binary: - `copyToClipboardOSC52` function present - `isOsc52Term` detection logic present - `terminal.isOsc52Term` check present ## Related Issues - **charmbracelet/crush#839** — "Console copy results in garbled Japanese text" (same bug, WSL2 + Windows) - **charmbracelet/crush#2155** — "Copy words in terminal, only english and numbers are copied" (fixed in crush v0.42.0+) - **charmbracelet/crush#851** — "Extra zero-width characters appear when entering Chinese text" - **sst/opencode#263** — "I can't copy messages" (related: clipboard not working) ## Suggested Fix Port the CJK clipboard fix from crush v0.42.0+ back to OpenTUI, or add a fallback to system clipboard (e.g., `clip.exe` on WSL, `pbcopy` on macOS, `xclip`/`xsel` on Linux) when OSC52 is detected but CJK characters are present. ## Workaround Use VSCode terminal's native copy instead: select text with mouse → `Ctrl+Shift+C` to copy. This bypasses OSC52 and handles CJK correctly.

signals.title: OpenCode repeatedly retries after a mid-tool provider disconnect
signals.text: ### Description If the provider connection closes after a streamed tool call has been delivered but before a clean message completion, OpenCode repeatedly retries the provider interaction instead of failing boundedly. In the latest local verification run, OpenCode made 588 provider requests and saw 588 mid-stream connection closures before the reproducer timeout killed the process. ### Plugins None. The standalone reproducer sets OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1. ### OpenCode version 1.17.4 ### Steps to reproduce Prerequisites: Docker, Python 3, and the GitHub CLI (`gh`) for the clone command below. The linked reproducer is self-contained and uses only Python standard-library modules plus Docker. It builds `opencode-ai@1.17.4` from the public npm package, starts a local mock provider, and runs the CLI in an isolated workspace. The Docker run is limited to 2 CPUs and 4 GiB RAM by default. Complete self-contained reproducer: https://gist.github.com/N0zoM1z0/5861579c2e83fed87126293bf76bbbcf ```bash gh gist clone 5861579c2e83fed87126293bf76bbbcf opencode-post-tool-transient-disconnect-reproducer cd opencode-post-tool-transient-disconnect-reproducer python3 opencode-post-tool-transient-disconnect.reproduce.py ``` To reuse an already-built local image: ```bash python3 opencode-post-tool-transient-disconnect.reproduce.py --skip-build ``` Expected successful reproduction output includes: ``` provider_requests=588 closed_mid_stream=588 process_timed_out=True REPRODUCED ``` ### Screenshot and/or share link Not applicable; this is a non-interactive CLI/provider protocol reproducer. ### Operating System Linux x86_64 Docker, using node:24-bookworm-based target image. ### Terminal Non-interactive CLI run from Python subprocess.
