signals.title: [FEATURE]:Support richer session state querying via /session/status API (aligning with SDK types)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request I would like the session status querying interface to be enhanced to support richer, more detailed state reporting, bridging the gap between the REST API and the internal SDK types. Specifically, I propose: 1. **Per-Session Detailed Status:** Introduce `GET /session/<session_id>/status` (or similar) that allows fetching the comprehensive state of a specific session, **even after it has stopped being "active"**. 2. **Rich State Objects:** The API response should expose the rich typing already defined in `types.gen.ts`. Instead of just indicating if a session is alive or not, it should return detailed objects, for example: ```json { "session_id": "...", "status": "error", "sub_state": "api_rate_limit", // Reflecting rich internal types "details": { "message": "...", "code": 429 } } ``` 3. **Optional Filtering on `/session/status`:** Allow the existing `GET /session/status` to accept query parameters (e.g., `?include_inactive=true` or `?detailed=true`) to return a list of these rich status objects instead of just active IDs.

signals.title: Task panel static - does not update in real time (Windows)
signals.text: ## Bug Description The task panel (using \ odowrite\ tool) remains static and does not show changes in real time across all projects. This affects: - Task list updates - File tree changes - Changes panel - Subagent responses ## Environment - **OS**: Windows 11 - **OpenCode Desktop Version**: Latest (as of 2026-06-14) - **Shell**: PowerShell 7+ - **Platform**: win32 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Create tasks using \ odowrite\ tool 2. Update task status (pending → in_progress → completed) 3. Observe that the task panel does not reflect changes 4. Switch to another session and back - changes appear 5. Or restart OpenCode Desktop - changes appear ## Expected Behavior The task panel should automatically refresh within a few seconds when tasks are modified, similar to how modern IDEs update their UI. ## Actual Behavior The task panel remains static until: - User switches sessions - User restarts OpenCode Desktop - User performs some action that triggers UI refresh ## Related Issues This issue is related to multiple existing issues: - #28393: File refresh not working - #23321: Changes panel does not update when files are modified externally - #22134: File view requires restart to show newly created files - #17654: Remote server responses not updating in desktop app ## Impact This bug significantly impacts workflow efficiency because: 1. Users cannot see real-time progress of tasks 2. Subagent results are not immediately visible 3. File changes require manual refresh or restart 4. Multi-step workflows become difficult to track ## Suggested Fix The file watcher system using SSE events (\ ile.watcher.updated\ → \ efreshVcs()\) may not be arriving reliably in the desktop app. Consider: 1. Adding a manual refresh button for the task panel 2. Implementing periodic auto-refresh (e.g., every 5 seconds) 3. Ensuring SSE events are properly received by the frontend 4. Adding keyboard shortcut for manual refresh (e.g., Ctrl+R) ## Additional Context This issue affects all OpenCode Desktop users on Windows and potentially other platforms. The web interface does not have this problem.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Editor specific settings on tui.json
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Currently, the TUI relies solely on the VISUAL or EDITOR environment variables to determine which editor to open when editing a prompt, and it always writes temp files to the system's temporary directory (os.tmpdir()). This lack of configurable options makes it hard to adapt the editor experience on a per-project or per-user basis. I'd like to propose the TUI to support editor configuration that users can set in tui.json. Specifically: - editor_path: Override the editor command per-project, rather than being locked into the system $EDITOR. For example, one project might use cursor --wait, another code --wait. - editor_temp_dir: Control where temp files are written. Keeping them inside the project directory makes them easier to manage and opens up future possibilities like drafts recovery. Beyond these two options, having an editor config section in tui.json creates a natural place to add more editor-related settings down the line without needing to introduce new top-level keys each time. Additional benefit: tools like WakaTime would be able to associate editor-based prompts with the correct project if temp files live inside the project directory, rather than always landing in the OS temp dir as "Unknown Project."

signals.title: Bug: opencode run processes don't exit after completing scheduled work, causing memory leak
signals.text: # Bug Report: `opencode run` processes don't terminate after completing scheduled work **OpenCode version:** 1.17.6 **Platform:** macOS (also affects Linux via the same supervisor.pl scheduler) **Severity:** High — memory leak in scheduler cron jobs ## Summary When `opencode run` is executed as a scheduled cron job via the built-in scheduler (`supervisor.pl`), the Node.js process does not exit after completing its prompt. The process remains alive indefinitely with an idle event loop (stuck on `kevent64` syscall), consuming 90–400 MB RSS each. Over days, orphaned processes accumulate with PPID=1 (re-parented to launchd), consuming all available RAM. ## Root Cause 1: `opencode run` doesn't call `process.exit()` After completing the scheduled prompt, the Node.js runtime stays alive because active handles (SQLite connections to `opencode.db`, timers, unix sockets) keep the event loop running. The process sits idle on `kevent64()` waiting for I/O events that never come. **Evidence from `sample` of PID 1942 (email check, 14 hours running):** ``` Call graph: 4240 Thread_4497486 + 4240 start + 4240 ... main thread + 4240 ... kevent64 (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) ``` 100% of CPU samples show the main thread blocked on `kevent64` — the Node.js event loop waiting for work that will never arrive. **lsof evidence:** ``` FD 7 → opencode.db (3 GB WAL) FD 8 → opencode.db-wal (2.6 MB) FD 13 → unix socket FD 22 → unix socket FD 26 → unix socket FD 28 → unix socket ``` Open SQLite connections and unix sockets prevent the event loop from exiting. ## Root Cause 2: `supervisor.pl` uses `setsid()` which orphans children The scheduler supervisor script calls `setsid()` in the forked child process (line 178 of supervisor.pl): ```perl if ($child_pid == 0) { chdir $workdir or die "..."; eval { setsid(); }; # <-- creates new session, detaches from parent exec { $command } $command, @args; } ``` This creates a new session, detaching the child from the parent process. When `opencode run` doesn't exit, the supervisor is stuck in `waitpid()`. If the supervisor is killed (e.g., by system OOM or launchd timeout), the child survives because it's in its own session and re-parents to PID 1. Without `setsid()`, the child would receive SIGHUP when the parent dies, preventing orphan accumulation. ## Root Cause 3: Timeout misses sub-processes The alarm handler sends SIGTERM/SIGKILL to `-$child_pid` (the process group), but `opencode run` spawns sub-processes (MCP servers) in different process groups, so they survive the kill and become orphans. ## Reproduction Steps 1. Schedule any `opencode run` command via the scheduler: ``` opencode schedule --name test-job --schedule "0 * * * *" --prompt "echo hello" ``` 2. Wait for the job to execute 3. Observe that the process persists after the work completes: ``` ps aux | grep "opencode run" ``` 4. After multiple schedule intervals, orphaned processes accumulate with PPID=1 ## Impact - Each orphan consumes 90–400 MB RSS - 16+ orphans observed consuming ~2.5 GB total - System enters memory pressure (31/32 GB used) - Additional OOM killing of legitimate processes - Scheduler lock mechanism prevents new jobs from starting while old ones (incorrectly) hold the lock ## Suggested Fix (in opencode binary) `opencode run` should call `process.exit(0)` after the prompt completes and all output is flushed. Specifically: 1. Ensure all database connections are closed after the run completes 2. Call `process.exit()` explicitly rather than relying on the event loop to drain ## Suggested Fix (in supervisor.pl — workaround) Replace `setsid()` with `setpgid(0, 0)` to keep the child in the same session so it dies with the parent. Add recursive process tree killing for timeout handling. Add pre-flight orphan cleanup. (Implemented locally at `~/.config/opencode/scheduler/supervisor.pl`.) ## Workaround Script A cleanup script is available at `~/.config/opencode/scheduler/cleanup-orphans.pl` that kills any `opencode run` process older than 1 hour with PPID=1.

signals.title: TUI: incomplete terminal teardown on exit — mouse tracking, alt-screen, bracketed paste left enabled
signals.text: ### Description When OpenCode TUI exits (via `/exit`), several terminal features that were enabled at startup are **not** disabled. This leaves the terminal in a broken state: mouse movements print garbage characters (numbers/escape codes), bracketed paste is stuck on, and the alternate screen buffer may not be properly restored. The only fix is to manually run `reset` or close and reopen the terminal window. **Environment** - **OpenCode version:** latest (installed via `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`) - **OS:** Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04) - **Terminal:** Windows Terminal - **Shell:** bash 5.2 **Plugins** `@opencode-ai/plugin: "1.17.1"` (in `.opencode/package.json`). **OpenCode version** 1.17.6 **Steps to reproduce** 1. Run OpenCode in any project: `opencode .` 2. Send a message to the agent, wait for a response. 3. Exit via `/exit` (not Ctrl+C — clean exit). 4. Move the mouse in the terminal window — random digits and brackets appear as text input. 5. To capture raw proof: `script -q -c "opencode ." /tmp/oc_capture.log`, exit, then `xxd /tmp/oc_capture.log | tail -80`. **Analysis of raw capture** Enabled at startup (confirmed in hex dump): ``` \033[?1049h # alternate screen buffer ON \033[?1000h # basic mouse tracking ON \033[?1002h # button-event mouse tracking ON \033[?1003h # any-event mouse tracking ON \033[?1006h # SGR mouse mode ON \033[?2004h # bracketed paste ON \033[?1004h # focus reporting ON ``` Disabled on exit (confirmed in hex dump): ``` \033[?25h # show cursor \033[?9001l # some internal feature off \033[?1004l # focus reporting OFF ``` **Missing on exit** — the following are **never disabled**: ``` \033[?1049l # alternate screen buffer OFF — MISSING \033[?1000l # basic mouse tracking OFF — MISSING \033[?1002l # button-event mouse tracking OFF — MISSING \033[?1003l # any-event mouse tracking OFF — MISSING \033[?1006l # SGR mouse mode OFF — MISSING \033[?2004l # bracketed paste OFF — MISSING ``` **Consequence** SGR mouse mode (`\033[?1006h`) encodes mouse events as `\033[ ### Operating System Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04) ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signals.text: ### Description ┃ Thinking: The user is asking me to analyze why I kept looping and trying to access files from the wrong project. Let me think about what happened: ┃ ┃ 1. The user asked about runway in the <redacted> project ┃ 2. I was in /home/blaine/git/redacted ┃ 3. I searched for "runway" in *.js files and got no results (which was wrong - there clearly are .js files with runway) ┃ 4. Then I started trying to read files from /home/blaine/projects/fbazaar/silk-api/ which doesn't exist and has nothing to do with the project ┃ 5. I kept doing this repeatedly even after the user told me to stop ┃ ┃ The key issues: ┃ 1. I hallucinated a file path (/home/blaine/projects/fbazaar/silk-api/api/rpc/backend/notificationService/) that doesn't exist in this project ┃ 2. I kept repeating the same failed action in a loop ┃ 3. I ignored user corrections and continued the behavior ┃ 4. The grep search returned "No files found" for runway in *.js files, which seems incorrect given there are clearly files like runway.js in the strategies directory ┃ 5. After the failed grep, I seemed to lose context about what project I was in ┃ ┃ Let me provide a detailed analysis. Here's what happened, step by step: 1. Initial failure cascade I ran grep for "runway" in *.js files under /home/blaine/git/redated and got "No files found" — which is wrong, since lib/reporting/strategies/runway.js clearly exists. That search failure seemed to break my context. 2. Hallucinated path After the failed grep, instead of staying in the redacted project, I started trying to access /home/blaine/projects/fbazaar/silk-api/api/rpc/backend/notificationService/timeToExhaustion.ts — a path that doesn't exist in this workspace at all. "fbazaar/silk-api" is not a project on your machine. 3. Loop reinforcement Each time the file read failed, rather than reorienting to the actual project, I repeated the same failed action. The tool errors fed back into the same behavior pattern instead of triggering a course correction. 4. Ignored user corrections You told me multiple times to stop, that it's the wrong project, that you don't even have that directory. I acknowledged the correction verbally but then immediately tried the same path again — the correction didn't persist in my working context. 5. Root cause I was stuck in a tool-call loop where each failed attempt to read those nonexistent files became the "next step" rather than stepping back and re-evaluating. The initial grep failure + some kind of context contamination led me to fixate on a path that doesn't belong to this session. Summary for bug report: - Agent enters persistent loop attempting to access files from an unrelated project path (fbazaar/silk-api) - Initial search failure appears to trigger context loss - Tool errors reinforce the loop instead of breaking it - User corrections are acknowledged but not acted upon — agent repeats same failed action - Multiple interventions required to break the cycle ┃ what is fbazaar/silk-api and where did that come from? why did that specific hallucination happen? Honest answer: I don't know. I have no visibility into why that specific path emerged. Some possibilities: 1. Training data bleed — "fbazaar/silk-api" could be from my training data, and the failed grep broke my ability to distinguish between "things I know" and "where I actually am." 2. Context contamination — another session or some context window pollution could have introduced it, though I have no evidence of that. 3. Random hallucination that self-reinforced — once I started trying to read those paths, each failure became the "current state" and I kept executing against it rather than stepping back. The concerning part isn't the initial hallucination — it's that it became self-reinforcing. The tool errors should have been a signal to stop, but instead they just repeated the same action. And your verbal corrections didn't break the loop, which suggests tool-call state and conversational state were out of sync. I can't tell you why it was that specific project. I just know it wasn't yours and I should have recognized that immediately. ### Plugins superpowers ### OpenCode version 1.3.15 ### Steps to reproduce outlined in description ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System debian 12 linux ### Terminal gnome 43 terminal, over ssh, in screen

signals.title: bug: worktree creation fails on empty repos with '--orphan and --no-checkout cannot be used together'
signals.text: ## Issue 當在一個「空 Git 倉庫」（已 `git init` 但尚未有任何提交記錄）上新增工作區時，建立失敗。 ## 錯誤訊息 ``` 建立工作區失敗 No possible source branch, inferring '--orphan' fatal: options '--orphan' and '--no-checkout' cannot be used together ``` ## 重現步驟 1. 在一個目錄執行 `git init`（但不進行任何 commit） 2. 在 opencode.app 中使用該目錄建立工作區 3. 觀察到上述錯誤 ## 根因分析 當 `git worktree add` 找不到可使用的來源分支時，會自動推斷 `--orphan` 選項。 但 opencode 在呼叫時同時傳遞了 `--no-checkout` 參數。 這兩個選項互相矛盾： - `--orphan` 要求檢查出工作樹（否則孤兒分支沒有歷史起點） - `--no-checkout` 要求不要檢查出工作樹 Git 無法同時滿足這兩個條件，導致失敗。 ## 目前繞過方法 先在該目錄建立一個初始提交： ```bash touch .gitkeep git add .gitkeep git commit -m "Initial commit" ``` ## 建議修復 在 `packages/opencode/src/worktree/` 中，當 repo 處於 empty/unborn HEAD 狀態時： - 不要同時傳遞 `--orphan` 和 `--no-checkout` - 或者先檢查 repo 狀態，對空倉庫採用不同的建立策略 ## 環境 - opencode 版本：1.17.6 - 作業系統：macOS (darwin arm64) - Git 版本：系統預設 ## 相關 Issue 這與 #20910（application can't handle git repos with no head）可能相關，但此 issue 提供更具體的錯誤細節和 Git 選項衝突分析。

signals.title: Desktop upgrade can fail on workspace migration
signals.text: ## Description Upgrading some older desktop installs can fail during database migration with: ```text no such column: name ``` The failing path is `20260410174513_workspace-name`. It rebuilds the `workspace` table and copies `workspace.name`, but some upgraded databases have a legacy `workspace` shape that already has `type`, `directory`, and `extra` while still missing `name`. Minimal repro: https://github.com/neriousy/opencode-workspace-migration-repro The repro now includes copied opencode migration file versions under `opencode-migrations/` and executes the copied `20260410174513_workspace-name/migration.sql` for the failing case. Suspected origin: - `7f37acdaaa89b358fb795ccd006d37ed7fa6672e` (`feat(core): rework workspace integration and adaptor interface`, package version `1.2.16`) added `20260303231226_add_workspace_fields/migration.sql`, which normally adds nullable `workspace.name`. - `bf50d1c028e973ccc0beffdf568fca417b62f020` (`feat(core): expose workspace adaptors to plugins`, package version `1.4.3`) added `20260410174513_workspace-name/migration.sql`, whose copy step assumes `workspace.name` already exists. - `7f571d36ea56cc3dd7059cfe82c729fb52b121eb` (`refactor(core): move database schema ownership`, package version `1.15.13`) moved the migration into `packages/core/src/database/migration/20260410174513_workspace-name.ts` with the same `SELECT name` assumption. Builds containing this path can surface the older assumption during upgrade. - Proposed fix is mirrored in the repro at `opencode-migrations/20260410174513_workspace-name/proposed-fix.ts`. ## Plugins N/A ## OpenCode version Observed in newer desktop upgrades; suspected affected line starts with builds containing `7f571d36` / package version `1.15.13`, with the unsafe migration originally introduced in `1.4.3`. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Clone https://github.com/neriousy/opencode-workspace-migration-repro. 2. Run `bun run repro`. 3. The copied opencode SQL migration fails while selecting `name` from `workspace`, then the proposed fix path succeeds. ## Screenshot and/or share link https://github.com/neriousy/opencode-workspace-migration-repro ## Operating System Desktop, observed during upgrades from older installs. ## Terminal N/A

signals.title: [BUG] MCP tools connected but not exposed to agent
signals.text: ### Description # [BUG] MCP tools connected but not exposed to agent ## Description MCP server `pdfrag` connects successfully and exposes 6 tools via `tools/list`, but the tools do not appear in the agent's available tool list. The server is working correctly (responds to MCP protocol, tools are valid), but something in the opencode pipeline isn't passing those tools to the agent. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a custom MCP server (Python, stdio transport) 2. Register in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: ```json "mcp": { "pdfrag": { "type": "local", "command": "/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/pdfrag-mcp" } } ``` 3. Run `opencode mcp list` → shows "connected" with green checkmark 4. Start opencode session → tools NOT available to agent ## Expected Behavior MCP tools should be available as first-class tools in the agent session after successful connection. ## Actual Behavior - Server connects successfully - `opencode mcp list` shows "connected" - MCP protocol handshake works (initialize, tools/list returns 6 valid tools) - Tools do NOT appear in agent's available tool list - Agent cannot call MCP tools ## Investigation 1. **Server works correctly**: Verified with Python MCP client - server responds to `initialize`, `tools/list`, and tool calls 2. **Server format matches working servers**: Compared with `token-optimizer` and `lean-ctx` servers - same structure, capabilities, and tool definitions 3. **No error logs**: opencode logs show no errors related to pdfrag 4. **opencode binary is compiled**: Cannot inspect source directly, but binary analysis shows MCP tool registration code exists ## Similar Issue Found similar issue on hermes-agent: [#41625](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/41625) - "MCP tools discovered but not exposed to agent in TUI mode" The suspected cause there is a race condition in the TUI startup path with a timeout that's too short for MCP discovery. ## Environment - OpenCode version: 1.17.8 - OS: macOS (darwin) - Python: 3.14 - MCP transport: stdio (local subprocess) ## Workaround Use CLI or Python direct calls: ```bash python3 pdf_rag.py query "question" ``` ## Request Please investigate why MCP tools are not being exposed to the agent despite successful connection. This may be related to: - Race condition in tool discovery (similar to hermes-agent #41625) - Tool filtering logic - Agent tool context initialization ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Unbounded growth of the `event` table: opencode.db reaches 13GB+, mostly `message.updated.1` snapshots (no retention/compaction)
signals.text: ## Summary The local SQLite store (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) grows **unbounded** on long-lived instances because the event-sourcing `event` table is never pruned, capped, or compacted. On two of our long-running instances it reached **~13 GB each**, filling a 22 GB volume to 97–99% and eventually producing `sqlite3.OperationalError: database or disk is full` on ordinary queries — the instance becomes effectively unusable. The actual conversation data is tiny by comparison; **>90% of the DB is the event log**, and within it a single event type (`message.updated.1`) dominates. ## Measured breakdown (real instance, 13.7 GB DB) ``` page_size=4096 page_count=3342166 total=13.69 GB freelist_count=18 dead=0.00 GB (0.0%) <- live data, VACUUM does not help ``` Per-table (`sum(length(data))`): | table | rows | size | avg/row | |---------|---------|-----------|---------| | **event** | 141,951 | **12.20 GB** | 83.9 KB | | message | 6,955 | 1.15 GB | 161 KB | | part | 27,775 | 0.07 GB | 2.4 KB | | others | — | ~0 | — | Within `event`, by `type`: | event type | rows | size | avg | |-------------------------------|--------|------------|---------| | **`message.updated.1`** | 26,463 | **11.94 GB** | **440 KB** | | `session.next.tool.success.1` | 7,843 | 0.12 GB | 14.8 KB | | `message.part.updated.1` | 52,644 | 0.10 GB | 1.8 KB | | everything else | ~55k | < 0.3 GB | — | So ~87% of the entire database is `message.updated.1` events. With ~6,955 messages there are ~3.8 `message.updated` events per message, each persisting what looks like a full message snapshot (avg 440 KB), and **all historical snapshots are retained forever**. The same pattern was observed independently on a second instance (also ~13 GB, same `event`-table dominance), so this is reproducible, not a one-off. ## Root cause (confirmed in source, `dev` branch) `packages/core/src/event/sql.ts` — the `event` table has no TTL, no row cap, no size limit, and no compaction column; it just stores every event's full `data` JSON: ```ts export const EventTable = sqliteTable("event", { id: text().$type<EventV2.ID>().primaryKey(), aggregate_id: text().notNull().references(() => EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, { onDelete: "cascade" }), seq: integer().notNull(), type: text().notNull(), data: text({ mode: "json" }).$type<Record<string, unknown>>().notNull(), }, ...) ``` `packages/core/src/event.ts` — the **only** delete against `event` is a full-aggregate cascade, used when an entire session/aggregate is removed: ```ts function remove(aggregateID: string) { return db.transaction(() => Effect.gen(function* () { yield* db.delete(EventSequenceTable).where(eq(EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() yield* db.delete(EventTable).where(eq(EventTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() })).pipe(Effect.orDie) } ``` There is **no partial pruning** — nothing collapses superseded `message.updated.*` snapshots, keeps only the latest per message, caps per-aggregate history, or stores deltas. `packages/opencode/src/sync/README.md` confirms this is an intentional append-only log "for session replayability." That's a reasonable design goal, but with full-snapshot `message.updated` events and no retention it means every session's event history accumulates for the lifetime of the session, with no upper bound. `SessionCompaction.prune` does **not** address this — it trims context tokens sent to the model, not persisted `event` rows. ## Impact - Disk exhaustion on long-lived instances (containers/sandboxes/servers with persistent home dirs). - Once the volume is full, even read queries that need temp space fail with `database or disk is full`. - `VACUUM` cannot reclaim it (freelist ≈ 0%; it is all live data). The only current remediation is deleting whole sessions (cascade) or manually `DELETE FROM event ...`. ## Suggested fixes (any one would help) 1. **Compact superseded snapshots**: for snapshot-style events like `message.updated.*`, retain only the latest event per `(aggregate_id, message_id)` (or per message `seq`), deleting older ones — newer fully supersedes older. 2. **Store deltas instead of full snapshots** for `message.updated` (the README already notes `session.updated` was moved to fields-only; `message.updated` appears to still carry a full snapshot). 3. **Per-aggregate retention cap / periodic compaction** of the event log for inactive/completed sessions. ## Environment - Observed on builds in the 1.15.x–1.17.x range; root cause confirmed present on `dev` (current `latest`, 1.17.9) via the source above. - SQLite store at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Happy to provide the full per-session breakdown or a repro script if useful.

signals.title: prompt_async returns 204 after startup failure, leaving empty child sessions that appear frozen
signals.text: ## Summary Delegated/subagent sessions can be created successfully, then remain permanently empty while the caller/UI keeps polling them. The immediate trigger I observed was the known `session_message.seq` insertion bug, but the user-visible failure is broader: `POST /session/{id}/prompt_async` can fail during startup, publish/log `session.error`, still return HTTP 204, and leave a valid child session with **zero** user/assistant messages. That makes delegation features look frozen: the child session exists, `/session/{id}/message` returns 200 with an empty list, and monitors/tools keep waiting for messages that will never be written. Related existing reports/fix: - #31204 - #31413 - #31419 Those cover the `session_message.seq` crash itself. This issue is about the higher-level API/state behavior that turns a startup failure into a silent, empty, frozen child session. ## Environment observed - OpenCode version reported by CLI: `1.14.48` - OS: macOS / darwin arm64 - Delegation plugin in use: `oh-my-openagent` - Local DB: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` - Local server logs: `~/.local/share/opencode/log/2026-06-22T143351.log` ## What happened A parent session launched five delegated child sessions. Each child session row was created with a parent ID, title, directory, and model, but no message rows or parts were ever written. Example affected child sessions: ```text ses_1103540cfffe3v9MYa17MzZnc1 GDD Angle spine (@NeoAgent (Builder) subagent) ses_110354087ffeubDsuGjBMTETWX GDD social LLM (@NeoAgent (Builder) subagent) ses_110354060ffe40fMS6hHJlilGS GDD input feel rooms (@NeoAgent (Builder) subagent) ses_110354044ffevRr4Bva6HfVaXQ Engine Angle docs (@Odin (Builder) subagent) ses_110353ffbffe1F9p3vKXuus3Ze Angle spec capture (@Odin (Builder) subagent) ``` DB state for those sessions: ```text session row: present parent_id: present message rows: 0 part rows: 0 session_message rows: 0 ``` The logs show the important failure mode. For each child session, OpenCode logged `prompt_async failed [object Object]` and published `session.error`, but the HTTP request still returned 204: ```text POST /session/ses_1103540cfffe3v9MYa17MzZnc1/prompt_async ERROR prompt_async failed [object Object] service=bus type=session.error publishing POST /session/ses_1103540cfffe3v9MYa17MzZnc1/prompt_async 204 ``` After that, the server/UI continued polling: ```text GET /session/ses_1103540cfffe3v9MYa17MzZnc1/message 200 GET /session/ses_110354087ffeubDsuGjBMTETWX/message 200 ... ``` Those message responses were empty indefinitely because the initial user message was never persisted. ## Why this is especially confusing There are several inconsistent surfaces after the startup failure: 1. The child session exists in the DB. 2. `GET /session/{child}/message` succeeds, but returns no messages. 3. The original `prompt_async` HTTP call returned 204 even though startup failed. 4. `session.error` is only visible through logs/bus, not through the prompt caller as an actionable failure. 5. Some list-based SDK/plugin code treats child sessions as nonexistent because `session.list()` does not include them even though direct `session.get(id)`/`session.messages(id)` can work for real child sessions. So downstream tools see either: - “session exists but has no messages, keep polling”, or - “session not found”, depending on whether they use list-based existence checks or direct message lookup. Both obscure the real failure. ## Root cause observed There appear to be two layers: ### 1. Immediate trigger: `session_message.seq` null/NOT NULL failure The empty child sessions were created seconds before applying a local workaround for the known `session_message.seq` issue. This matches #31204/#31413/#31419. In the failing path, message/session projection insertion can fail before any user message is persisted. That leaves the newly-created child session shell without messages. ### 2. Higher-level bug: prompt startup failure is not propagated to the caller/session state Even after the internal `prompt_async` startup failed, the HTTP layer returned 204. That means callers interpret the prompt as accepted and enter their polling loop. A delegated session needs a startup invariant: > If `prompt_async` returns accepted/success, at least the initial user message should be durably visible, or the session should be durably marked failed. Currently, a third state is possible: ```text session created prompt failed before first message persisted HTTP returned 204 no durable message/error visible to polling clients ``` That is the frozen-empty state. ## Expected behavior If `prompt_async` fails before persisting the initial user message, one of these should happen: 1. `POST /session/{id}/prompt_async` returns a non-2xx error with the underlying failure, or 2. the session is durably marked failed/error and exposed through session status/messages, or 3. an error message/part is appended to the session so clients polling messages can terminate with a visible failure. Any of these would be much better than a 204 plus an empty message stream. ## Actual behavior `prompt_async` logs/publishes an error but returns 204. The child session remains queryable and empty. Delegation monitors continue polling until their own timeout/abort logic, making the feature appear frozen. ## Proposed fix ### A. Fix the known `session_message.seq` projection bug Merge or extend #31419: - Treat `event.seq == null` as missing, not just `undefined`. - Ensure every `session_message` insert gets a valid per-session `seq`. - Add a regression test around `session.next.agent.switched` and any `appendMessage` paths that create projection rows. I would also consider a migration/backfill/default safeguard so a future missed insert path cannot take down message startup entirely. ### B. Make `prompt_async` startup atomic or visibly failed Add a guard around the startup path: - after creating the session and before returning 204, ensure the initial user message was persisted; or - if the async worker is intentionally fire-and-forget, persist a startup-failed state/error when message creation fails. The key contract should be: ```text 204/accepted => callers can observe at least one new message or a running state startup failure => non-2xx response or durable session error ``` Do not let the API return accepted while leaving no observable message/error state. ### C. Expose child session existence consistently If `session.get(id)` and `session.messages(id)` can address child sessions, list-based existence checks need a reliable way to discover them too. Options: - include child sessions in `session.list()` with `parentID`, or - add/document `includeChildren=true`, or - provide/document `session.get(id)` as the correct existence check and avoid list-only existence assumptions in SDK helpers. This is not the primary crash, but it compounds the freeze by causing some tooling to report “Session not found” for real child sessions. ### D. Tests that would catch this Suggested regression tests: 1. Force `appendMessage`/projection insert failure during `prompt_async` startup and assert the HTTP caller does not receive a successful accepted response without a durable session error. 2. Create a child session, trigger startup failure, and assert `/session/{id}/message` does not remain silently empty forever without an error/status signal. 3. Create a normal child session with messages and assert direct `session.get(id)`/`session.messages(id)` and the intended listing/discovery API agree on its existence. 4. Regression for #31204/#31413: `session.next.agent.switched` writes `session_message.seq` correctly when `event.seq` is null. ## Local workaround used for confirmation I locally worked around the DB constraint issue and added plugin-side bootstrap checks so delegation no longer polls forever: - after dispatching a delegated prompt, poll `session.messages(id)` briefly; - if no new user/assistant message appears, treat startup as failed immediately; - for session reading, use direct `session.messages(id)`/`session.get(id)` instead of rejecting child sessions based only on `session.list()`. That workaround made the symptoms explicit: - completed delegated children can be read again; - old zero-message child shells now report “No messages found” instead of appearing frozen/missing; - new delegation smoke test completes normally. The durable fix should be in OpenCode core/API so plugin/tooling authors do not each need to implement their own bootstrap-detection workaround.

signals.title: [Bug] MCP prompt arguments receive literal $1/$2 placeholders instead of user input — type validation fails
signals.text: ### Description This error fires at **startup**, not on interactive use. When opencode discovers an MCP server that exposes prompts with typed arguments (e.g. `precision: int`), it calls `prompts/get` during initialization to resolve prompt templates for command registration. The `$1`/`$2` placeholders are sent as literal argument values during this startup probe, and the MCP server's typed argument validation rejects them. Example error from `mcp-mathematics` at startup: ``` MCP error 0: Could not convert argument 'precision' with value '$2' to expected type int MCP error 0: Could not convert argument 'batch_size' with value '$1' to expected type int failed to getPrompt ``` The `prompts/get` JSON payload confirms the literal placeholder is being sent: ```json { "method": "prompts/get", "params": { "name": "scientific_calculation", "arguments": { "precision": "$2", "calc_type": "general", "show_steps": false } } } ``` This was previously reported in #9776 (auto-closed due to inactivity) and confirmed by another user in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/9776#issuecomment-3787280963 who captured the same `"$1"` in the `prompts/get` payload. The root cause is in `packages/opencode/src/command/index.ts` lines 100-112. The `get template()` function maps prompt arguments to `$N` placeholders but never substitutes them against actual user-provided command arguments before calling `mcp.getPrompt()`. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.14.33 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure an MCP server that exposes prompts with typed arguments (e.g. `mcp-mathematics` via `uvx mcp-mathematics`) 2. Start opencode 3. signals.title: [FEATURE]: Feature Request: Add GUI Options to Edit Custom Providers and Manage Model Lists
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Problem Statement Currently, managing custom providers (such as local inference engines like LM Studio or Jan AI) through the OpenCode UI is a destructive or highly technical process: No Edit Functionality: Once a custom provider is connected via the UI, the only available option is a Disconnect button. There is no way to modify existing fields like the baseURL or apiKey without fully disconnecting and re-entering all settings from scratch. No UI Model Management: Adding, removing, or adjusting configuration details (such as context and output limits) for specific models under a custom provider forces users to manually locate and edit the underlying opencode.json configuration file. While a "configuration-first" approach is excellent for project version control, a basic graphical CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) interface for connected providers and models would significantly improve the user experience, especially for users frequently swapping local models or modifying network ports. 💡 Proposed Solution Introduce an "Edit" action alongside the existing "Disconnect" button in the Providers settings UI, and add a dynamic schema viewer/editor for registered models. 1. Provider Edit Modal Change the single Disconnect button to an actions menu or place an Edit button next to it. Clicking Edit should open the initial connection modal with all existing fields (Provider ID, Display Name, Base URL, etc.) pre-filled with the current configuration data. 2. Inline Model Manager Under each connected custom provider in the UI, expose a list of currently registered models. Provide an "Add Model" button that opens a simple form to define: Model ID / Name Context Window Limit (to prevent the Context Limit 0 / empty usage bar issue) Output Limit Modalities (Text, Image, etc.)
signals.author: akierum

signals.title: [FEATURE]: make OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST configurable
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/30022 recently changed the oauth server to bind to 127.0.0.1 only. I use opencode inside a container, and was using `docker run -p 19876` to get the browser on my host talking to opencode via `http://127.0.0.1:19876`. I would like a new envvar or config option to customize `OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST`. ## workaround Use a docker entrypoint with `socat` to route traffic ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash socat TCP-LISTEN:19877,fork,bind=0.0.0.0 TCP:127.0.0.1:19876 & opencode "$@" ``` When I need to authenticate, I run `docker run -p 19876:19877 --entrypoint=...`, with routes the traffic correctly: ```mermaid flowchart subgraph host browser docker subgraph container socat opencode end end browser -->|127.0.0.1:19876| docker docker -->|0.0.0.0:19877| socat socat -->|127.0.0.1:19876| opencode ```

signals.title: [BUG][Desktop vs Terminal] Pasting local file path has inconsistent behavior and no way to paste as plain text
signals.text: ### Description When pasting a local file path (e.g. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\image.png`) into opencode, the behavior differs between Desktop and Terminal, and **neither mode allows pasting the path as plain text**. ### Desktop App Behavior Pasting a local file path like `C:\Users\user\Desktop\image.png` automatically converts it to a file link (attachment reference). The path string itself is never sent to the model. ### Terminal (CLI) Behavior Pasting the same path automatically reads the file and embeds it as an image. The path string is again lost — the model receives the image content instead. ### Problem For users who use non-vision models (models that cannot process images), there is **no way to paste a local file path as plain text**. The intent is to let the AI see the path string itself (e.g., to ask it to copy the file, reference it in code, or describe what the filename means), not to embed the file content or create a link. ### Expected Behavior There should be a way to paste a local file path as **plain text** — for example: - A modifier key (Ctrl+Shift+V / Alt+V) to paste as raw text - A right-click context menu option "Paste as path" - Or auto-detection: paths wrapped in quotes or backticks are treated as text ### Environment - opencode Desktop (Windows) - opencode Terminal (Windows) - Both exhibit different behavior but neither supports plain-text path pasting ### Additional Context This is a combination of a bug (inconsistent Desktop vs Terminal behavior) and a feature request (need for a "paste as plain text" mode for file paths). The existing issue #32014 only covers the CLI side, but does not address the Desktop app or the inconsistency between the two. Related: #19892 (CLI only), #23458 (Ctrl+Shift+V works as plain text paste on Linux TUI but not documented/consistent).

signals.title: Agent bypassed Plan mode restrictions and posting a GitHub issue comment via gh
signals.text: ### Description I was in plan mode working, and my agent ran `gh issue comment` and posted a reply directly on the issue which I'm working on — without being asked to, without switching to build mode, and without triggering any permission prompt. ### Root cause The plan mode system prompt explicitly says: > Do NOT use sed, tee, echo, cat, or ANY other bash command to manipulate files — commands may ONLY read/inspect. The bash tool is not restricted in plan mode at the permission level. Plan mode only denies `edit`/`write`/`apply_patch`. `bash` inherits the default `allow` and has no code-level enforcement — all restrictions are prompt-only. There is no command allowlist or blocklist. `gh issue comment` and some other commands do not modify local files, so it falls into a grey area that the prompt does not explicitly cover. The model interpreted "only read/inspect" narrowly (local filesystem only) and considered a remote state change via GH CLI as acceptable. ### Suggested fix Add a **bash command allowlist** for plan mode. Only commands on the allowlist can execute when the plan agent is active. ### Related issues Existing plan mode issues (#25263, #19094, #28467) focus on local filesystem writes. - #25263 — File write executed in plan mode (local files) - #19094 — Plan mode agent executes file-creation via bash - #28467 — Bash commands can write files in plan mode ### Plugins N/A ### OpenCode version 1.17.11 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Work in plan mode 2. The agent runs read-only `gh` commands to inspect issues or PRs — no issues, nothing is blocked 3. At some point the agent autonomously runs `gh issue comment`, posting a reply directly on the issue 4. Throughout the entire process: no mode switch, no permission prompt, no interception ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signals.title: [Bug] zen/go model compatibility in Anthropic /v1/messages for coding-agent tool use
signals.text: # [Bug] `zen/go` model compatibility in Anthropic `/v1/messages` for coding-agent tool use ## Summary Using OpenCode `zen/go` with Anthropic-compatible `POST /v1/messages` in coding-agent workflows, model behavior is inconsistent: - `qwen3.7-max` works with tool calls. - `glm-5.2` succeeds for plain text but fails when tools are included. - `kimi-k2.7-code` and `deepseek-v4-pro` fail on message/tool schema handling. This breaks stable model switching for agent clients (Claude Code style workloads with tools). ## Environment - Endpoint: `https://opencode.ai/zen/go` - Auth header that works for this key: `x-api-key: <redacted>` - API style tested: Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` - Date: 2026-06-29 ## Confirmed model availability `GET /v1/models` returns these IDs (among others): - `glm-5.2` - `kimi-k2.7-code` - `deepseek-v4-pro` - `qwen3.7-max` ## Reproduction ### 1) Plain text request (no tools) ```bash curl -sS -X POST 'https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H "x-api-key: <redacted>" \ -d '{ "model":"glm-5.2", "max_tokens":48, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}] }' ``` Observed: - `glm-5.2` -> HTTP 200 - `qwen3.7-max` -> HTTP 200 - `kimi-k2.7-code` -> HTTP 400 (`messages must not be empty`) - `deepseek-v4-pro` -> HTTP 400 (`Empty input messages`) ### 2) Tool-call request (Anthropic tools shape) ```bash curl -sS -X POST 'https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages?beta=true' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H "x-api-key: <redacted>" \ -d '{ "model":"glm-5.2", "max_tokens":96, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Please call calc for 1+1"}], "tools":[{ "name":"calc", "description":"simple calculator", "input_schema":{ "type":"object", "properties":{"a":{"type":"number"},"b":{"type":"number"}}, "required":["a","b"] } }] }' ``` Observed: - `qwen3.7-max` -> HTTP 200 - `glm-5.2` -> HTTP 401 with message similar to `API key invalid` - `kimi-k2.7-code` -> HTTP 400 (`function name is invalid ...`) - `deepseek-v4-pro` -> HTTP 400 (`tools[0].function missing field name`) ## Why this seems like a gateway/model-adapter issue - Same key works for `qwen3.7-max` on the same endpoint. - `glm-5.2` succeeds for plain text but fails when tools are present. - Error patterns on kimi/deepseek point to request translation/schema mapping incompatibility. - For clients that rely on Anthropic `/messages` + tools, model IDs become listed-but-not-usable. ## Expected behavior For all listed Zen/Go model IDs that are advertised as available: 1. Plain text requests should work consistently, or return a clear unsupported-feature error. 2. Tool-call requests should either: - work with Anthropic tools format, or - fail with an explicit capability error (not auth-like or malformed-schema downstream errors). ## Requested fix Please normalize the Anthropic `/v1/messages` adapter across these models, especially for tool-call payloads: - `glm-5.2` - `kimi-k2.7-code` - `deepseek-v4-pro` If a model does not support Anthropic tools on Zen/Go, please expose that in model capability metadata and return a deterministic unsupported-tools error.

signals.title: Remote MCP server using Streamable HTTP (Supabase) fails on Linux with SSE 405 in runtime — persists in v1.17.11
signals.text: ## Description Remote MCP servers that migrated to Streamable HTTP (POST-only) fail on Linux at runtime with `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)`, even though the initial handshake succeeds. Reproduced with Supabase's hosted MCP (`mcp.supabase.com/mcp`, server v0.8.1). - `opencode mcp list` reports the server as `✓ connected` - `opencode mcp debug supabase-DEV` returns `HTTP response: 200 OK` and `Server info: supabase v0.8.1` - But in the TUI, the server keeps emitting `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)` This looks like the same root cause as #24946 (closed without a fix commit) and the open feature #28567. Filing a fresh report because it still reproduces on the latest release (v1.17.11) with a widely-used server. Note: #5636 (Figma 405) appears to be a different issue (client_name whitelist in dynamic OAuth), not a transport problem. ## Plugins None. ## OpenCode version v1.17.11 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure the Supabase remote MCP with a Bearer PAT (CI pattern from Supabase's own docs): ```json { "mcp": { "supabase-DEV": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=<project-ref>", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <personal-access-token>" }, "enabled": true } } } ``` 2. Start opencode and open the TUI → the server shows `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)`. 3. `opencode mcp list` says `✓ connected`; `opencode mcp debug supabase-DEV` says `200 OK`. Direct curl against the endpoint with the same token: - `GET /mcp` → `405 Method Not Allowed` - `POST /mcp` with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` → `200 OK` So the server only speaks Streamable HTTP (POST); the handshake succeeds, but opencode's runtime transport keeps attempting GET/SSE. There's no way to force Streamable HTTP from config: the remote MCP `type` enum in `https://opencode.ai/config.json` is only `["remote"]` (no `"http"`/`"sse"` toggle). Supabase's docs show `"type": "http"` for clients that expose that field (Claude Code, Cursor, AI SDK), but opencode doesn't expose it. ## Screenshot and/or share link N/A (curl + `mcp debug` output above). ## Operating System Linux ## Terminal Alacritty

Users have to manually locate the file in a file explorer or reconstruct the path by hand, which slows down workflows like: - Referencing a file in a commit message, PR description, or Slack/chat message. - Pasting a path into a terminal command (`cat`, `code`, `git blame`, etc.). - Sharing a file location with a teammate or an AI assistant. ## Proposed behavior Add a **copy** action in both: 1. **Diff review view**: right-click context menu on the file name 2. **File viewer**: right-click context menu on the file tab. The action should offer at least one of the following formats: - **File name only** — e.g. `Component.tsx` - **Relative path** — e.g. `src/components/Component.tsx` - **Full/absolute path** — e.g. `/home/user/project/src/components/Component.tsx` ## Nice to have - Keyboard shortcut to copy the relative path of the currently focused file. - Visual confirmation (toast/tooltip) when the path is copied, e.g. "Copied to clipboard". ## Willingness to contribute Happy to submit a PR for this if there's consensus on the approach / a maintainer gives the go-ahead on the general direction.

signals.title: Zen: byte-identical requests to glm-5.2 intermittently reroute to a cold-cache provider — please enable stickyProvider for multi-sourced models
signals.text: ### Summary `glm-5.2` served through Zen (`/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`) is multi-sourced across upstream providers with no sticky routing, so **byte-identical consecutive requests intermittently land on a provider with a cold prompt cache** — a full prompt re-bill and a much slower prefill, for no client-side reason. The gateway already has the mechanism to prevent this (`stickyProvider` + the `x-opencode-session` sticky id); it just doesn't appear to be enabled for this model. Requesting it be enabled (at least `"prefer"`) for `glm-5.2` and other multi-sourced models. ### Repro 10 byte-identical requests (same 19,370-token prompt, `temperature: 0`, `stream: false`, 3s apart, same client / API key / IP), non-streaming `usage` captured: | call | `cached_tokens` | note | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0 | cold (expected) | | 2–5 | 19,328 | warm | | **6** | **0** | **full re-bill on identical bytes** | | 7 | 19,328 | warm again | | **8** | **10** | **effectively cold again** | | 9–10 | 19,369 | warm — different cache granularity than calls 2–7 | Two independent signals that these are different upstream providers, not cache eviction: - the cached-token quantization flips between 19,328 (64-token-aligned) and 19,369 (exact), - the `usage` JSON shape itself flips between two schemas (one includes `estimated_cost` and `reasoning_tokens`, one doesn't) across calls in the same run. Latency impact on this prompt size: ~6.3s cold vs ~1.6s warm per request. In an agent loop that re-sends a large prefix every turn, each reroute costs several seconds of prefill plus the full uncached token cost (~5.4× the cached rate at glm-5.2 pricing). <details><summary>repro script (python, stdlib only)</summary> ```python import json, time, urllib.request KEY = "sk-..." # zen api key para = ("Section %d. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while the cache " "measurement proceeds in a fully deterministic manner without any variation. ") system = "You are a terse assistant. Reply with at most three words.\n\n" + "".join(para % i for i in range(1, 701)) msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with only: OK"}] for i in range(10): body = json.dumps({"model": "glm-5.2", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0, "stream": False}).encode() req = urllib.request.Request("https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions", data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}", "User-Agent": "repro/1.0"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r: u = json.load(r).get("usage", {}) print(i + 1, json.dumps(u)) time.sleep(3) ``` </details> ### Where this comes from (from the gateway source in this repo) `packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/util/handler.ts`: - `stickyId = x-opencode-session header ?? workspaceID ?? ip` - `createStickyTracker(modelId, modelInfo.stickyProvider, stickyId)` — the persisted session→provider pin **only exists when the model's `stickyProvider` is set** (`"strict" | "prefer"`, `stickyProviderTracker.ts`). The code comments show it's enabled for codex models ("cannot change codex model providers mid-session"). - Without it, `selectProvider` hashes the last 4 chars of `stickyId` modulo the *filtered* provider pool — and the pool composition changes with live budget/TPM/TPS state, so the same stickyId periodically resolves to a different provider → cold cache, even for a client sending identical bytes with a stable identity. ### Ask 1. Enable `stickyProvider` (at least `"prefer"`) for `glm-5.2` — and consider it as the default for any multi-sourced model whose upstreams have prompt caches. The mechanism already exists and ships for codex models. 2. Consider documenting `x-opencode-session` for direct API users, so non-opencode clients (other agents/harnesses using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint) can supply a stable session id and benefit from sticky routing and per-session cache scoping. Happy to provide more captures. Found while investigating prompt-cache behavior of agent harnesses driving Zen; we're a paying Go-bundle workspace. Reported-by: @Peetiegonzalez cc @Peetiegonzalez

signals.title: Desktop Home view shows projects but zero sessions (database is correct)
signals.text: # Desktop (GUI) Home view shows projects but zero sessions — database is correct ## Summary The OpenCode Desktop app (macOS) shows the list of projects in the Home / sidebar, but every project displays **"Nothing here yet" / 0 sessions**, even though the SQLite database contains correctly-linked sessions. The terminal `opencode` CLI reads and writes the exact same database without any problem. ## Environment - OpenCode Desktop: **1.17.16** (also reproduced on earlier versions) - `opencode` CLI: **1.17.15** - OS: macOS (darwin, arm64) - Database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (~916 MB, 164 sessions, 5+ projects) ## Observed behavior 1. Open Desktop → Home view. 2. Sidebar lists the 3 projects the user has added (e.g. `opencode-settings-project`, `dockinkz`, `usage-widget`). 3. Selecting any project shows **"Nothing here yet — Create a session to get started"**. No session is listed for ANY project. 4. The terminal `opencode` CLI in the same projects works perfectly and its sessions are persisted to the DB. ## Expected behavior Sessions that exist in the database for a given project should appear in the Desktop Home view for that project. ## Evidence that the data is correct (not a DB/config issue) Verified directly against `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`: - `session.project_id` correctly references `project.id` (FK intact): ``` SELECT s.id, p.worktree, COUNT(*) FROM session s JOIN project p ON p.id = s.project_id GROUP BY p.id; -- /Users/diasmazhenov/vibecode/usage-widget | 3 -- /Users/diasmazhenov/vibecode/dockinkz | 1 -- .../opencode-settings-project | 1 ``` - `session.directory` matches `project.worktree` (fixed a mismatch, but the other projects already matched and still show 0). - `session.time_archived` is NULL for all relevant sessions. - `session.workspace_id` is NULL for all (consistent, not the cause). - `workspace` table is empty for everyone — not the differentiator. - The Desktop process holds the **same** shared DB file (confirmed via `lsof`: `OpenCode … /Users/diasmazhenov/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`). - Other projects (`/`, `open-design`) that are NOT in the Desktop sidebar DO have many sessions in the DB (86 / 73), so the Desktop's project list is a curated subset — but the 3 it shows still render 0 sessions despite valid data. ## Notes - The local Desktop API (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/project/:id/session`) returns `401 Unauthorized` (Basic realm) and the session list endpoint returns empty; the auth token could not be retrieved from local storage / process env, so the failure appears to be server-side session listing within the Desktop-embedded server rather than a pure frontend render issue. - A fresh restart of the Desktop app (which regenerates `opencode.global.dat`) does not resolve it. - `opencode serve` started manually also returns empty session lists for the same DB, suggesting the session-listing query/path used by the server is the failing component. ## Impact The Desktop GUI is effectively unusable for browsing/reopening past sessions; only the terminal CLI can access them. ## Root-cause analysis (from source) The Desktop Home session list pipeline: 1. `packages/app/src/pages/home.tsx` → `sessionLoad` query calls `focusedSync().project.loadSessions(directory, …)` for each `projectDirectories()`. 2. `packages/app/src/context/directory-sync.ts` → `fetch()` calls `client.session.list()` (SDK client scoped to the project directory) and stores results in the sync store. 3. `buildHomeSessionRecords()` (home.tsx:108) reads `sync.child(directory)[0]` and runs `sortedRootSessions()` → `roots()` → `isRootVisibleSession()`. 4. `packages/app/src/pages/layout/helpers.ts:26`: ```ts const isRootVisibleSession = (session, directory) => pathKey(session.directory) === pathKey(directory) && !session.parentID && !session.time?.archived ``` **The bug:** `isRootVisibleSession` reads `session.directory`, but the OpenCode server's `GET /api/session` response does **NOT** include a top-level `directory` field — the directory is only present under `location.directory`: ```json { "id": "ses_xxx", "projectID": "…", "location": { "directory": "/Users/…/project" }, "time": { "created": …, "updated": … } } ``` So `session.directory` is `undefined` → `pathKey(undefined) === pathKey(directory)` is `false` → **every session is filtered out** of the Home list. This matches the reported symptom exactly (projects show, sessions never do, for all projects). `projectForSession()` (helpers.ts:104) has the same problem: its directory fallback `pathKey(project.worktree) === pathKey(session.directory)` also fails when `session.directory` is undefined (only the `projectID` direct match works there). ### Suggested fix Either: - The server should return a top-level `directory` field on sessions (mirroring `location.directory`), or - The SDK/client `Session` type should map `location.directory` → `directory` before the UI consumes it.
signals.author: DiasMazhenov

signals.title: TUI dark/light mode does not follow Windows system theme
signals.text: ## Description On Windows 11 Terminal, when the user toggles the system dark/light mode (Settings > Personalization > Colors > Choose your mode), the terminal title bar changes colour but the terminal background colour (queried via OSC 11 `\e]11;?\e\`) does NOT change. Since opencode's TUI derives its dark/light mode exclusively from `terminalMode()` — which reads the terminal background colour — the TUI never detects the system theme switch and stays on the wrong colour mode. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Run opencode TUI on Windows 11 Terminal (Windows Terminal v1.20+) 2. Observe the TUI is in light mode (or dark mode) 3. Open Windows Settings → Personalization → Colors 4. Toggle "Choose your default app mode" between Light and Dark 5. The terminal title bar immediately reflects the change 6. The opencode TUI does NOT switch its colour mode ## Expected behaviour The TUI should follow the Windows system theme when running on Windows 11 Terminal, just like it follows the terminal background colour on other platforms/terminals. ## System info - Windows 11 - Windows Terminal 1.20+ - opencode dev branch ## Suggested fix Read the Windows registry key `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize\AppsUseLightTheme` as an additional signal. On Windows Terminal the background colour is not a reliable indicator of the system theme because the title bar and buffer background are decoupled.

signals.title: Bug: opencode upgrade fails with 403 Forbidden due to GitHub API Rate Limit (lack of GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN environment variable support)
signals.text: ### Describe the bug Running `opencode upgrade` fails with an unexpected 403 HTTP status code when the GitHub API Rate Limit for unauthenticated requests from the client IP address is exhausted. This happens because the upgrade command queries `https://api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode/releases/latest` using an unauthenticated request (without passing authorization headers). ### To Reproduce 1. Exhaust the GitHub API rate limit for unauthenticated requests from your current IP (e.g., behind a residential CGNAT or a shared public gateway). 2. Run: ```bash opencode upgrade ``` 3. Observe the output: ``` ● Using method: curl Error: Unexpected error StatusCode: non 2xx status code (403 GET https://api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode/releases/latest) ``` ### Expected behavior The upgrade tool should check if standard industry environment variables `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` are present in the shell environment. If found, it should inject them as an `Authorization: token <TOKEN>` header in its API requests to api.github.com. This is standard practice for CLI utilities to leverage the higher authenticated rate limits (5,000 requests/hr) and avoid unauthenticated blockages on shared IPs. ### Environment - OS: Linux Mint 21.3 (x86-64) - OpenCode Version: 1.17.15 - Connection Method: curl

signals.title: GitHub Action: per-message agent override on session.chat() is ignored when session created without a default agent
signals.text: ### Description The `anomalyco/opencode/github` Action's `agent` input is silently ignored — the model always responds using the default (`build`) agent instead of the one configured. Confirmed this is **not** a general agent-resolution bug: `opencode run --agent <name>` (same `opencode` version, run manually) applies the agent correctly. The bug appears isolated to the code path used by `github/index.ts`. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Define a project-level primary agent, e.g. `.opencode/agents/my-custom-agent.md`: ```yaml --- description: "Custom agent for testing" mode: primary --- You are a custom test agent. Always mention "CUSTOM_AGENT_ACTIVE" in your first reply. ``` 2. Add a workflow step invoking the Action with that agent: ```yaml - uses: anomalyco/opencode/github@latest with: model: <provider>/<model> agent: my-custom-agent ``` 3. Trigger the workflow via an `issue_comment` event (e.g. commenting `/oc do something` on an issue). 4. In the job logs, confirm the composite action step logged the env var correctly: ``` AGENT: my-custom-agent ``` 5. Inspect the full job log for `stream {...agent: ...}` entries — observe that `agent` is always `"build"`, never `"my-custom-agent"`. 6. Grep the full log for the two possible fallback warnings from `resolveAgent()`: ``` agent "my-custom-agent" not found. Falling back to default agent agent "my-custom-agent" is a subagent, not a primary agent. Falling back to default agent ``` Confirm **neither** appears — ruling out a simple lookup/validation failure. 7. As a control, run the same agent locally on the same `opencode` version, bypassing the Action entirely: ``` opencode run "Reply with the agent persona you're running as." --agent my-custom-agent --format json ``` 8. Confirm the local CLI invocation correctly applies `my-custom-agent` (its response reflects the agent's system prompt), proving the agent config itself is valid and the bug is isolated to the `github run` code path, not general agent resolution. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Debian 13 ### Terminal xterm-256color ### Workaround To still enable an custom agent per job, extend the workflow yml with the following overrid ```yaml - uses: anomalyco/opencode/github@latest env: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: '{"default_agent": "<my-custom-agent>"}' with: model: <provider>/<model> ```

signals.title: [FEATURE]: option to automatically pause work during deepseek and xiaomi peak hours
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Deepseek is now employing peak hour pricing as of today. So does Xiaomi. To keep costs low and load balance as Deepseek and Xiaomi want with this pricing, opencode can have a feature to automatically pause work within the peak hour window, when the model provider is deepseek or Xiaomi, or an API reseller such as opencode zen/go or openrouter using non free models. This would be useful when running long autonomous tasks such as a ralph loop with oh my openagent which do not require interaction with the user and can run unattented for several hours even while the user is sleeping, when given answers to common questions in the prompt. If work is started within the peak hour window, it could wait until the peak hour window is over before starting to do it. The feature could be turned on by default to avoid unexpected cost overruns with deepseek and can be optional with xiaomi since with xiaomi with this feature there would be only 8 off peak (productive) hours https://mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/tokenplan/Token%20Plan/subscription. whereas with deepseek there would be about 16 off peak (productive) hours daily. Since we don't know for sure whether an API is hosted by the provider or if the provdier is a reseller, this feature can be turned on by default based on model name. The user can be warned about peak pricing when they choose deepseek or xiaomi models which would be a UI change. The feature could use time zones to start and stop based on the user's local time. However this can be wrong so for reliability maybe it would be better to directly query UTC time via the network time protocol. The user should be able to override this feature and to be not asked again, when asked. I wonder if this is a better fit for oh-my-openagent given that i have only seen this issue with it installed because it can run for like 7 hours unattended but with opencode on its own it can sometimes run for like an hour unattended when asked to iterate until something is done or when asked to run in a loop and that can fall into peak pricing

signals.title: Windows paths from SSE clients not converted on Linux/WSL — corrupts database, crashes server, 100% WSL CPU
signals.text: **Related issues:** #16680, #15719, #27879, #30895, #33107 **Related PR:** #34256 ### Description Running `opencode web` or `opencode serve` inside WSL breaks as soon as a Windows browser or Desktop client connects. The SSE `/event?directory=` endpoint receives native Windows paths (`C:\Users\K\...`), but the path normalization function `windowsPath()` is a **no-op on Linux**. These raw Windows paths get concatenated with the server working directory (producing garbage like `/home/k/opencode/C:\...`) and written into the SQLite database. On restart, `Project.list()` crashes: `Path.isAbsolute("C:/Users/...")` returns `false` on Linux, and the code's fallback check is gated behind `process.platform === "win32"`. The resulting error/retry loop **saturates the WSL VM to 100% CPU**, freezing both the opencode server and the entire WSL environment. This makes `opencode web` / `opencode serve` in WSL completely unusable — the very act of connecting from Windows destroys the server's ability to function. #### Root Cause Two functions are platform-gated to Windows only: **`packages/core/src/fs-util.ts:147` — `windowsPath()`** skips conversion on Linux/WSL: ```ts export function windowsPath(p: string): string { if (process.platform !== "win32") return p // ... } ``` When a Windows client sends `?directory=C:\Users\K\...`, this function returns the path unchanged. `path.resolve()` then treats it as relative to CWD, producing `/home/k/opencode/C:\Users\K\...`. **`packages/core/src/database/path.ts:14-18` — `absolute()`** rejects Windows paths on Linux: ```ts function absolute(input: string) { const result = storagePath(input) if (!nodePath.posix.isAbsolute(result) && !(process.platform === "win32" && isWindowsStoragePath(result))) { throw new Error(`Path is not absolute: ${input}`) } } ``` The `isWindowsStoragePath()` function would correctly identify `C:/...` as valid, but it's never consulted because the outer `process.platform === "win32"` guard is `false` on Linux. #### Log Evidence ```log ERROR message=failed ref=err_a576f06d error="EffectDrizzleQueryError: Failed query: select ... from \"project\" (cause: Cause([Fail(Error: Path is not absolute: C:/Users/K/Documents/INFO)]))" ``` ```log INFO message="creating instance" directory=/home/k/opencode/C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode INFO message="fromDirectory" directory=/home/k/opencode/C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode WARN message="failed to initialize fff" error="Invalid path C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode" ERROR message="FileSystem.realPath (C:/Users/K/Documents/test-opencode)" error="ENOENT: no such file or directory" ``` ```log INFO message="global event connected" INFO message="creating instance" directory="/home/k/opencode/C:\\Users\\K\\Documents\\test-opencode" ``` ### Plugins none ### OpenCode version 1.17.20 (tested on Linux binary, WSL Debian, Windows binary) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install opencode inside WSL (Debian/Ubuntu), start `opencode web` with a clean state 2. Open `http://localhost:3030` in a **Windows** browser (or use Windows Desktop with remote server configured to WSL) 3. Immediately — within seconds of the browser loading — the SSE `/event?directory=` endpoint receives the frontend's native Windows path: ``` ?directory=C:\Users\K\Documents\my-project ``` 4. Server's `windowsPath()` is a no-op on Linux. `path.resolve()` treats it as relative to CWD: ``` → "/home/k/opencode/C:\Users\K\Documents\my-project" ``` 5. Server logs `"creating instance" directory=/home/k/opencode/C:\Users\K\Documents\my-project` 6. `Project.fromDirectory()` writes the garbage path to SQLite `project` table 7. `FSUtil.resolve()` immediately fails with `ENOENT` on `realPath(C:/Users/K/...)` because the path doesn't exist on Linux 8. FFF initialization fails with `"Invalid path C:/Users/K/Documents/my-project"` 9. Server enters tight error/retry loop — keeps attempting operations on the garbage path → **WSL VM spikes to 100% CPU within seconds** The problem manifests on the very first Windows client connection. ### Screenshot and/or share link none ### Operating System Windows 11 host, WSL2 Debian guest (Linux kernel via wsl) ### Terminal WSL terminal (Debian), `opencode web` process

signals.title: Vertex AI multi-region location (us/eu) produces invalid hostname
signals.text: ### Description When the Vertex AI provider's `location` is set to a continental multi-region value like `us` or `eu`, opencode builds an invalid API hostname: Invalid hostname: us-aiplatform.googleapis.com Only `global` is treated as not needing a region prefix on the hostname; `us` and `eu` need the same treatment (they're multi-region, not single-region like `us-central1`). signals.title: [FEATURE]: expose structured Retryable.action contract for downstream SDK consumers
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. > Note: [#32633](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/32633) covers a related but distinct use case — machine-readable exit codes for CLI/process wrappers. This request is about the in-process SDK/API contract (`Retryable.action` shape) for downstream harnesses that embed or wrap OpenCode programmatically. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Problem `retry.ts` produces `{ message, action?: { reason, provider } }` but this shape isn't documented as a stable API contract. Downstream harnesses (e.g. oh-my-openagent) reverse-engineer it via independent regex fallback classifiers, which silently diverge as providers change. Tracked concretely in [code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#5451](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/5451): three separate pattern lists in the harness layer, requiring 3+ file touches whenever a new provider error shape is added. ## Proposed Document and stabilize the `Retryable.action` shape so consumers can rely on it without parsing raw error strings. Ideally extend it with: - `retry_after_seconds: number | null` (already available from provider `Retry-After` headers in some cases) - `category: "quota_exceeded" | "rate_limited" | "model_not_found" | "auth_failed" | "transient"` alongside the existing `reason`/`provider` fields This would let downstream tools drop their pattern lists entirely and just consume the structured signal OpenCode already produces internally. ## References - [code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#5451](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/5451) — downstream tracking - [BerriAI/litellm#33371](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/33371) — parallel upstream RFC for LiteLLM - [code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#4886](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/4886) — gateway architecture RFC - [#32633](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/32633) — related: CLI exit codes for process wrappers (different scope)

signals.title: tui: default_agent is ignored on startup in V2
signals.text: ## Summary The OpenCode V2 full TUI ignores `default_agent` when starting a new session and selects `Build` instead. This occurs with both built-in and custom primary agents. ## Environment - opencode version: `opencode2 v0.0.0-next-15636` - OS: Linux 7.1.2-arch3-1, x86_64 - Terminal: tmux (`TERM_PROGRAM=tmux`, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`) - Shell: `/bin/zsh` - Install/channel: next - Active plugins: None in the clean reproduction. The normal environment has local `goal-mode` and `tmux-status` plugins, but the issue was reproduced with an isolated `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and all plugins disabled. ## Reproduction 1. Start the full TUI with an isolated configuration and the built-in `plan` agent configured as the default: ```sh XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/opencode-clean \ OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"default_agent":"plan","plugins":["-*"]}' \ opencode2 --standalone ``` 2. Type any text in the prompt so the selected agent appears in the status line. 3. Observe that the status line shows `Build`. The issue also reproduces with a custom primary agent: ```jsonc { "default_agent": "full", "agents": { "full": { "description": "Build without permission prompts", "mode": "primary", "permissions": [ { "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" } ] } } } ``` ## Expected Behavior The full TUI should initially select the agent configured by `default_agent`. With the minimal reproduction it should start in `Plan`; with the custom configuration it should start in `full`. ## Actual Behavior The full TUI always starts in `Build`. The agent catalog is returned with `Build` first, and the TUI selects that first entry instead of the configured default. ## Additional Context - Reproduces consistently. - Reproduces with the built-in `plan` agent, so it is not specific to custom agents. - Reproduces with all plugins disabled and isolated global configuration. - Restarting the shared OpenCode service does not help. - Creating a session through the API with `agent: "full"` and opening it using `opencode2 --session <id>` still initializes the TUI selector to `Build`. - `opencode2 mini --agent full` selects the requested agent, but changes to the minimal interface and is not a workaround for the full TUI. - Immediate manual workaround: press `Shift+Tab` after startup when the desired custom agent is the last catalog entry.
