signals.title: fff watcher: GitStatusCache loops even after file changes stop, resulting in 100% cpu usage
signals.text: ### Description ### Summary An idle opencode session pins one core at ~100% for many minutes. The hot thread is `fff-watcher-own`. For every batch of file-watcher events it opens the git repository, computes git status, and frees the repository again. A fresh `Repository::open` per batch means libgit2 re-reads and re-parses the whole 6.3 MB index every cycle — including a SHA-1 hash over the full file — so each cycle costs hundreds of milliseconds. The event queue drains slower than build tools produce events, and the thread keeps burning CPU long after all file writes stop. The events that trigger this are all gitignored paths: a Gradle daemon writing `.gradle/9.6.0/fileHashes/fileHashes.bin`, lock files, and `executionHistory.bin`. A normal Gradle build writes thousands of files under `build/` and `.gradle/`, so on Android/JVM projects every build re-pins the core. ### Observed - Process at ~100% CPU from launch: 4:30 CPU time in 4:37 elapsed. `ps -M` shows one thread at 98.6%; all others idle. - Verified with `fd --changed-within 60s`: zero file modifications in the repo in the previous minute. A fresh `sample` in the same minute still shows the watcher thread at full load in the same stacks, still inside `FilePicker::handle_file_modify` — it is draining a backlog, not reacting to live events. - `.git/index` mtime unchanged throughout, so this is not a feedback loop through the index file. ### Stack evidence 5-second `sample(1)` of the process, `fff-watcher-own` thread (4159 samples total, 3433 in the watcher loop; trimmed, full files attached): ``` 4159 Thread: fff-watcher-own 3433 thread main loop ├─ 1917 fff_search::git::GitStatusCache::git_status_for_paths (+432) │ └─ 1916 git2::repo::Repository::status_file │ └─ 1670 git_status_file │ └─ 1383 git_repository_index__weakptr → git_index__open → git_index_read │ ├─ 504 parse_index → git_hash_buf → SHA1DCUpdate ← hashes the whole 6.3 MB index │ ├─ 492 parse_index → git_index_entrymap_put ← mostly __tolower in put/resize │ └─ 313 parse_index → index_entry_dup → git_path_str_is_valid (next_hfs_char, strncasecmp) ├─ 1516 fff_search::git::GitStatusCache::git_status_for_paths (+1384) │ └─ read_status_impl → git2::repo::Repository::statuses → git_status_list_new ├─ 459 git_repository_free ├─ 182 git2::repo::Repository::open ├─ 39 fff_search::file_picker::FilePicker::handle_file_modify └─ 32 git2::repo::Repository::is_path_ignored ``` Reading of the numbers: - `Repository::open` (182) and `git_repository_free` (459) both show up hot → the repository handle is not kept alive between event batches. - Because of that, `git_status_file` hits `git_index__open` → `git_index_read` → `parse_index` on nearly every call: 1383 of 1670 samples inside `git_status_file` are index re-parsing, dominated by SHA1DC hashing of the index file and per-character `tolower` while building the case-insensitive entry map. - On top of the per-path `status_file` calls, `read_status_impl` also runs a full `git_status_list_new` worktree scan (1516 samples). ### Why this hurts Cost per event batch on this repo: full index parse (SHA-1 over 6.3 MB + 28k-entry map build) + per-path status + a full status list scan. That is hundreds of milliseconds per batch. Gradle touches thousands of gitignored files per build, so the watcher falls behind and pins a core for the whole build plus many minutes afterwards, while the session looks idle. ### Configuration that should prevent this, but does not Global `opencode.jsonc` already excludes every directory involved, and snapshots are off: ```jsonc "snapshot": false, "watcher": { "ignore": ["node_modules/**", "dist/**", ".git/**", "**/build/**", ".kotlin/**", ".gradle/**", ".venv/**", "build/**"] } ``` The events driving the CPU burn are all under `.gradle/`, which this config explicitly ignores. So `watcher.ignore` has no effect on the fff watcher — consistent with #37740. `snapshot: false` rules snapshots out as the trigger (also confirmed by `.git/index` mtime staying unchanged during the burn) ### Expected - The watcher keeps one open `Repository` (or at least the parsed index) per repo and invalidates it on `.git/index` change, instead of open → status → free per batch. - Gitignored paths are dropped before the git-status pipeline runs. `is_path_ignored` appears in the samples, but the expensive status work runs for batches whose only content is gitignored build output. - One batched `statuses()` call per debounced event group instead of per-path `status_file`. ### Related - #37740 — `watcher.ignore` never reaches the embedded fff engine; a root `.ignore` file is the only channel fff honors. This report is a concrete consequence: the config above ignores `.gradle/**`, yet fff still runs its git-status pipeline for `.gradle` events. --- ## Local workaround Per #37740, a root `.ignore` file is the only ignore channel fff honors. - Root `.ignore` with `.gradle/`, `.git/`, `**/build/**` - `.ignore` added to `.git/info/exclude` so it stays out of the repo ### Plugins - ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open an opencode session in a large repo (tens of thousands of tracked files; a multi-MB `.git/index`). 2. Run any tool that churns gitignored files in the workspace (a Gradle build is a reliable source; anything writing thousands of files under an ignored directory should do). 3. Watch the process: one thread (`fff-watcher-own`) sits at ~100% during the churn and long after it stops. `sample <pid>` shows the stacks above. ### Screenshot and/or share link - ### Operating System macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Apple Silicon ### Terminal iTerm2, IntelliJ embedded terminal

signals.title: run --agent ignores the agent's declared model and silently resolves the global default — banner misleads headless runs
signals.text: # run --agent ignores the agent's declared model and silently resolves the global default — banner misleads headless runs ## Summary When an agent file declares its own `model:`, `opencode2 run --agent <name>` does not use it for headless sessions. The session model silently resolves to the global config default instead, and the run banner advertises that default with no indication that the agent's declared model was ignored. In an interactive TUI this might be noticed; in headless automation (CI, benchmarking, agent harnesses) it is completely silent — runs happen on an unintended model with zero error or warning. ## Reproduction Global config `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "model": { "providerID": "opencode", "model": "deepseek-v4-flash-free" } } ``` Agent file `.opencode/agents/modelprobe.md`: ```yaml --- description: "Model resolution probe" mode: primary model: opencode/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free --- Reply with exactly: OK ``` Run: ``` $ opencode2 run --agent modelprobe --auto "Reply with exactly: OK" > modelprobe · deepseek-v4-flash-free OK ``` Expected: `> modelprobe · nemotron-3.5-lightning-free` (the agent's declared model). Actual: the global default, silently. The agent's model is **not a parse failure** — `opencode2 debug agents` resolves it correctly: ``` $ opencode2 debug agents agent name: modelprobe agent model field: {"id": "nemotron-3.5-lightning-free", "providerID": "opencode"} ``` Contrast — the explicit CLI override IS honored: ``` $ opencode2 run --agent modelprobe --model opencode/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free --auto "Reply with exactly: OK" > modelprobe · nemotron-3.5-lightning-free OK ``` ## Impact - Headless harnesses (CI, benchmarking, agent pipelines) silently run on the wrong model — no error, no warning, no exit-code difference, and the banner actively *confirms* the wrong model without helping. - Model choice changes tool-call behavior: in our harness, the wrongly resolved default (a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint) refused tool calls and hallucinated tool names (`google:search`, etc.), contaminating multiple probe runs before the mismatch was finally noticed via the banner. ## Expected behavior - `run --agent` should use the agent's declared `model:` first, with `--model` as an explicit override (the override path already works). - If the agent's model cannot be used for any reason, emit a visible warning on stderr/banner explaining what was resolved instead — never substitute silently. ## Environment - `opencode2` 0.0.0-next-17430 (channel `next`; observed on 17403 in the same session before upgrade) - macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 (Apple Silicon) - Shell zsh, terminal ghostty; user plugin `notify.ts` present - Config layout: global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (default model), project `.opencode/agents/*.md` (agent model)

signals.title: Windows Desktop: 'Open in PowerShell' fails (directory passed as script argument)
signals.text: ## Describe the bug In OpenCode Desktop on Windows, the session header **Open in** menu's **PowerShell** entry fails. Picking it spawns `powershell.exe` with the project directory passed as a **script-file argument**, so PowerShell exits immediately with `CommandNotFoundException` (exit code 1). The app shows a "Request failed" error toast (from the `open-path` IPC rejection), and a PowerShell window briefly flashes with the script error. This is distinct from the earlier `spawn [object Promise] ENOENT` bug (#26928/#27078), which is already fixed in current versions — `resolveAppPath()` is now correctly awaited. This is a remaining functional bug in how the resolved app path is invoked for PowerShell on Windows. ## Reproduction steps 1. Open OpenCode Desktop on Windows (tested on 1.18.18). 2. Open a project (e.g. one whose path contains spaces). 3. In the session header, open the **Open in** dropdown and select **PowerShell**. 4. Observe the error. ## Expected behavior Selecting PowerShell should open a working PowerShell session rooted at the current project directory (like the working terminal paths do). ## Actual behavior `powershell.exe` is launched with the directory as a positional argument, which PowerShell interprets as a script file path. Result: `CommandNotFoundException`, exit code 1, and a "Request failed" toast. The exact main-process call is effectively: ``` execFile("C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe", ["C:\\path\\to\\project"]) ``` Error from PowerShell: ``` The term 'C:\path\to\project' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program. ... CommandNotFoundException ``` File Explorer (shell.openPath) works, and View → Toggle Terminal / session terminal (PTY path) work — only the Open in → PowerShell path is broken. ## Suggested fix On Windows, don't pass the directory as a positional script argument. Use the child's working directory instead, e.g.: ``` execFile(pwsh.exe, ["-NoExit"], { cwd: projectDir }) ``` or, for Windows PowerShell (the current `where powershell` resolution), something like: ``` execFile(powershell.exe, ["-NoExit", "-Command", `Set-Location -LiteralPath '${projectDir}'`], { windowsHide: false }) ``` ## Environment - OpenCode Desktop: 1.18.18 - Install source: https://opencode.ai/download, Windows x64 installer - OS: Microsoft Windows 11, x64 - `where powershell` → `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` - `where pwsh` → `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Show subagent start time and execution duration
signals.text: **Description:** It would be very useful to display timing information for subagent calls in the UI. Currently, when multiple subagents are invoked, it can be difficult to understand **when each subagent was started** and **how long it took to complete**, especially when several agents are running or being delegated in sequence. ### Proposed enhancement For each subagent invocation, display: * **Invocation time** — when the subagent was started. * **Execution duration** — how long the subagent took to complete. * Optionally, **completion time** as well, if it fits naturally into the existing UI. For example, the UI could show something similar to: ```text ▣ Delegators/Workers/Openai-Gpt-5.6-Luna/... 15:02:31 Completed in 42s ▣ General 15:03:14 Completed in 18s ▣ Code-Reviewers/Openai-Gpt-5.6-Luna/... 15:03:35 Completed in 1m 07s ``` This would make it much easier to understand the execution flow, identify slow subagents, and debug or analyze complex multi-agent workflows. ### Why this would be useful This information would help with: * understanding the timeline of agent/subagent execution; * identifying slow or unexpectedly long-running subagents; * debugging delegation and parallel execution; * comparing execution times between different agents; * getting a clearer picture of overall workflow performance. The timestamp could be displayed inline with the subagent call, while the duration could be added once the subagent finishes. ### Example ![Example of the proposed UI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99d97500-f35b-413e-9a44-f5c6cce6e374) I think even a minimal implementation showing the **start time + execution duration** would already provide a lot of value.

signals.title: opencode web: server tidak mount route API v2 (model/default, project/current, generate)
signals.text: ## Summary OpenCode Web in 1.18.18 serves a frontend bundle that calls API v2 routes which the same server does not mount. The result is that the built-in web UI loads, but cannot send a message. ## Environment - Windows 11 - OpenCode CLI 1.18.18 (npm latest at the time of testing) - Also reproduced with 1.18.16 in an isolated installation - Server started with `opencode web --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` - Authenticated localhost server; no public bind or Funnel ## Reproduction 1. Start the server with the command above. 2. Open the web UI served by that server and create or open a session. 3. Submit a message from the frontend. 4. Inspect the network requests and response content. ## Observed behavior - `GET /api/health`, `/api/location`, `/api/agent`, `/api/session`, message reads, and `/api/session/active` are available. - `GET /api/model/default`, `/api/project`, `/api/project/current`, and `/api/config` return the HTML fallback instead of the API response. - `POST /api/session/{id}/generate` returns HTTP 200 with the HTML fallback instead of a JSON generation response. - The frontend bundle served by the same server requests the missing v2 routes, so the UI cannot complete message submission. - CLI `opencode attach` can connect to the server in an interactive TUI, which suggests the server/session path itself is available while the web API surface is inconsistent. ## Expected behavior The server and the frontend shipped in the same release should agree on the API route version. The v2 routes requested by the frontend should be mounted and return the documented JSON responses, or the frontend should use the routes actually exposed by the server. ## Request Please check the release/build packaging or route registration that causes the server's web frontend and API route table to be out of sync.

signals.title: Client stalls at single-core 100% CPU during long sessions with many rapid tool-calling turns — unrecoverable except via SIGINT
signals.text: Title: Client stalls at single-core 100% CPU during long sessions with many rapid tool-calling turns — unrecoverable except via SIGINT ## Summary During a long-running session involving a background job monitored via repeated short tool-calling turns, the OpenCode client stalls completely — no partial output, no tool call, nothing — for 20+ minutes. `Escape` does not cancel the stalled turn. Only killing the process from the terminal (`Ctrl+C`) recovers, requiring the session to be resumed afterward. Confirmed reproducible twice in the same day, same workflow signature. ## Environment - Provider: `github-copilot`, model: `claude-sonnet-5` - Platform: Linux (see full env details on request) - Session was long-running (~1.5h+) at the time of the stall, with substantial accumulated context (`cache.read` ~248,000 tokens by the time of the incident) ## Reproduction pattern 1. Start a long-running background job (in this case via `tmux new -d -s NAME '<command> | tee log'`). 2. Poll it repeatedly from the agent in short tool-calling turns (in this case: ~12-13 turns of `sleep 115; tmux list-sessions; cat log`, each turn ~2 minutes apart). 3. After the background job actually completes (~20-25 min in), the *next* agent turn — which should be cheap (just reading a finished log / detecting the tmux session ended) — instead stalls completely for 20+ minutes before producing any output at all. ## Evidence gathered (from `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) Querying the local SQLite session DB (`message`, `part`, `event` tables) for the stalled turn showed: - The stalled message's own `time.created` timestamp was ~23.5 minutes **before** its own first `part` (not even a `step-start` part) appeared. This rules out "a tool/bash call took a long time to execute" — the stall happened before the turn even began producing anything. - The eventual token/cost breakdown for that same message (once it finally completed) was: `input: 2, output: 426, reasoning: 0, cache.read: 247987, cache.write: 597`, `finish: "tool-calls"`. This is a **cheap**, almost entirely cache-hit request — model inference for 426 output tokens should take seconds, not 23+ minutes. - This rules out a slow/expensive model generation as the cause of the wall-clock delay. ## Key additional fact: CPU was pinned at 100% on a SINGLE core during the stall (both occurrences) This is the detail that rules out "waiting on a slow/stalled network response" (which would show near-zero CPU, blocked on I/O) and instead points to **a synchronous, non-yielding operation blocking the client's single-threaded main/event-loop**. Single-core saturation + a completely unresponsive UI (Escape doesn't register at all) is consistent with the JS/Bun main thread being busy in a tight loop or an O(n²)-or-worse computation, not legitimate parallel work and not I/O wait. `Escape` failing to cancel is consistent with this: if the main event loop is blocked synchronously, it cannot process the keypress event that would trigger a cancel action. `Ctrl+C` works because the terminal's line discipline delivers `SIGINT` to the process at the OS level, independent of whether the app's own event loop is currently responsive — the process then dies (unhandled/stuck signal → default termination), which matches needing to "resume the session" afterward rather than a graceful cancel. ## Hypothesis (unconfirmed — I don't have access to the OpenCode source to verify) Given the correlation with (a) a large accumulated context (`cache.read` ~248k tokens) and (b) many rapid successive short tool-calling turns in the same session, I suspect some client-side bookkeeping step that runs synchronously on the main thread and scales with conversation/context size (e.g. serialization, token/cache accounting, or persistence to the local SQLite DB) has worse-than-linear complexity, and becomes a multi-minute main-thread stall once a session crosses some size/turn-count threshold. I have not been able to locate the specific code path causing this. ## Request - Any pointers to where in the codebase a per-turn synchronous operation might scale with session size would help narrow this down further. - In the meantime, is there a supported way to reliably interrupt a stalled turn without killing the whole client process? (`Escape` did not work in either occurrence.) ## Diagnostic method for anyone else hitting this Query `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` directly: ```sql -- find message.time_created (turn issued) vs its parts' time_created (turn actually starts producing output) SELECT m.id, m.time_created, (SELECT MIN(p.time_created) FROM part p WHERE p.message_id = m.id) as min_part, (SELECT MAX(p.time_created) FROM part p WHERE p.message_id = m.id) as max_part FROM message m WHERE m.session_id = '<session_id>' ORDER BY m.time_created; -- pull full token/cost breakdown for a specific stalled message from the event log SELECT data FROM event WHERE aggregate_id = '<session_id>' AND type = 'message.updated.1' AND data LIKE '%<message_id>%' ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1; ``` Happy to provide the exact (anonymized) query outputs from both occurrences if useful.
signals.author: shmty

signals.title: Desktop 1.18.12: sessions spanning the 2026-08-14 message-ID wrap stop accepting messages (loop exits at step=0)
signals.text: ### OpenCode Desktop 1.18.12: sessions spanning the 2026-08-14 message-ID wrap stop accepting messages (agent loop exits at step=0) **Environment**: Windows 11 · OpenCode Desktop 1.18.12 (embedded sidecar server) · SQLite storage. ## Symptom Since `2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`, sessions whose last assistant message was created *before* that moment can no longer receive messages: - Sending a message writes the user text to the DB, but the agent loop exits immediately (`loop ... step=0` → `exiting loop` in the log) and never calls the LLM — the conversation "ends" instantly with no reply. - After reloading the session, the sent message appears out of order / missing, because the UI renders messages sorted by ID. - New sessions created after the wrap work normally, which made it look like a single broken conversation. ## Root cause (问题原因) Message/part IDs are generated by the `ascending()` helper: ```ts const current = BigInt(timestamp) * 0x1000n + BigInt(counter); // ID = 48-bit hex of (timestamp << 12 | counter) + 14 random base62 chars ``` The embedded time field is only 36 bits: `Date.now() mod 2^36`, which wraps every `2^36` ms ≈ **2.18 years**. The wrap occurred at `Date.now() = 26 × 2^36 = 1,786,706,395,136 ms = 2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`: - IDs generated just before the wrap start with `msg_ffff...` (high lexicographic value) - IDs generated just after the wrap start with `msg_0001...` (low value) In the run loop the "nothing to do" check is roughly: ```ts if (lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasPendingToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id) { log("exiting loop"); break; } ``` For an affected session, the pre-wrap assistant message (`msg_ffff...`) sorts *after* the freshly sent user message (`msg_0001...`), so `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` evaluates true and the loop concludes the newest message was already answered — it never runs. ## Reproduction 1. In a session, exchange at least one assistant reply before `2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`. 2. After that time, send a new message in that same session. 3. Observed: the message row is persisted, the loop logs `step=0` then `exiting loop`, no assistant reply is produced, and the rendered order is broken after refresh. This affects (a) sessions with messages on both sides of the wrap, and (b) sessions whose last message is a pre-wrap assistant reply when the user sends after the wrap. Any long-lived session will hit it again at the next wrap. ## Workaround applied (解决办法) Because restarting/updating cannot fix the stored ordering, I rewrote the affected sessions' message/part IDs in SQLite to a monotonic scheme (backup taken via `VACUUM INTO` first, IDs regenerated in `time_created` order, `parentID`/JSON references and event data remapped, foreign keys verified). After that, the loop proceeds normally again. ## Suggested fix - Stop encoding the time modulo 2^36 — use a full-width timestamp (or a wider ID), so IDs stay monotonic across the wrap boundary; and/or - Make the loop-completion check and UI ordering compare `time_created` (with ID only as a tiebreaker) instead of lexicographic ID order. --- *This issue was automatically created by an AI assistant on behalf of a user (auto-generated report: root cause analysis, workaround, and suggested fix were compiled by the assistant; reproduction steps verified against the local database).*
signals.author: 11inyuan

signals.title: OpenAI WebSocket 1009 retries the same oversized response.create five times before HTTP fallback
signals.text: ### Description With the OpenAI Responses WebSocket enabled, an oversized request containing base64 image tool outputs is deterministically rejected with: ``` ProviderResponseStreamError: WebSocket closed before response.completed (code 1009: message too big) ``` OpenCode retries the same oversized WebSocket request five times with backoff before falling back to HTTP. The session therefore appears stuck for about a minute and repeats a request that cannot succeed over that transport. Cancelling or restarting before fallback starts the cycle again. The session eventually recovered over HTTP and then compacted, so this report is about delayed recovery and unnecessary retries, not permanent data loss. In the observed session, one tool round read six 1920x1080 PNG files. Their base64 data URLs totaled 17,390,364 bytes. Including an image from the immediately preceding round, the request history contained 19,895,594 bytes of image data before JSON overhead. The next model request produced five consecutive code 1009 failures. In v1.18.18, the complete `response.create` payload is sent as one WebSocket message: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.18/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts#L289-L295 Code 1009 is currently only annotated as `message too big`: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.18/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts#L350-L354 Expected behavior: code 1009 should immediately bypass WebSocket and retry once over HTTP, or OpenCode should preflight the serialized payload size and use HTTP for oversized requests. It should not replay the same known-too-large WebSocket message five times. Related issues: - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/14562 covers the same base64-image root cause through HTTP 413 and compaction, but not WebSocket code 1009 or delayed HTTP fallback. - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29646 covers generic early WebSocket disconnects (for example transient code 1006). Code 1009 is deterministic and should trigger immediate transport fallback. ### Plugins `telegram-notify.js` (not involved in request construction) ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start OpenCode with `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WEBSOCKETS=true`. 2. Use the OpenAI provider with `gpt-5.6-sol`. 3. In one tool round, read enough PNG images for the base64 tool-result attachments to exceed the WebSocket message-size limit (six 1920x1080 PNGs totaling about 17.4 MB reproduced it here). 4. Continue the turn so OpenCode sends the next `response.create`. 5. Observe five consecutive code 1009 errors before HTTP fallback succeeds. ### Screenshot and/or share link No public share link. The raw error and measured payload sizes are included above. ### Operating System Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 host; Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2) ### Terminal PowerShell 7 launcher; headless `opencode serve` running in WSL2

signals.title: [FEATURE]: allow user to inject custom instruction when compacting a session
signals.text:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Problem When a session is compacted, the LLM generates a structured summary of the conversation. However, the user has no way to provide per-compaction guidance — e.g., what to prioritize in the summary, what information is no longer relevant, or what the next work focus should be. The existing `experimental.session.compacting` plugin hook can inject context into the compaction prompt, but: - It only receives `{ sessionID }` — no per-invocation dynamic input - The injected content is static (determined by plugin code), not changeable per compaction Additionally, the recent conversation that the user might use to convey such guidance is often excluded from the compaction scope (it falls into the "recent" portion that is preserved verbatim), so the compaction LLM never sees it. ## Proposal Allow the user to pass an optional `instruction` string when triggering a compaction, which gets appended to the compaction LLM prompt. ### Suggested changes 1. **API layer** — Add `instruction?: string` to `SummarizePayload` (`packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/session.ts`) 2. **Handler** — Pass `instruction` through `compactSvc.create()` → `compaction.process()` (`packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts`) 3. **Compaction prompt** — Append the user instruction to the summary prompt in `processCompaction`: ```ts if (input.instruction) { nextPrompt += `

Additional user instruction for this compaction:
${input.instruction}` } 4. TUI — When the user triggers /compact (or <leader>c), show a DialogPrompt input box (already available at packages/tui/src/ui/dialog-prompt.tsx) with a placeholder like "Optional: guide the compaction (what to prioritize, what to drop)…". The user can type a one-liner or leave it empty and press Enter to proceed. Why - Per-compaction guidance is a common pattern in agent frameworks (e.g., Claude Code's /compact with optional instructions) - The change is minimal — one field threaded through 4 layers, each just passing it along - No breaking changes — instruction is optional; existing behavior is preserved when it's absent Context - Current compaction implementation: packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts (V1 path, actively used) - V2 core compaction (packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts) does not yet support plugin hooks; this proposal should be considered for both paths - DialogPrompt component already exists and is used by other commands (e.g., session rename, provider config)

signals.title: Loop doesn't exit after finish=stop — model re-invoked with no input until the session is quit
signals.text: ### Description When the agent finishes a turn with finish=stop and no tool calls, the session should go idle. Instead the loop keeps running and re-calls the model every ~10-20s with no new user message. The UI shows "busy" the whole time while the model just returns one-line filler ("Standing by", "Ready", "Idle"). From the logs: - Normal cycles end with an exiting loop event. The stuck cycle never emits one — it runs loop step=0..28+ over ~25 minutes. - The repeating pattern is loop step=N -> process (new message) -> stream (new model call), with nothing in between. - Every filler message is finish=stop and its step-finish reason=stop, so the model is correctly signaling "done" and the loop is ignoring it. - Esc fires cancel + error=Aborted (finish=None, 0 parts), then the loop restarts at step=0 and sticks again. Esc doesn't break it; only quitting the session does. Also notable: the model's hidden reasoning in those filler turns literally says "I'm being repeatedly prompted with no user message — this is an artifact", so it's aware it's being re-called with nothing to do. Version 1.17.18, model deepseek-v4-pro (opencode-go), Linux/WSL. Reproduced in one session, then again right after resuming it. Looks related to #42363 and #22329. ### Plugins No plugins ### OpenCode version 1.17.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run opencode (v1.17.18) with deepseek-v4-pro (opencode-go). 2. Do a normal multi-turn agent task — several tool calls, some reasoning, then a finish=stop (e.g. "implement X, run the tests, commit, summarize"). 3. Let it reach a turn that ends with no tool calls. Instead of going idle, it keeps re-calling the model every ~10-20s with no new input — the UI stays "busy" and it appends one-line "Standing by" / "Ready" / "Idle" replies. 4. Press Esc: the current generation aborts, but the loop restarts at step=0 and sticks again. 5. Only quitting the session (Ctrl+C) stops it. Note: not fully deterministic — I only hit it after long sessions with a lot of reasoning/tool history, so it may depend on context length. ### Screenshot and/or share link Recreated using sql db trace by ds4 pro ### Operating System WSL on Windows 11 ### Terminal westerm

signals.title: catalog: models without declared capabilities default to image input support
signals.text: ## Summary Models without declared capabilities are defaulted to image input support (`capabilities.input: ["text", "image"]`), so text-only models on custom providers are sent image attachments, which their providers reject with HTTP 400. Plugins reading the catalog (e.g. opencode-eyesight) are also misled into treating those models as vision-capable. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-next-17444 - OS: macOS 25.5.0 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64) - Terminal: Apple_Terminal, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: next - Active plugins: `superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git`, `/Users/bankja/projects/opencode-eyesight` (local dev) ## Reproduction 1. Use a V1-format `opencode.json` with a custom provider (`npm: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, e.g. `wd` in the example below) whose model declares **no** `modalities`: ```jsonc { "provider": { "wd": { "name": "MY LOCAL AI", "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "models": { "Deepseek-V4-Flash": { "name": "Deepseek-V4-Flash", "options": { "temperature": 1.0 } } } } } } ``` 2. Start `opencode2` with a session using `wd/Deepseek-V4-Flash`. 3. Attach an image (`@`-mention a file or paste) and send the message. ## Expected Behavior The catalog should report only capabilities the model actually declares. A model with no `modalities`/`tool_call` should not be presented as image-capable, so the runner does not send image parts to it and plugins can rely on `capabilities.input`. ## Actual Behavior - `GET /api/model` reports `caps: {"tools": true, "input": ["text", "image"], "output": ["text"]}` for the model. - The session request includes the image, and the provider rejects it: `Error: Provider request failed with HTTP 400` (finish: `error`), with the error `Provider request failed with HTTP 400` surfaced on the assistant message. ## Additional Context The default comes from `Model.Info.default` in `packages/schema/src/model.ts` (`capabilities: { tools: true, input: ["text", "image"], output: ["text"] }`), which the catalog applies when creating model entries (`packages/core/src/catalog.ts`, model `update`). V1-config migration leaves `capabilities` undefined when the model declares no `tool_call`/`modalities` (`packages/core/src/v1/config/migrate.ts`), after which the default triple kicks in. Explicit declarations are honored — models with `modalities: { input: ["text", "image"] }` normalize to `tools: false` with the declared input. Consequences observed: - Runner forwards the image to a text-only model → provider HTTP 400 on every image message. - Plugins that gate on `catalog.model.list()` capabilities (e.g. opencode-eyesight's vision fallback) skip transcription and pass the image through. Workarounds: - Declare explicit `modalities` (`{ "input": ["text"], "output": ["text"] }`) on text-only models. - (Plugin-side) treat the exact default triple as "unknown" rather than image support. Suggested fix: default models without declared capabilities to text-only (`input: ["text"]`, `tools` unchanged), or leave capabilities empty instead of asserting image support that the provider may not honor.
signals.author: bankjaneo

signals.title: Bug Report: Message ID generation wraps every ~2.18 years, causing sessions to stop responding silently
signals.text: ### Description ## Summary The ID generator in `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts` only stores 48 bits of a `timestamp_ms * 0x1000 + counter` value. Because `timestamp_ms mod 2^36` is what actually survives, the "time" portion of every ID wraps every `2^36 ms` (≈ 2.18 years). After a wrap, newly generated IDs sort **before** older IDs lexicographically. For sessions that span the boundary, `MessageV2.latest()` then picks the wrong "latest" assistant message and the prompt loop (`runLoop` in `session/prompt.ts`) exits immediately without calling the model — the session silently stops producing responses. This is present in **v1.15.13** and still present on **dev** (verified `2026-08-14`, `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts` is identical). *Discovered with assistance from an AI coding tool (opencode) while debugging a session that stopped responding.* ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`: ```ts let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) now = direction === "descending" ? ~now : now const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // <-- only 48 bits stored for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } return prefix + "_" + timeBytes.toString("hex") + randomBase62(LENGTH - 12) ``` - `now = Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` needs ~53 bits, but only the low **48 bits** are kept. The stored value is effectively `(Date.now() mod 2^36) * 0x1000 + counter`. - `2^36 ms = 68,719,476,736 ms ≈ 795.4 days ≈ 2.18 years`. Whenever `Date.now()` crosses an integer multiple of `2^36`, the ID "clock" resets: IDs go from `...ffff...` back to `...0000...`. - The first wrap since 1970 that users will hit is `k = 26`, i.e. `26 * 2^36 ms ≈ 1,786,706,395,136 ms` (mid-2026). Impact on ordering and logic: 1. **`session/message-v2.ts` → `latest()`** picks the newest user/assistant by max ID string: ```ts if (info.role === "assistant" && (!assistant || info.id > assistant.id)) assistant = info ``` After the wrap, an *old* assistant message (from before the boundary, `msg_ffff…`) has a **larger** ID than a *new* user message (`msg_0003…`). 2. **`session/prompt.ts` → `runLoop()`** stops the loop when the last assistant already finished: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // <-- true after the wrap ) { /* exiting loop */ break } ``` A freshly sent user message has `id < lastAssistant.id` after the wrap, so the loop concludes "the assistant already replied" and **breaks without calling the model**. The user sees: message is saved, but nothing is generated. 3. **`Identifier.timestamp()`** also returns `(t mod 2^36)`, i.e. wrong absolute time for IDs created after the wrap. ## Symptoms - A session that was working stops responding to new messages (message is stored, but no assistant reply is produced). - Log shows the prompt loop exiting immediately without a model call: ``` INFO service=session.prompt session.id=ses_xxx step=0 loop INFO service=session.prompt session.id=ses_xxx exiting loop ``` (no `session.processor`, no `llm` lines in between) - Sessions created entirely after the wrap, or sessions whose history predates it but are not continued across the boundary, are unaffected. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.15.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create/continue a session that has messages with IDs before **and** after the boundary (`26 * 2^36 ms`; mid-2026). Any session whose last pre-boundary message ID starts with a high hex char (e.g. `msg_ffff…`) and that receives a new message after the wrap (ID `msg_0003…`) reproduces it. 2. Send any message. 3. Observe: the prompt loop logs `step=0 loop` then `exiting loop` within ~50 ms; no assistant message is ever produced. A long-running session used daily between ~2024 and 2026 reproduces this exactly once the wrap is crossed. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signals.title: Scripted-exec endpoint is authorised to every authenticated user
signals.text: `shared/scripted-exec.ts` installs a scripted REST operation that evaluates server-side script. The operation is created with six fields and no authorisation settings, so ServiceNow authenticates the caller and then permits **any** authenticated user on the instance. `GlideEvaluator.evaluateString` does not enforce ACLs, so reaching the endpoint is equivalent to admin. Three things make it worse than a normal permission gap: - The artefact is permanent. It is never removed, and it stays on production instances. - Seven tools plant it, one of them (`snow_create_ui_policy`) unconditionally on every call — so it can appear on an instance where nobody asked for script execution. - `update-set-guard.ts` exempts the `script-execution` subcategory, so there is no update set to back it out with. Because the artefact already exists on instances that ran an older version, the fix has to repair as well as prevent. **Scope of exposure known to us:** only our own PDI. Two orgs ever invoked a planting tool through the platform and both resolve to `dev380262`. Anyone running the CLI over stdio or self-hosted is not visible to us and cannot be counted.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Support keyless custom OpenAI-compatible providers
signals.text:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Allow OpenCode’s native LLM runtime to use custom `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` providers without requiring an API key.

Self-hosted inference services such as SGLang, vLLM, Ollama, and LM Studio are commonly configured as custom providers and may intentionally accept unauthenticated requests over a private network.

The native runtime currently rejects custom provider IDs and separately requires a non-empty API key. Together, these restrictions prevent valid self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints from using the native runtime.

Desired behavior:

- Accept custom `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider IDs in the native runtime.
- Allow `apiKey` to be absent.
- Send an authorization header only when a key is configured.
- Preserve existing behavior for authenticated providers.

Related issues:

- #38893 covers the native runtime’s hardcoded provider allowlist.
- #39072 covers unconditional authorization requirements for another provider.

This request covers the combined custom-provider and optional-authentication behavior needed by self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

signals.title: ID generator wraps after ~795 days, breaking chronological sorting of message IDs
signals.text: ## Summary `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts` (and the client-side replicas in OpenChamber) encodes the timestamp as `Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` into a **6-byte (48-bit) hex prefix**, which wraps around every 2^36 ms ≈ **795 days**. The latest wrap occurred on **2026-08-14 11:19:55 UTC**. After the wrap, newly created IDs sort **before** all older IDs lexicographically, silently breaking the "ascending ID = chronological order" contract that the format implies. ## Reproduction (real data) Same session, before and after the boundary: ``` msg_fffc192a8001… 2026-08-14 10:11 UTC (prefix near FFFF…) msg_0005afbc2002… 2026-08-14 12:59 UTC (prefix wrapped to 0000…) ``` String comparison orders the 12:59 messages **before** the 10:11 ones. In OpenChamber this rendered the newest messages at the **top** of any conversation that spans the boundary. ## Impact - Any code that derives chronological order from ID string comparison (the documented intent of the `ascending` IDs, and what third-party clients such as OpenChamber relied on) breaks every ~795 days. - `Identifier.timestamp(id)` in `id.ts` returns a wrong (mod-2^36-ms) value for IDs created after a wrap. - opencode's own DB queries (`message-v2.ts` uses `ORDER BY time_created, id`) are unaffected, but the *sortable-ID contract* exposed to clients is broken. - Note this also affects the **same-millisecond counter**: `lastTimestamp`/`counter` are process-global, and client-generated IDs (OpenChamber's optimistic inserts replicate this format) collide in ordering with server IDs generated in the same millisecond. ## Client-side workaround (already shipped) OpenChamber fixed the display-side impact by ordering messages on `time.created` instead of raw IDs: commit `53830952` on `openchamber/openchamber@main` ("fix(chat): keep messages chronological across ID rollover"). That only masks the root cause — the ID generator itself still wraps. ## Suggested fixes 1. **Encode 7 bytes (56 bits) instead of 6** — pushes the wrap to ~3.4M years while keeping a compact ID. 8 bytes (64 bits) is also fine. 2. If the format cannot change, **document the ~795-day wrap** and recommend clients order by `time.created` (already present on every message) rather than by ID. 3. Keep in mind old IDs with the 12-hex prefix will remain in existing stores — a format change alone doesn't reorder existing data, so clients should still prefer time-based ordering.

signals.title: "Snapshot mechanism stalls on large workspaces: ~1min per git snapshot, permanent index.lock deadlock after a crash"
signals.text: ### Description On a large git workspace (~5,300 tracked files) running opencode 1.18.18 on Windows, the **project snapshot mechanism** becomes pathological: 1. Every agentic iteration triggers a full `git add -A` + `git commit` inside a custom snapshot repository. On a large workspace each of these takes **~1 minute** (`git add -A` ≈ 57s, `git commit` ≈ 19s measured locally), so **every single model interaction is blocked for ~1 minute before anything is sent**. 2. When a snapshot git process crashes (or is killed), it leaves a stale `index.lock` in the snapshot repository. From then on, **every snapshot operation fails with `fatal: Unable to create '...index.lock': File exists`** and opencode retries indefinitely — memory balloons to 6–8 GB, disk reads exceed 10 GB, and no response is ever produced. The only fix is to manually delete the `index.lock` file. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a large repo (several thousand tracked files) in opencode on Windows. 2. Verify the snapshot git repo under `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<projectID>/...`: - Run `git add -A` in that repo → observe tens of seconds. - Run `git commit` → same. 3. Trigger a snapshot operation and then kill the opencode process mid-operation → a stale `index.lock` is left behind. 4. Restart opencode in the same directory → every interaction now logs: ``` WARN level=WARN message="failed to add snapshot files" exitCode=128 stderr="fatal: Unable to create '.../snapshot/.../index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to be running in this repository..." ``` The session becomes unresponsive: ~6–8 GB RSS, continually increasing disk reads, and no answer is returned, because snapshot never succeeds and opencode retries forever. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System windows ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: 48-bit ID timestamp wraparound on 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC wedges all pre-existing sessions (loop exits at step 0, prompts silently ignored)
signals.text: ### Description **All sessions created before `2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC` silently stop processing prompts** due to a 48-bit timestamp wraparound in the ID generator (`packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`). This is likely the root cause behind #42605 and a spike of "agent stops responding in an existing session" reports starting today. #### Root cause `Identifier.create()` encodes `Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` into **6 bytes** (48 bits): ```ts let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // ← only the low 48 bits survive for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } ``` `Date.now() * 4096` is a ~53-bit number, so the sortable prefix wraps every `2^36 ms ≈ 2.18 years`. The most recent wrap boundary was: ``` 1786706395136 ms = 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC ``` Before the boundary, ascending IDs were near the top of the range (`msg_ffd4…`); after it they restart near zero (`msg_000b…`). Any new user message in a pre-existing session now **sorts before the entire session history**. The v2 session loop, which picks up work by ID ordering, sees nothing new past its watermark and exits immediately: ``` level=INFO message=loop session.id=ses_… step=0 level=INFO message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_… ``` No provider call is ever made; the message is stored but never processed. Retrying, switching models, and `/summarize` all fail the same way. Sessions created entirely after the boundary work fine (all IDs post-wrap, internally consistent). #### Evidence (from two independent production sessions, v1.18.4) Session A — last processed message vs. newly posted prompts: ``` last assistant msg (Aug 13): msg_ffd4c8ecc001nKKJtMDUGfajRL new user msg (Aug 14): msg_000bcb6970013Jm92xkWhlZiOA ← sorts before all history ``` Verification of the encoding: the new message was created at `1786718762656 ms`; `1786718762656 − 1786706395136 = 12,367,520 = 0xBCB6A0` → matches the observed `000bcb6…` prefix exactly. Session B — same split within one session: ``` first msg (Aug 13): msg_ffb02725b001iqapSOS18lP6Rb new msgs (Aug 14): msg_0007f07f9001…, msg_000e4a4c2001…, msg_000ebffe9001… ``` Newest row in the `message` table is a `user` message with no assistant response; every prompt produces the step-0 loop exit above. Also note `Identifier.timestamp()` in the same file decodes post-wrap IDs to garbage (it assumes the full timestamp survived), so anything deriving times from IDs is silently wrong after the boundary too. #### Impact - Every session with history from before 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC is permanently wedged on current releases (reproduced on 1.18.4; #42605 reports 1.18.1). `id.ts` is unchanged at current HEAD, so the bug is still live. - Next wrap: ~October 2028, when it will happen again for all then-active sessions. #### Suggested fixes 1. Widen the encoded value (8 bytes removes the problem for ~570 years), with a migration/compat story for existing IDs, or 2. Seed the generator / the loop watermark from `max(message.id)` per session at instance init, so new IDs always sort after existing ones, and 3. Short term: detect the condition (new user message ID < session max ID) and either re-key the message or surface an explicit error instead of silently ignoring the prompt. ### OpenCode version 1.18.4 (also reproduced indirectly on 1.18.1 via #42605); `id.ts` unchanged at HEAD as of 2026-08-14. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Take any session with messages created before 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC. 2. Send a new prompt. 3. Observe: message row is written, log shows `loop step=0` → `exiting loop`, no model call, no response. (Equivalent synthetic repro: create a session, insert a message with an ID in the `ff…` range, then prompt normally.) ### Operating System Linux (server mode, headless); also reported on Windows 11 Desktop (#42605).

signals.title: OpenChamber transcript hides new messages in sessions created before 1.18.16
signals.text: ### Description Environment: opencode 1.18.16 (upgraded from 1.18.15), OpenChamber 1.18.3 web UI (Home Assistant add-on). Symptom: In sessions that existed before the 1.18.16 upgrade, new messages no longer appear at the end of the transcript. The transcript appears to end at the last pre-upgrade message; new questions/answers are effectively invisible. Sessions created after the upgrade work fine. Data is intact — GET /session/{id}/message returns every message including the newest, so this is a client-side ordering problem, not data loss. Root cause (confirmed against real data): opencode's message-ID generation changed in 1.18.16. Through 1.18.15 IDs were a monotonic sequence (msg_f7… → msg_ff…) so string order equalled chronological order. Starting 1.18.16 new IDs are msg_00…-prefixed. OpenChamber's transcript store sorts and merges messages by message-ID string comparison (the J6/Q6 comparators and gb/nL/eL/tL/X6 helpers in the web bundle), with eL/tL doing binary-search insertion keyed on ID. For any session containing both ID namespaces, string order is 00… < f7… < ff…, so new messages sort to the top of the transcript and the visible "end" stays at the last pre-upgrade message. Example: a 314-message session spanning the upgrade — the actual newest message (created the day after the upgrade) sorts to index 50 of 314, and the bottom of the transcript shows content from the day before. Suggested fix: order transcript messages by time.created (falling back to ID for ties) instead of message-ID string order, or keep message IDs monotonic/backward-compatible across releases so ID order remains chronological. ### Plugins Home Assistant add-on ### OpenCode version 1.18.16 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System HAOS ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: [BUG] OpenAI Responses: assistant messages sent as {role:"assistant", content:[{type:"output_text"}]} rejected by strict OpenAI-compatible servers
signals.text: ## Summary When a conversation history contains an assistant text message and opencode sends it to an OpenAI Responses (`/responses`) endpoint, the request body uses: ```json {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]} ``` This shape is **not valid** per OpenAI's Responses input schema. Real `api.openai.com` tolerates it, but strict OpenAI-compatible servers that validate with the official OpenAI SDK types (e.g. a self-hosted Qwen server exposing `/v1/responses`) reject it with a 422/400 validation error, so switching a session to such a model fails. ## Environment - opencode 1.18.18 (Snap, stable) - Default runtime (AI SDK path), `@ai-sdk/openai` 3.0.84 - Server: self-hosted OpenAI-compatible `/v1/responses` endpoint (validates with `openai` Python SDK pydantic types) ## Repro 1. Configure a custom provider/model pointing at an OpenAI-compatible `/responses` server. 2. Switch an existing session to that model so the history (including prior assistant text) is resent. 3. The request fails with a pydantic `ValidationError` on the `input` array, e.g.: ``` loc: ('body', 'input', 'list[union[EasyInputMessageParam, Message, ResponseOutputMessageParam, ...]]', 2, 'ResponseFunctionToolCallParam', 'call_id') msg: 'Field required' input: {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'output_text', 'text': '...'}]} ``` ## Root cause `@ai-sdk/openai` builds assistant input items as `{ role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "output_text", text }], id }` (`convertToOpenAIResponsesMessages`, dist/index.js ~3127). Per the official OpenAI schema (`openai-python` types): - `EasyInputMessageParam` allows `role: "assistant"` but `content` must be `str | list[input_text | input_image | input_file]` — `output_text` is **not** a valid easy-input content part. - `output_text` is only valid inside a full output item `{ type: "message", role: "assistant", id, status, content: [...] }` (`ResponseOutputMessageParam`, where `type`/`id`/`status` are required). OpenAI's own API is lenient and accepts the non-conformant shape, which is why this has gone unnoticed. The same bug also exists in the native llm protocol (`packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-responses.ts`, `lowerMessages`). ## Proposed fix Emit assistant text as an easy-input message with `input_text` parts: ```json {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "..."}]} ``` or, when an item id is available, the complete `{"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "id", "status": "completed", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]}`. A local fix for the native protocol is ready and tests pass (59 tests, `packages/llm`). The AI SDK path will additionally need a fix in `vercel/ai` (or a bumped `@ai-sdk/openai`) to fix the released builds.
signals.author: j34ni

signals.title: [BUG] Zen Go Anthropic endpoint: tools requests fail for all GLM models ([1210] / 422 'web_search' translation error)
signals.text: ## Description On the OpenCode Zen **Go** Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages`), **any request with a non-empty `tools` array fails for all GLM models** (glm-5.3, glm-5.2, glm-5.1). The same request without `tools`, or with the same `tools` against other models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus), succeeds — so this looks like a broken Anthropic→GLM tools translation in the Console Go gateway, not a client or account issue. This effectively makes GLM models unusable from Claude Code, which always sends `tools`. ## Environment - Endpoint: `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages` (Anthropic-compatible, Go plan) - Client: plain `curl` (reproduces without any client), and Claude Code - Reproduced with **3 independent Go plan API keys** (3 separate workspaces) — identical errors, so account-independent - Date: 2026-08-15 ## Repro 1 — glm-5.3 + one minimal tool → `[1210]` ```bash curl -X POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: <REDACTED>" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "glm-5.3", "max_tokens": 2048, "tools": [{ "name": "get_weather", "description": "query weather", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"] } }], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "What is the weather in Beijing? Please call the tool."}]}] }' ``` Response: ```json {"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [1210] Invalid API parameter, please check the documentation."}} ``` Notes: - `"tools": []` (empty array) → 200 OK, so it's specifically non-empty `tools`. - Fails regardless of tool shape (with/without `description`, with extra `type` field, complex schemas). ## Repro 2 — glm-5.2 / glm-5.1 + same tool → 422 with revealing param path ```json {"error":{"param":"tools.0.function-after[_domain_filters(), WebSearchTool].type","type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] Input should be 'web_search'"}} ``` The mangled param path `tools.0.function-after[_domain_filters(), WebSearchTool].type` suggests the gateway is translating ordinary Anthropic function tools into Zhipu's **web_search tool format** before forwarding upstream. ## Control experiments (why I believe it's a gateway translation bug) | Request | Result | |---|---| | glm-5.3, no `tools` → `/zen/go/v1/messages` | ✅ 200 | | glm-5.3, 1 minimal tool → `/zen/go/v1/messages` | ❌ `[1210]` | | glm-5.2 / glm-5.1, same tool → same endpoint | ❌ 422 `Input should be 'web_search'` | | **kimi-k3**, same tool → same endpoint | ✅ 200, clean `tool_use` block | | **qwen3.7-plus**, same tool → same endpoint | ✅ 200, clean `tool_use` block | | glm-5.3, same tool → `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (**OpenAI** endpoint) | ✅ 200, correct `tool_calls` with parsed arguments | | glm-5.2, same tool → **Zhipu native** `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/anthropic/v1/messages` | ✅ 200, clean `tool_use` block | So: the GLM models themselves handle tools fine (OpenAI endpoint + Zhipu native Anthropic endpoint both work), the Zen Anthropic endpoint's tool translation works fine for other vendors (kimi/qwen) — the failure is specific to the Anthropic→GLM tools translation path in the Console Go gateway. ## Expected behavior `tools` on the Anthropic-compatible endpoint should work for GLM models the same way it does for kimi-k3 / qwen3.7-plus on the same endpoint, and for glm-5.3 on the OpenAI endpoint. ## Additional notes - glm-5.3 appears to be newly added to the model list (around 2026-08-14). - Side observation: on Zhipu's native Anthropic endpoint, requesting `glm-5.2` now returns `"model": "glm-5.3"` in the response — the alias seems to have been repointed upstream. Not sure if that's related to the routing difference between the `[1210]` (glm-5.3) and 422 (glm-5.2/5.1) errors.

signals.title: SIGUSR2 theme reload interrupts an in-flight session
signals.text: ### Description Changing the desktop theme while opencode is working interrupts the run. Omarchy signals opencode on every theme change — `omarchy-restart-opencode` runs `killall -SIGUSR2 opencode`. In the TUI, SIGUSR2 calls the worker's `reload` RPC (`packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:216`), and that reload invalidates config and then disposes every instance (`packages/opencode/src/cli/tui/worker.ts:63`). Disposing an instance cancels the session runners it owns, so whatever is in flight — a model stream or a shell command — is aborted. The theme itself does not depend on that reload: the TUI re-detects the terminal palette and re-scans theme files from its own SIGUSR2 handler in `packages/tui/src/context/theme.tsx`. ### OpenCode version 1.18.18, also reproduced on dev @ e23586af2 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start the TUI. 2. Start something long-running, e.g. `!sleep 45`. 3. From another terminal, `kill -SIGUSR2 <tui pid>` (this is what an Omarchy theme switch does). 4. The run is aborted immediately with "User aborted the command", and the log shows `disposing all instances` within milliseconds of the signal. ### Operating System Arch Linux (Omarchy), Hyprland ### Terminal foot

signals.title: [BUG] Bash tool subprocess killed with SIGKILL when stdout streams many small writes (e.g. pytest tests/)
signals.text: ## Title [BUG] Bash tool subprocess killed with SIGKILL when stdout streams many small writes (e.g. `pytest tests/`) ## Body ### Environment - OpenCode CLI, version from 2026 - Running inside WSL (Ubuntu 24.04) on Windows 11 - Default provider config (model details irrelevant) - Memory: 19 GB total, 17 GB free at time of failure (NOT an OOM) - Disk: 946 GB free (NOT a disk-full) ### Observed behavior When the bash tool (or any sub-agent invocation that uses bash) runs a command that emits **many small writes to stdout in rapid succession**, the subprocess is killed with exit code 9 (SIGKILL). The parent OpenCode process and the user session remain alive. ### Reproduction In a Python project with pytest tests: ```bash # DOES reproduce (kills with SIGKILL, exit code 9): pytest tests/ -m "not integration" pytest tests/infrastructure/test_foo.py # Does NOT reproduce (succeeds normally): echo "hello" for i in $(seq 1 30); do echo "line $i"; done pytest tests/ --collect-only -q pytest tests/infrastructure/test_fastapi_app.py # 23 tests, single file ``` ### Hypothesis The trigger is the **streaming write pattern**, not the output size or the command. Pytest emits one write per test (a "." or "F" character) plus a carriage-return progress bar. Other commands that emit a single large write at the end (echo, `--collect-only`) or fewer writes survive. ### Attempts to work around (all failed) - `-q` flag (quiet mode) - `--tb=line --no-header --no-summary` - `-p no:cacheprovider` - `python3 -u` (forced unbuffered — made it worse if anything) - Different providers/models in `opencode.json` - Different MCP server configuration ### Related upstream issues - #40439 — TUI sessions hang permanently: zombie git child under project-copy-refresh snapshot step - #35241 — fix(shell): three timeouts and an exit fallback for the bash tool hang class - #28780 — fix(shell): add timeout guards for pre-spawn pipeline and post-SIGKILL cleanup - #24077 — opencode (default mode) closes entire terminal window on Linux / i3wm The pattern matches #35241's "bash tool hang class" most closely. ### Impact Blocks any verification that requires running a full test suite through the bash tool. Workarounds: split tests into many small pytest invocations, or run verification outside of OpenCode entirely.

signals.title: Desktop: remote server on Windows cannot correctly load/use projects and sessions from macOS client
signals.text: ### Description OpenCode Desktop can connect successfully to an `opencode serve` instance running on a Windows workstation from a macOS Desktop client, but the remote projects/sessions are not usable from the macOS client. The underlying API works correctly: the Mac can retrieve the Windows server's sessions and projects, and the Desktop connection is shown as green. However, the Desktop UI does not correctly load/use those remote projects and sessions. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 in both machines ### Steps to reproduce ## Environment - OpenCode Desktop: 1.18.18 - Server: Windows 11 - Client: macOS - Server: `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` - Connection: SSH tunnel - Windows Desktop can use the server normally ## Reproduction 1. Run `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` on Windows. 2. Connect Windows OpenCode Desktop to `127.0.0.1:4096`. 3. Create/use sessions and projects on that server. 4. Expose port 4096 to a Mac through an SSH tunnel. 5. Connect macOS OpenCode Desktop to `127.0.0.1:4096`. 6. The connection is shown as green. 7. From the Mac, verify that the server contains the sessions: curl http://127.0.0.1:4096/session 8. The Desktop UI, however, does not correctly populate/use the remote projects/sessions. Opening a new session (in the client) gets stuck, it doesn't produce any error, simply it doesn't respond. New sessions in the host don't show up either. The same server works correctly from Windows Desktop. From macOS, /session returns the Windows sessions successfully, demonstrating that this is not a networking or server-state problem. Related issues: #19348 #29766 #25264 ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 and MacOS 26.5.2 ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: TUI system theme never refreshes terminal palette without a ?997 report (stale inside herdr)
signals.text: ### Description When OpenCode's TUI runs inside a terminal multiplexer that caches and replays the host terminal's color scheme (herdr), the `system` theme never re-detects the palette when the host appearance changes. The palette is only refreshed on a `\e[?997` color-scheme report or SIGUSR2; there is no re-query on window focus or any manual refresh command. Reproduced: with `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` set to `{"theme": "system"}` inside herdr on macOS: 1. Host terminal dark → OpenCode `system` theme renders dark. 2. Host terminal switched to a light profile, Terminal window refocused. 3. OpenCode `system` theme stays dark indefinitely; no `?997` report arrives from the host (Terminal.app doesn't emit one) and nothing triggers a re-query. The relevant code only refreshes on `CliRenderEvents.THEME_MODE` / the `?997` handler / SIGUSR2 (`packages/tui/src/context/theme.tsx` `resolveSystemTheme`/`refreshSystemTheme`, plus `renderer.getPalette` in `packages/core/src/renderer.ts`). ### Plugins None relevant. Running as `opencode` TUI inside herdr. ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. `tui.json`: `{ "theme": "system" }`. 2. Run `opencode` inside a herdr pane with a dark host terminal; confirm dark `system` theme. 3. Switch the host terminal to a light profile and refocus the window. 4. Observe the `system` theme stays dark; it never refreshes. ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS 26.5.2 ### Terminal Terminal.app, inside herdr 0.8.0

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Native Model Fallback / Failover Support
signals.text: ## Problem OpenCode supports: - Provider fallback **only** when the model ID is the same - Static agent-level model overrides There is **no way to define fallback between different models**, e.g.: > “If model A errors or rate-limits → automatically retry with model B” This causes long-running agent workflows to fail on transient provider/model issues and forces users to rely on external routers or proxies (like litellm). --- ## Request Add **first-class model fallback support** to OpenCode. ### Example (global) ```jsonc { "models": { "coder": { "fallback": [ "anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet", "openai/gpt-4o", "deepseek/deepseek-r1" ] } } } ``` ### Example (agent-level) ```jsonc { "agents": { "build": { "model": { "fallback": ["claude-sonnet", "gpt-4o-mini"] } } } } ``` --- ## Behavior - Switch models on: rate limits, provider/model unavailability, 5xx errors - Do not retry on prompt or validation errors - Optional retry limit --- ## Why in Core - Model routing is an orchestration concern - External routers break plugin auth flows and agent semantics - Complements existing provider-order routing (e.g. #2153) --- ## Status - No existing plugin or PR implements true model fallback Thanks,

signals.title: Don't Automatically Scroll Chat Window
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request It's very frustating to never be able to comfortably and fully read what the agent is generating until after they're completely finished, which can take many minutes in some cases. This wastes a lot of the user's time by forcing the user to wait for long periods of time until the agent has finished generating their entire response. Collectively during a given day, this can waste an hour or more of our time. For example, I tell the agent to perform a task. The agent starts working. The task might be a complex, multi-step implementation plan that takes 10 minutes or more. During that period, I'm constantly trying to fight against the auto-scroll behavior of the OC window to read what the agent is doing. In this context, "fight against the auto-scroll" means this: Start reading new agent output, then agent generates more output, window scrolls automatically to latest agent output, now I need to scroll back up and find my previous place in the chat stream, agent generates more output and window scrolls even farther away from where I was previously reading, now I need to scroll back up even farther again, etc....... This is very frustrating because agents often do stupid or undesirable things, but if I can't read and observe what they are doing quickly, there's no opportunity to stop them and give them corrective guidance. This also wastes a huge amount of time during a day because I can't prevent the agents from making time-wasting mistakes and going off on rabbit trails that would be much easier to prevent or correct if I could simply read and observe their output sooner. So there should be a way to disable the auto-scroll behavior so that the user can read what the agents are generating sooner.

signals.title: Feature Request: Add HTTP Streamable transport support for remote MCP servers
signals.text: ## Summary The current `type: "remote"` MCP configuration only supports **SSE (Server-Sent Events)** transport. However, the MCP protocol now includes **HTTP Streamable** transport (also called `http` or `streamable-http`), which is used by several major MCP servers including Sanity. ## Problem When configuring Sanity's hosted MCP server: ```json { "mcp": { "sanity": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.sanity.io", "oauth": {} } } } ``` OpenCode fails with: ``` SSE error: Non-200 status code (405) ``` This is because Sanity uses HTTP Streamable transport, not SSE. The 405 "Method Not Allowed" occurs because OpenCode sends a GET request expecting SSE, but Sanity expects POST requests for HTTP streaming. ## Current Workaround Using `mcp-remote` as a local proxy: ```json { "mcp": { "sanity": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.sanity.io", "--transport", "http-only"], "timeout": 60000 } } } ``` This works but adds unnecessary overhead and complexity. ## Proposed Solution Add native support for HTTP Streamable transport in remote MCP configuration: ```json { "mcp": { "sanity": { "type": "remote", "transport": "http", // or "streamable-http" "url": "https://mcp.sanity.io", "oauth": {} } } } ``` Or alternatively, a new type: ```json { "mcp": { "sanity": { "type": "http", // new type alongside "remote" (SSE) and "local" "url": "https://mcp.sanity.io", "oauth": {} } } } ``` ## Reference Other MCP clients already support this: - **Claude Code**: `claude mcp add -t http sanity https://mcp.sanity.io` - **Cursor**: `{ "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.sanity.io" }` - **VS Code**: `{ "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.sanity.io" }` See: https://www.sanity.io/docs/compute-and-ai/mcp-server ## Environment - OpenCode version: 1.1.14 - macOS version: 15.7.4 - Affected MCP server: Sanity (https://mcp.sanity.io)

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Hot-reload agents, skills and commands.
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Allow configs to be invalidated and reloaded while OC is running. This not only enables the users to create new agents/skills/commands and instantly use them, but it also allows the agents themselves to develop these skills or create new agents on the fly and instantly use them (Ralph Loops, anyone?). Proposal: - Watch instance + config directories when hot-reload is enabled. - When agent/, skill/, or command/ markdown changes: invalidate cached state and reload immediately. - When custom tool .ts/.js changes: re-import with cache busting. (I believe this is a side effect that can be removed) - Emit config.updated, skill.updated, command.updated so TUI/Desktop refresh live. Is it safe? Not necessarily, and is not for everyone. I have a functioning version of it, that is locked behind EXPERIMENTAL_HOT_RELOAD flag. Kept changes to minimum and preserved everything from upstream. https://github.com/IgorWarzocha/opencode/tree/agent-skills-commands-hot-reloading It works, but there are some caveats - agents would need a create skill/command/agent tool for creating a markdown files that pass the parsing check (if it fails, nothing happens). This is probably the easiest implementation - let agent do the thing, and as a return of the tool call, give it a path to the file and ask it to expand the instructions set and leave the frontmatter alone. Toast on reload would be a nice addition, but I'm not doing either until I know if there's actually a demand for this.

signals.title: feat(opencode): add Kiro provider
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #9165, #26680 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [X] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds Kiro (AWS) as a provider to opencode through bundled plugin ([opencode-kiro](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-kiro)). It uses the AI SDK compatible package [kiro-acp-ai-provider](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kiro-acp-ai-provider) which communicates with Kiro ACP. Auth plugin checks for an existing kiro-cli auth token. If not authenticated it launches kiro-cli login and polls until auth completes. Supports whatever authentication kiro-cli supports (Builder ID, IAM Identity Center, API keys, etc). Cost display: Kiro is credit-based so the standard $0.00 cost display doesn't apply. The plugin includes a modification to the TUI to show the current session's credit usage. This cost will be shown alonside $ cost if Kiro and a $ cost based provider are used in the same session. Models are in a separate [models.dev PR](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/2559) **Wiring into existing code:** - `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts`: one import (`import { KiroAuthPlugin } from "opencode-kiro/server"`) and one entry added to the `internalPlugins()` array. - `packages/opencode/package.json`: one dependency line, `"opencode-kiro": "0.3.6"`. - `bunfig.toml`: `opencode-kiro` and `kiro-acp-ai-provider` added to `minimumReleaseAgeExcludes`. Reason: these packages were freshly published, so they have not yet cleared the configured minimum release-age window; the exclude lets the pinned versions install. This mirrors the existing entries for `opencode-gitlab-auth` and others. - `bun.lock`: regenerated to record the new dependency tree (adds `opencode-kiro@0.3.6` and its dependency `kiro-acp-ai-provider@2.1.2`). The bundled internal plugin is server-side only (no TUI). It contributes a `provider: "kiro"` auth hook with OAuth via the official `kiro-cli login`, plus a `provider.models` hook that adds reasoning-effort variants (see Reasoning effort below). The ACP protocol details are fully encapsulated in `kiro-acp-ai-provider@2.1.2` (a dependency of `opencode-kiro`), so opencode core never deals with ACP directly. `opencode-kiro` pins its only runtime dependency (`kiro-acp-ai-provider`) to an exact version rather than a range, so the bundled dependency tree is fully determined and not subject to drift. ### Auth flow, and the credits-sidebar consent prompt The bundled auth plugin shows a consent prompt during sign-in, and on approval it writes a TUI config file in the user's home config directory. When a user runs the `/connect` flow for Kiro, the plugin declares a Yes/No `select` via opencode's standard auth-method `prompts` contract: > Enable the Kiro credits sidebar? [Yes / No] - If the user picks Yes, the plugin writes the global `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/tui.json` when that is set), merging only `"plugin": ["opencode-kiro"]` into it. The write is idempotent and non-destructive, and a write failure never fails auth. - The credits sidebar is appended as its own box; it does not disable or replace the native context box. - If the user picks No, nothing is written and login still succeeds. This config is what enables the opt-in credits sidebar described below. It is separate from the `opencode plugin opencode-kiro` installer path, which is opencode-core functionality that patches the `plugin` arrays of `.opencode/opencode.json` and `.opencode/tui.json`. ### Reasoning effort Models that expose an effort setting (Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 4.6) get selectable effort levels through opencode's variant toggle (ctrl+t). The plugin's `provider.models` hook maps each model's supported levels to opencode variants, and `kiro-acp-ai-provider` applies the chosen level through kiro-cli. minimax m2.5/m2.1 stream reasoning with no selectable effort. **Why not reuse PRs #9164 / #18408:** - Neither is compliant with the current [Kiro T&C](https://kiro.dev/faq/#with-which-tools-can-i-use-my-kiro-subscription). ### How did you verify your code works? - End-to-end tested using multiple kiro models : chat streaming, tool calling (bash, file ops), tool result round-trips, multi-turn conversations, compaction, revert, fork, subagent isolation. - Credit display verified in TUI. - The opencode-kiro kiro-acp-ai-provider tests suites passing independently ### Screenshots / recordings ### Checklist - [X] I have tested my changes locally - [X] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR
