signal.title: fix(tui): prioritize composer keybinds
signal.text: ## What Replace the Shell tab's hard-coded `Ctrl+D` interceptor with OpenTUI keymap layer priority for the full composer. Closes #42377. ## Before / After **Before:** #42366 restored the default Shell kill shortcut with a raw event interceptor that recognized only literal `Ctrl+D`. Custom bindings and the adjacent composer navigation/Subagents layers still depended on equal-priority registration order against focused-editor bindings. **After:** Composer navigation and active tab actions use contextual priority. Their configured bindings win while the composer is active, including custom bindings, without matching physical keys manually. ## How - Give the composer navigation layer contextual `priority: 1`. - Give Shell and Subagents action layers the same priority. - Remove the Shell-specific raw event interceptor. - Extend the composer keymap test to exercise tab navigation and a custom Shell kill binding while a textarea remains focused. ## Investigation Focused rendered-component tests showed permission rejection, textual forms, autocomplete destructive actions, and ordinary non-default editor collisions already behave correctly. Lowering `app.exit` priority did not fix the real TUI. Applying priority to the active composer layers did. ## Testing - `bun run test test/cli/tui/composer-keymap.test.tsx` from `packages/tui`: 3 passed - `bun typecheck` from `packages/tui`: passed - Push hook repository typecheck: 34 packages passed - Live PTY with `termctrl` against the elected service: opened composer, switched Subagents → Shell, pressed `Ctrl+D`, observed the shell disappear, and confirmed its ID was absent from `/api/shell` ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Key[Configured keypress] --> Mode{Composer active?} Mode -- no --> Editor[Normal global/editor binding] Mode -- yes --> Priority[Priority 1 composer layer] Priority --> Action[Navigation or active-tab action] ```

signal.title: feat(opencode): native OpenAI and Anthropic passthroughs for Cloudflare AI Gateway
signal.text: ## Summary Cloudflare AI Gateway models currently all ride the unified OpenAI-compatible \`/compat\` endpoint. That breaks new OpenAI models (gpt-5.5+/pro reject \`tools\` + \`reasoning_effort\` on chat completions and require the Responses API) and squeezes Claude through an OpenAI-shaped body (no native thinking blocks, no \`cache_control\`, reasoning efforts silently dropped or mistranslated). This PR routes gateway models through the provider-native passthroughs that \`ai-gateway-provider\` 3.2 ships: - \`openai/*\` → native OpenAI passthrough on the **Responses API** - \`anthropic/*\` → native Anthropic passthrough on the **Messages API** - everything else → unified \`/compat\`, unchanged The passthrough wrappers inject a \`CF_TEMP_TOKEN\` sentinel the gateway strips before dispatch, so upstream billing stays on the gateway (Unified Billing / stored BYOK) and the Cloudflare token never reaches a third-party provider. ## Changes - **\`provider.ts\` loader**: prefix routing in \`getModel\`; keeps the Workers AI token scoping (the Cloudflare token is only forwarded upstream for \`workers-ai/\` and \`@cf/\` models — includes #33597, co-authored) - **\`provider.ts\` \`cloudflareGatewayNpm\`**: resolves the native npm (\`@ai-sdk/openai\` / \`@ai-sdk/anthropic\`) **before** variants are computed, so reasoning variants produce payloads the native SDKs understand — Claude effort variants become \`thinking\` + \`output_config.effort\` (previously silently dropped), OpenAI variants gain \`reasoningSummary\` + encrypted reasoning includes for stateless multi-turn - **\`plugin/cloudflare.ts\`**: removed the \`chat.params\` maxOutputTokens workaround — it existed because compat couldn't rename \`max_tokens\` for OpenAI reasoning models; the Responses API accepts \`max_output_tokens\`, so the hack now just uncapped output - **Tests**: e2e suite asserts the envelope per route (provider + endpoint + wire payload), reasoning-effort fidelity on all three routes, and the token-scoping invariants (\`authorization\`/\`x-api-key\` stripped on passthroughs, secret never in the body, Workers AI still receives the token) ## Live verification Tested against a real gateway with Unified Billing: OpenAI models with tools + reasoning efforts (the previously failing case), Claude models, and \`workers-ai/@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6\` (compat regression). Also live-verified the gateway's boundaries, which shaped this scope: under Unified Billing the legacy endpoint serves exactly \`openai/\`, \`anthropic/\`, and \`workers-ai/\` — Google/xAI fail spend-limit resolution (catalog slug ≠ route prefix) and DeepSeek gets no managed credentials. The models.dev catalog was aligned accordingly (models.dev#4674, #4676, #4693, #4715). Other providers arrive with the REST (\`/ai/v1\`) transport in V2. Supersedes #33597 — its token-scoping fix is included here with commit authorship preserved and co-author credit.

signal.title: feat(server): safely evict idle directory instances
signal.text: ## Summary Add an opt-in, server-scoped idle eviction mechanism for per-directory instances. This bounds retained plugin/MCP/LSP/watcher/database state without evicting active work. The feature is disabled unless `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_INSTANCE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` is set to an integer of at least 3600000 ms. A 2-hour value (`7200000`) is the intended initial deployment setting. ## Safety model - exact-entry activity leases around HTTP and ACP instance use - non-acquireable disposal tombstones; concurrent loads wait and retry - activity-generation guards for session runners/status, background jobs, and PTYs - immutable lexical PTY ownership keys - final synchronous validation before tombstone installation - alias reservations across tombstone waits and symlink retargets - scoped sweeper fiber and explicit disposal de-duplication This intentionally does not use entry-count LRU and does not evict while active work, detached/running PTYs, session runners/status, or background jobs exist. ## Verification - focused lifecycle/store/flags/eviction tests - Core and OpenCode typechecks - formatting, lint, and diff checks - full native Linux x64 build and smoke test - independent concurrency/data-integrity review: approved This is split from the SSE replacement-stream fix so each behavior can be reviewed independently.

signal.title: chore(core): compress bundled models snapshot
signal.text: ## What Store the bundled models.dev catalog as deterministic gzip/base64 instead of embedding its 3.6 MB JSON source directly in production artifacts. The reviewable `snapshot.txt` remains the source of truth. Production builds embed the generated compressed asset and decompress it lazily on first catalog access. ### Artifact measurements | Artifact | Before | After | Raw reduction | Distribution gzip | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Bun macOS arm64 executable | 125,630,306 B | 122,443,490 B | 3,186,816 B (2.54%) | -15,065 B | | Node bundle | 26,257,175 B | 23,085,890 B | 3,171,285 B (12.08%) | +6,036 B | | Node SEA | 193,617,744 B | 190,449,456 B | 3,168,288 B (1.64%) | +2,691 B | The isolated first decode and parse adds approximately 12.7 ms once per process or isolate. Twelve-run end-to-end CLI benchmarks did not show a statistically meaningful startup difference. Subsequent reads use the existing in-memory cache. ## How - `packages/core/script/update-models-snapshot.ts` writes both the reviewable JSON and deterministic level-9 gzip/base64 asset. - `packages/core/src/models-dev.ts` decodes and decompresses the asset through portable `Uint8ArrayFromBase64` and `DecompressionStream("gzip")` APIs before the existing catalog decoder and normalizer. - `packages/core/test/models.test.ts` verifies the generated asset restores byte-for-byte to the reviewable source. - `packages/cli/script/build-node.ts` verifies Node bundles contain the compressed marker and reject the uncompressed catalog marker. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[models.dev api.json] --> B[update snapshot script] B --> C[snapshot.txt for review] B --> D[gzip/base64 asset] D --> E[production bundle] E --> F[lazy gzip decode] F --> G[existing catalog decode and normalize] G --> H[in-memory isolate cache] ``` ## Scope - This reduces installed and unpacked artifact size; compressed release download size is effectively unchanged. - The PR does not use Brotli. Brotli produced a smaller payload, but workerd's `DecompressionStream` supports gzip and deflate rather than Brotli. - The PR does not change catalog data, normalization, refresh behavior, or public APIs. ## Testing - `bun run test test/models.test.ts` from `packages/core`: 14 passing tests. - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core`. - `bun typecheck` from `packages/cli`. - `bun run test test/workerd.test.ts` from `packages/server`. - `bun run probe:workerd` from `packages/server`. - Full `bun turbo typecheck --concurrency=3` push hook: 33 tasks successful. - Built production Bun macOS arm64 executable and Node macOS arm64 SEA. - Ran `models --standalone` from both artifacts with fetching disabled and confirmed identical 104-line output against the baseline. - Regenerated the gzip/base64 asset twice and confirmed identical SHA-256 output.

signal.title: refactor(protocol): derive simulation wire contracts
signal.text: ## What Make `@opencode-ai/protocol/simulation` the authoritative schema-first simulation contract that standalone controllers can consume without copying OpenCode internals. Each simulation operation now defines its method, payload, and success schemas once. The module derives JSON-RPC request decoders and precise Effect RPC groups from those definitions, and exposes a typed union for backend notifications. This advances #42136. It creates the publication seam needed for the follow-up Drive migration that deletes Drive's copied protocol. ## How - `packages/protocol/src/simulation.ts` - Adds private operation and endpoint descriptors. - Derives frontend/backend request schemas, decoders, and `UiRpcs` / `BackendRpcs` from the descriptors. - Adds canonical `Backend.Notification` schemas and decoders for `llm.request`, `tool.invocation`, and `tool.cancel`. - Validates that the established capability tuples exactly cover request operations, notifications, and feature capabilities. - Preserves protocol-v1 capability order and literal-union types. - Preserves `llm.finish` request normalization while retaining the optional Effect RPC payload. - Requires exactly one JSON-RPC response outcome at runtime and in TypeScript. - `packages/simulation/test/protocol.test.ts` - Covers capability compatibility, RPC alignment, notification decoding, finish normalization, and response exclusivity. - Adds compile-time checks for capability literals and JSON-RPC response outcomes. - `packages/simulation/test/simulated-provider.test.ts` - Exercises the omitted finish reason through the real websocket server. ## Scope This PR does not migrate `opencode-drive` yet. That follows after an OpenCode `next` release publishes this Protocol surface, at which point Drive can pin the matching Protocol/Client versions and delete its copied schema. This PR also does not change simulation activation. signal.title: [BUG] Bash tool subprocess killed with SIGKILL when stdout streams many small writes (e.g. pytest tests/)
signal.text: ## Title [BUG] Bash tool subprocess killed with SIGKILL when stdout streams many small writes (e.g. `pytest tests/`) ## Body ### Environment - OpenCode CLI, version from 2026 - Running inside WSL (Ubuntu 24.04) on Windows 11 - Default provider config (model details irrelevant) - Memory: 19 GB total, 17 GB free at time of failure (NOT an OOM) - Disk: 946 GB free (NOT a disk-full) ### Observed behavior When the bash tool (or any sub-agent invocation that uses bash) runs a command that emits **many small writes to stdout in rapid succession**, the subprocess is killed with exit code 9 (SIGKILL). The parent OpenCode process and the user session remain alive. ### Reproduction In a Python project with pytest tests: ```bash # DOES reproduce (kills with SIGKILL, exit code 9): pytest tests/ -m "not integration" pytest tests/infrastructure/test_foo.py # Does NOT reproduce (succeeds normally): echo "hello" for i in $(seq 1 30); do echo "line $i"; done pytest tests/ --collect-only -q pytest tests/infrastructure/test_fastapi_app.py # 23 tests, single file ``` ### Hypothesis The trigger is the **streaming write pattern**, not the output size or the command. Pytest emits one write per test (a "." or "F" character) plus a carriage-return progress bar. Other commands that emit a single large write at the end (echo, `--collect-only`) or fewer writes survive. ### Attempts to work around (all failed) - `-q` flag (quiet mode) - `--tb=line --no-header --no-summary` - `-p no:cacheprovider` - `python3 -u` (forced unbuffered — made it worse if anything) - Different providers/models in `opencode.json` - Different MCP server configuration ### Related upstream issues - #40439 — TUI sessions hang permanently: zombie git child under project-copy-refresh snapshot step - #35241 — fix(shell): three timeouts and an exit fallback for the bash tool hang class - #28780 — fix(shell): add timeout guards for pre-spawn pipeline and post-SIGKILL cleanup - #24077 — opencode (default mode) closes entire terminal window on Linux / i3wm The pattern matches #35241's "bash tool hang class" most closely. ### Impact Blocks any verification that requires running a full test suite through the bash tool. Workarounds: split tests into many small pytest invocations, or run verification outside of OpenCode entirely.

signal.title: fix(tui): preserve tab drag source
signal.text: ## What Make session tab dragging preserve the tab where the gesture began, including vertical drags started from the detail row or moved through an inter-tab separator. ## Before / After **Before:** OpenTUI captures the renderable beneath the first drag event rather than the tab that received `mousedown`. A vertical drag starting from a tab's second row could first cross the separator or another tab, causing the wrong tab to preview, reorder, or become selected. Releasing over the add or close affordances could also activate that control after the reorder. **After:** The pressed tab remains the drag source for the complete gesture. The rail or strip owns preview and release handling across rows, separators, overflow markers, and controls. The synthetic mouse-up following `drag-end` cannot add or close a tab. ## How - `packages/tui/src/component/session-tabs.tsx` records source identity on tab press instead of deriving it from row-local drag callbacks. - Vertical rails and horizontal strips handle drag targeting and release at the container level. - A short-lived click-suppression latch distinguishes OpenTUI's trailing drop-target mouse-up from a real click. - Close, add, context-menu, and ordinary selection behavior remain unchanged for non-drag gestures. ## Scope This PR fixes drag identity and gesture lifecycle within the visible vertical rail and horizontal strip. It does not add edge-triggered auto-scrolling into hidden tabs or change OpenTUI's renderer-level mouse capture API. ## Testing - `bun typecheck` from `packages/tui` - `bun run test` from `packages/tui` (691 passed, 5 skipped) - Push hook monorepo typecheck (34 packages successful) - Fixture-driven live TUI checks for title/detail rows, active/inactive tabs, both directions, separators, return-to-origin, scrolled vertical rails, horizontal overflow markers, add/close drop targets, normal clicks, and context menus ## Demo The fixture-driven V2 TUI story shows the active tab dragged from its detail row through the separator into slot 3. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/801af48f-31d2-4065-aa2a-027e3236f128

signal.title: 48-bit ID timestamp wraparound on 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC wedges all pre-existing sessions (loop exits at step 0, prompts silently ignored)
signal.text: ### Description **All sessions created before `2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC` silently stop processing prompts** due to a 48-bit timestamp wraparound in the ID generator (`packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`). This is likely the root cause behind #42605 and a spike of "agent stops responding in an existing session" reports starting today. #### Root cause `Identifier.create()` encodes `Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` into **6 bytes** (48 bits): ```ts let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // ← only the low 48 bits survive for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } ``` `Date.now() * 4096` is a ~53-bit number, so the sortable prefix wraps every `2^36 ms ≈ 2.18 years`. The most recent wrap boundary was: ``` 1786706395136 ms = 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC ``` Before the boundary, ascending IDs were near the top of the range (`msg_ffd4…`); after it they restart near zero (`msg_000b…`). Any new user message in a pre-existing session now **sorts before the entire session history**. The v2 session loop, which picks up work by ID ordering, sees nothing new past its watermark and exits immediately: ``` level=INFO message=loop session.id=ses_… step=0 level=INFO message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_… ``` No provider call is ever made; the message is stored but never processed. Retrying, switching models, and `/summarize` all fail the same way. Sessions created entirely after the boundary work fine (all IDs post-wrap, internally consistent). #### Evidence (from two independent production sessions, v1.18.4) Session A — last processed message vs. newly posted prompts: ``` last assistant msg (Aug 13): msg_ffd4c8ecc001nKKJtMDUGfajRL new user msg (Aug 14): msg_000bcb6970013Jm92xkWhlZiOA ← sorts before all history ``` Verification of the encoding: the new message was created at `1786718762656 ms`; `1786718762656 − 1786706395136 = 12,367,520 = 0xBCB6A0` → matches the observed `000bcb6…` prefix exactly. Session B — same split within one session: ``` first msg (Aug 13): msg_ffb02725b001iqapSOS18lP6Rb new msgs (Aug 14): msg_0007f07f9001…, msg_000e4a4c2001…, msg_000ebffe9001… ``` Newest row in the `message` table is a `user` message with no assistant response; every prompt produces the step-0 loop exit above. Also note `Identifier.timestamp()` in the same file decodes post-wrap IDs to garbage (it assumes the full timestamp survived), so anything deriving times from IDs is silently wrong after the boundary too. #### Impact - Every session with history from before 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC is permanently wedged on current releases (reproduced on 1.18.4; #42605 reports 1.18.1). `id.ts` is unchanged at current HEAD, so the bug is still live. - Next wrap: ~October 2028, when it will happen again for all then-active sessions. #### Suggested fixes 1. Widen the encoded value (8 bytes removes the problem for ~570 years), with a migration/compat story for existing IDs, or 2. Seed the generator / the loop watermark from `max(message.id)` per session at instance init, so new IDs always sort after existing ones, and 3. Short term: detect the condition (new user message ID < session max ID) and either re-key the message or surface an explicit error instead of silently ignoring the prompt. ### OpenCode version 1.18.4 (also reproduced indirectly on 1.18.1 via #42605); `id.ts` unchanged at HEAD as of 2026-08-14. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Take any session with messages created before 2026-08-14 12:39:55 UTC. 2. Send a new prompt. 3. Observe: message row is written, log shows `loop step=0` → `exiting loop`, no model call, no response. (Equivalent synthetic repro: create a session, insert a message with an ID in the `ff…` range, then prompt normally.) ### Operating System Linux (server mode, headless); also reported on Windows 11 Desktop (#42605).

signal.title: SIGUSR2 theme reload interrupts an in-flight session
signal.text: ### Description Changing the desktop theme while opencode is working interrupts the run. Omarchy signals opencode on every theme change — `omarchy-restart-opencode` runs `killall -SIGUSR2 opencode`. In the TUI, SIGUSR2 calls the worker's `reload` RPC (`packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:216`), and that reload invalidates config and then disposes every instance (`packages/opencode/src/cli/tui/worker.ts:63`). Disposing an instance cancels the session runners it owns, so whatever is in flight — a model stream or a shell command — is aborted. The theme itself does not depend on that reload: the TUI re-detects the terminal palette and re-scans theme files from its own SIGUSR2 handler in `packages/tui/src/context/theme.tsx`. ### OpenCode version 1.18.18, also reproduced on dev @ e23586af2 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start the TUI. 2. Start something long-running, e.g. `!sleep 45`. 3. From another terminal, `kill -SIGUSR2 <tui pid>` (this is what an Omarchy theme switch does). 4. The run is aborted immediately with "User aborted the command", and the log shows `disposing all instances` within milliseconds of the signal. ### Operating System Arch Linux (Omarchy), Hyprland ### Terminal foot

signal.title: fix(opencode): defer config reload until sessions are idle
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #42621 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? SIGUSR2 makes the TUI worker reload config, and that reload disposes every instance. Instance disposal cancels the session runners the instance owns, so a signal that lands mid-run kills whatever is in flight. Desktop environments send SIGUSR2 on theme changes (Omarchy runs `killall -SIGUSR2 opencode`), so switching themes while opencode is working aborts the request. The reload now waits until no instance has a busy session before invalidating config and disposing, so the reload is deferred rather than dropped. Signals that arrive while waiting join the pending reload instead of stacking. Themes still update immediately — that path never went through the worker. The TUI re-detects the terminal palette and re-scans theme files from its own SIGUSR2 handler. `InstanceStore.list()` is new; the wait needs it to check `SessionStatus` per instance. ### How did you verify your code works? Manually, before and after, using a shell command so no model call is involved: 1. `bun dev`, then `!sleep 45`, then `kill -SIGUSR2 <tui pid>` from another terminal. 2. On dev: the run aborts with "User aborted the command", and the log shows `disposing all instances` ~5ms after the signal. 3. On this branch: the run finishes normally, and `disposing all instances` appears once the session goes idle — so the config reload still happens, just later. Tests: - `test/server/global-lifecycle.test.ts` (new): `awaitSessionsIdle` returns while idle, and blocks until a busy session goes idle. Checked that it fails if the busy predicate is broken. - `test/project/instance.test.ts`: coverage for `InstanceStore.list()`. - `bun typecheck` clean in `packages/opencode`; `bun test test/server/httpapi-global.test.ts test/project/` passes. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro via zen/go: reasoning_content inconsistency causes "must be passed back to the API" error in multi-turn tool calls
signal.text: ## Description When using DeepSeek V4 Pro via the `opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` endpoint, multi-turn conversations with tool calls fail intermittently with: ``` Error from provider (DeepSeek): The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API. ``` ## Root Cause DeepSeek V4 Pro's thinking mode is **all-or-nothing**: once ANY assistant message in the conversation history includes `reasoning_content`, ALL subsequent assistant messages MUST also include it. If even one message lacks it (e.g., a `tool_calls` message where reasoning was omitted), the API rejects the entire request. ## Reproduction (minimal) **FAILS** — first assistant has `reasoning_content`, second (tool_calls) does NOT: ```json { "model": "deepseek-v4-pro", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "帮我查下文件"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "好的，我来帮你查。", "reasoning_content": "用户需要查文件，我应该用工具。"}, {"role": "user", "content": "读SOUL.md"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [{"id":"c1","type":"function","function":{"name":"read","arguments":"{\"path\":\"SOUL.md\"}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "SOUL内容"}, {"role": "user", "content": "写个总结"} ], "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"read","description":"read","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}}}}} ], "max_tokens": 20 } ``` → Returns: `"The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API."` **PASSES** — ALL assistant messages consistently have `reasoning_content`: ```json { "model": "deepseek-v4-pro", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "读SOUL.md"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [{"id":"c1","type":"function","function":{"name":"read","arguments":"{\"path\":\"SOUL.md\"}"}}], "reasoning_content": "需要读文件，调用read工具。"}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "# SOUL\n我是时崎狂三"}, {"role": "user", "content": "总结"} ], "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"read","description":"read","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}}}}} ], "max_tokens": 30 } ``` → Works fine (200 OK). ## Impact - Any multi-turn conversation using DeepSeek V4 Pro with tool calls (e.g., OpenClaw, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) will fail after the first tool call - The zen/go proxy appears to sometimes omit `reasoning_content` from tool_calls responses, creating the inconsistency - This is the typical pattern for coding agents where model generates text → calls tools → continues conversation ## Suggested Fix The zen/go proxy should either: 1. Ensure `reasoning_content` is consistently included in ALL assistant messages when thinking mode is active, including tool call messages, OR 2. Strip `reasoning_content` from ALL messages in the history before forwarding to DeepSeek if consistency cannot be guaranteed ## Environment - Endpoint: `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` - Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` - Timestamp: 2026-04-30 03:30 UTC

signal.text: SUPPORT MEMO Subject: Commercial Multiplatform System Architectural Design — OpenCode Session Not Responding Date: August 14, 2026 Issue Description The OpenCode session associated with the project “Commercial Multiplatform System Architectural Design” stopped responding during the execution of the comprehensive QA process. OpenCode had completed an analysis stage and presented the following questions before continuing: Whether XAMPP/MySQL could be started to run the test scripts and verify the fixes. Whether the pending security issues should be fixed: PermissionMiddleware wiring. Refactoring of $_GET / $_POST. Removal of unsafe addslashes() usage. Whether OpenCode should stop and present the QA report as-is. The intended response was to authorize OpenCode to continue the QA process, apply the authorized security and quality fixes, and perform regression testing. Problem After OpenCode displayed these questions, the session stopped responding. The input box is still visible, but when a new instruction is entered and submitted, OpenCode does not respond and does not resume processing. The session appears to remain open, but no further response or agent activity occurs. Additional Information The interface also displays the Git/Review section with the message: “No changes detected.” The OpenCode session has deliberately not been closed or restarted, in order to avoid potentially losing the current conversation context, agent state, or any work performed during the QA process. The last visible activity from OpenCode is the QA-related question shown above. Request to Support Please investigate the following: Why the OpenCode agent stopped responding. Whether the current session is frozen or experiencing an agent/model/tool execution issue. Whether the project context and current state are still intact. Whether there is a safe way to recover the current session without losing the work already performed. Whether the issue is related to the interface, connection, model/agent, or tool execution. What procedure should be followed to safely resume the QA process from the exact point where it stopped. Important This project is currently in the QA and stabilization phase. signal.title: [BUG] Zen Go Anthropic endpoint: tools requests fail for all GLM models ([1210] / 422 'web_search' translation error)
signal.text: ## Description On the OpenCode Zen **Go** Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages`), **any request with a non-empty `tools` array fails for all GLM models** (glm-5.3, glm-5.2, glm-5.1). The same request without `tools`, or with the same `tools` against other models (kimi-k3, qwen3.7-plus), succeeds — so this looks like a broken Anthropic→GLM tools translation in the Console Go gateway, not a client or account issue. This effectively makes GLM models unusable from Claude Code, which always sends `tools`. ## Environment - Endpoint: `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages` (Anthropic-compatible, Go plan) - Client: plain `curl` (reproduces without any client), and Claude Code - Reproduced with **3 independent Go plan API keys** (3 separate workspaces) — identical errors, so account-independent - Date: 2026-08-15 ## Repro 1 — glm-5.3 + one minimal tool → `[1210]` ```bash curl -X POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: <REDACTED>" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" -H "content-type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "glm-5.3", "max_tokens": 2048, "tools": [{ "name": "get_weather", "description": "query weather", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"] } }], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "What is the weather in Beijing? Please call the tool."}]}] }' ``` Response: ```json {"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [1210] Invalid API parameter, please check the documentation."}} ``` Notes: - `"tools": []` (empty array) → 200 OK, so it's specifically non-empty `tools`. - Fails regardless of tool shape (with/without `description`, with extra `type` field, complex schemas). ## Repro 2 — glm-5.2 / glm-5.1 + same tool → 422 with revealing param path ```json {"error":{"param":"tools.0.function-after[_domain_filters(), WebSearchTool].type","type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] Input should be 'web_search'"}} ``` The mangled param path `tools.0.function-after[_domain_filters(), WebSearchTool].type` suggests the gateway is translating ordinary Anthropic function tools into Zhipu's **web_search tool format** before forwarding upstream. ## Control experiments (why I believe it's a gateway translation bug) | Request | Result | |---|---| | glm-5.3, no `tools` → `/zen/go/v1/messages` | ✅ 200 | | glm-5.3, 1 minimal tool → `/zen/go/v1/messages` | ❌ `[1210]` | | glm-5.2 / glm-5.1, same tool → same endpoint | ❌ 422 `Input should be 'web_search'` | | **kimi-k3**, same tool → same endpoint | ✅ 200, clean `tool_use` block | | **qwen3.7-plus**, same tool → same endpoint | ✅ 200, clean `tool_use` block | | glm-5.3, same tool → `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (**OpenAI** endpoint) | ✅ 200, correct `tool_calls` with parsed arguments | | glm-5.2, same tool → **Zhipu native** `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/anthropic/v1/messages` | ✅ 200, clean `tool_use` block | So: the GLM models themselves handle tools fine (OpenAI endpoint + Zhipu native Anthropic endpoint both work), the Zen Anthropic endpoint's tool translation works fine for other vendors (kimi/qwen) — the failure is specific to the Anthropic→GLM tools translation path in the Console Go gateway. ## Expected behavior `tools` on the Anthropic-compatible endpoint should work for GLM models the same way it does for kimi-k3 / qwen3.7-plus on the same endpoint, and for glm-5.3 on the OpenAI endpoint. ## Additional notes - glm-5.3 appears to be newly added to the model list (around 2026-08-14). - Side observation: on Zhipu's native Anthropic endpoint, requesting `glm-5.2` now returns `"model": "glm-5.3"` in the response — the alias seems to have been repointed upstream. Not sure if that's related to the routing difference between the `[1210]` (glm-5.3) and 422 (glm-5.2/5.1) errors.

signal.title: Console Go: Anthropic-route tool calls fail with 400 'function name is invalid' for Kimi models (kimi-k3, kimi-k2.7-code)
signal.text: **Summary** Requests to `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages` (Anthropic route) with any tool that carries an `input_schema` fail with HTTP 400 for the Kimi models (`kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`). Other models on the same route accept the identical request. **Error** ``` 400 invalid_request_error "Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] Invalid request: function name is invalid, must start with a letter and can contain letters, numbers, underscores, and dashes" ``` The error is misleading: the tool names are all valid (`Bash`, `Edit`, `mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore`, ...). Bisection shows the trigger is the *presence* of the `input_schema` key, not its content and not the name. **Reproduction** 1. Build an Anthropic `/v1/messages` request with `model: "kimi-k3"` and any single tool, e.g.: ```json {"name": "Bash", "description": "run", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}}} ``` 2. POST to `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages` with an `opencode-go` key. 3. Result: 400 with the error above. **Bisection results** (same body, only the tool definition varied, model `kimi-k3`): | tool definition | result | |---|---| | `name` only | OK | | `name` + `description` | OK | | `name` + `description` + `input_schema` (any content, even `{}`) | 400 | | same with `deepseek-v4-flash` / `qwen3.8-max` / `minimax-m3` / `gpt-5.6-luna` | OK | | same with `kimi-k2.7-code` | 400 | | same with `glm-5.2` | 422 | | `grok-4.5` | 401 "Model grok-4.5 is not supported for format anthropic" | **Additional data** - The OpenAI route works for the same models: `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `tools: [{type: "function", ...}]` on `kimi-k3` succeeds. So this is specific to the Anthropic-route tool-schema conversion for the Kimi upstream. - Affects every Claude Code session pointed at `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/go` with a Kimi model — the very first request fails because Claude Code always sends tool schemas. - Workaround today: use a non-Kimi model (`qwen3.8-max`, `minimax-m3`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, `gpt-5.6-luna`) on the Anthropic route. Claude Code's native OpenAI env route is not an alternative in v2.1.220 (it rejects models not in its own list). **Environment** - Gateway: `opencode.ai/zen/go` ("Console Go" provider) - Client: Claude Code 2.1.220, also plain HTTP replay against the gateway (no client involved) - Date: 2026-08-07

signal.title: fix(ai): remove over-safe provider error handling
signal.text: ## Summary This removes the native request executor's vibed, over-safe provider-error policy and aligns it with pre-existing legacy behavior such as the AI SDK path. Specifically, this kills: - the 500-character gate that discarded valid structured provider messages - the 16 KiB response-body cap and `bodyTruncated` behavior - structural response-body redaction based on names such as `token`, `secret`, `key`, and `authorization` - literal replacement of request header and query values echoed by providers - automatic masking of request URL query parameters - automatic and `CurrentRedactedNames`-driven request/response header redaction at the executor seam - raw-body display for short unrecognized payloads Structured `error.message` and top-level `message` values are now parsed from the complete response and surfaced regardless of size. Complete response bodies, URLs, headers, and transport messages are retained in HTTP diagnostics. Unrecognized or malformed payloads use the generic HTTP status fallback rather than being printed as the user-facing message. ## Why The removed behavior was vibed, "over-safe", and inconsistent with pre-existing legacy behavior from integrations such as the AI SDK. It silently threw away useful provider errors based on arbitrary body-length thresholds and applied a separate sanitization policy only to the native path. Matching the established behavior makes native and legacy provider failures predictable and preserves the actual diagnostic evidence. ## Checks - `bun test test/executor.test.ts --timeout 30000 --test-name-pattern 'RequestExecutor'` - `bun test test/provider/openai-chat.test.ts test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts test/provider/anthropic-messages.test.ts --timeout 30000 --test-name-pattern 'fails HTTP provider errors before stream parsing'` - `bun typecheck` Requested by: @rekram1-node (Aiden Cline via Slack)

signal.title: [BUG] OpenAI Responses: assistant messages sent as {role:"assistant", content:[{type:"output_text"}]} rejected by strict OpenAI-compatible servers
signal.text: ## Summary When a conversation history contains an assistant text message and opencode sends it to an OpenAI Responses (`/responses`) endpoint, the request body uses: ```json {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]} ``` This shape is **not valid** per OpenAI's Responses input schema. Real `api.openai.com` tolerates it, but strict OpenAI-compatible servers that validate with the official OpenAI SDK types (e.g. a self-hosted Qwen server exposing `/v1/responses`) reject it with a 422/400 validation error, so switching a session to such a model fails. ## Environment - opencode 1.18.18 (Snap, stable) - Default runtime (AI SDK path), `@ai-sdk/openai` 3.0.84 - Server: self-hosted OpenAI-compatible `/v1/responses` endpoint (validates with `openai` Python SDK pydantic types) ## Repro 1. Configure a custom provider/model pointing at an OpenAI-compatible `/responses` server. 2. Switch an existing session to that model so the history (including prior assistant text) is resent. 3. The request fails with a pydantic `ValidationError` on the `input` array, e.g.: ``` loc: ('body', 'input', 'list[union[EasyInputMessageParam, Message, ResponseOutputMessageParam, ...]]', 2, 'ResponseFunctionToolCallParam', 'call_id') msg: 'Field required' input: {'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'output_text', 'text': '...'}]} ``` ## Root cause `@ai-sdk/openai` builds assistant input items as `{ role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "output_text", text }], id }` (`convertToOpenAIResponsesMessages`, dist/index.js ~3127). Per the official OpenAI schema (`openai-python` types): - `EasyInputMessageParam` allows `role: "assistant"` but `content` must be `str | list[input_text | input_image | input_file]` — `output_text` is **not** a valid easy-input content part. - `output_text` is only valid inside a full output item `{ type: "message", role: "assistant", id, status, content: [...] }` (`ResponseOutputMessageParam`, where `type`/`id`/`status` are required). OpenAI's own API is lenient and accepts the non-conformant shape, which is why this has gone unnoticed. The same bug also exists in the native llm protocol (`packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-responses.ts`, `lowerMessages`). ## Proposed fix Emit assistant text as an easy-input message with `input_text` parts: ```json {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "..."}]} ``` or, when an item id is available, the complete `{"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "id", "status": "completed", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]}`. A local fix for the native protocol is ready and tests pass (59 tests, `packages/llm`). The AI SDK path will additionally need a fix in `vercel/ai` (or a bumped `@ai-sdk/openai`) to fix the released builds.

signal.title: feat(ai): persist OpenAI Responses WebSocket across steps
signal.text: ## Problem The native OpenAI Responses WebSocket route currently uses a fresh socket for each `LLMClient.stream()` call: 1. `WebSocketTransport.json.frames()` opens a connection with `Effect.acquireRelease`. 2. It sends exactly one `response.create` message. 3. The connection is released and closed when that response stream ends. 4. The Responses request schema does not expose `previous_response_id`, so subsequent steps resend full input rather than continuing incrementally. This implements a one-shot WebSocket transport, but misses the primary benefit of OpenAI's WebSocket mode: retaining a connection across sequential model/tool steps and continuing with only new input plus `previous_response_id`. OpenAI reports substantial latency improvements for long tool-heavy chains when the active connection's response cache is reused: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/websocket-mode ## Relevant code - `packages/ai/src/route/transport/websocket.ts`: connection opened and released inside each `frames()` call - `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-responses.ts`: one `response.create` message per prepared request - `packages/ai/src/protocols/open-responses.ts`: shared request fields omit `previous_response_id` - V2 session runner/LLM ownership: determine the correct session- or execution-scoped owner for a reusable connection ## Desired implementation Add lifecycle-aware OpenAI Responses WebSocket continuation so sequential steps in one agent workflow can reuse the active socket and send incremental input with the latest response ID. Keep connection ownership above the stateless protocol model, and preserve clean fallback/recovery behavior when reuse is unavailable. ## Acceptance criteria - Sequential Responses steps can reuse one WebSocket connection rather than reconnecting per step. - Continuations send `previous_response_id` and only newly added input/tool-result items where valid. - The latest response ID is captured from provider events and scoped to the owning workflow/session. - Only one response is in flight per connection; unrelated or parallel sessions do not share unsafe state. - A closed/expired connection, `previous_response_not_found`, failed turn, cancellation, or non-reusable history falls back safely to a new connection with full input. - `store: false` remains supported. - Tests cover reuse, incremental continuation, isolation, closure, cancellation, and fallback. - HTTP/SSE Responses behavior remains unchanged.

signal.title: fix(ai): reject WebSocket transport for OpenAI Chat
signal.text: ## Problem The OpenAI Chat provider entrypoint shares `Settings` with the Responses entrypoint, so it accepts `transport: "websocket"`. However, `chatModel()` ignores `settings.transport` and always selects `configure(config(settings)).chat(modelID)`, whose `/v1/chat/completions` route uses HTTP/SSE. This makes a WebSocket selection on `@opencode-ai/ai/providers/openai/chat` silently behave like the default transport. OpenAI documents persistent WebSocket mode for the Responses API, not Chat Completions: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/websocket-mode ## Relevant code - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai.ts`: shared `Settings.transport` and `chatModel()` - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai/chat.ts`: exports `chatModel` as `model` - `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts`: HTTP/SSE Chat route ## Expected behavior Make unsupported transport selection impossible or explicit for the Chat entrypoint. Prefer a Chat-specific settings surface that does not expose `transport`; if runtime input can still contain it, reject `transport: "websocket"` with a clear error instead of silently ignoring it. ## Acceptance criteria - The OpenAI Chat package entrypoint no longer silently accepts WebSocket transport. - Type-level coverage prevents WebSocket selection at normal TypeScript call sites. - Runtime coverage verifies a clear failure for untyped/serialized unsupported input, if that input reaches this boundary. - OpenAI Responses keeps its existing `"http" | "websocket"` setting.

signal.title: codemode: execute catalog ignores agent permission denies on shipped next builds
signal.text: ## Summary The `execute` (Code Mode) tool catalog includes **every connected codemode-enabled MCP server's tools for every agent**, ignoring the agent's permission deny rules. Denying a server's namespace with `resource: "*"` (which the docs say hides a server's tools) does not remove it from the catalog delivered in `execute`'s instructions. Verified on shipped `next` builds (next-17403 and next-17430); branch head `packages/core/src/tool.ts` already contains the intended `whollyDisabled` filtering, so this is a shipping gap, not a design question. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-next-17430 (also reproduced on 0.0.0-next-17403) - OS: Darwin 25.5.0 (darwin arm64) - Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-ghostty, COLORTERM=truecolor) - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: next (Homebrew, /opt/homebrew/bin/opencode2) - Active plugins: ~/.config/opencode/plugins/notify.ts ## Reproduction 1. Configure three local MCP servers (codemode default `true`, e.g. filesystem servers rooted at different dirs plus a shell server). 2. Define an agent whose permissions deny two of the three namespaces with `resource: "*"` (rules ordered so the last matching rule for those actions is the deny): ```yaml permissions: - action: "*" resource: "*" effect: allow - action: fs_c_* resource: "*" effect: deny - action: shell_c_* resource: "*" effect: deny - action: fs_b_* resource: "*" effect: allow ``` 3. Start a session with that agent and ask it to list the namespaces inside its `execute` catalog (headless: `opencode2 run --agent test-b --auto "list the namespaces in your execute tool's catalog"` from a project with the above config). 4. Observe the reply. ## Expected Behavior The `execute` catalog contains only the allowed server (`fs-b`, 14 tools) plus `$codemode.search` — the denied namespaces are filtered out before catalog assembly, consistent with: - the branch head implementation in `packages/core/src/tool.ts` (`snapshot()` applies `whollyDisabled(tool.options?.permission ?? name, rules)` to the active set before splitting direct/codemode registrations and building `CodeModeTool.catalog(codemode)`), and - the permissions docs for V2: deny rules with `resource: "*"` hide a server's tools. ## Actual Behavior The catalog lists all three namespaces: `fs-b (14 tools), fs-c (14 tools), shell-c (1 tool)`. The deny rules do not affect catalog visibility on shipped builds. Execution of the leaked tools **is** still blocked per call: each MCP tool's `execute` runs `permission.assert({ action: name(server, tool), ... })` (packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts), so cross-folder access is denied at runtime. The impact is therefore: - context bloat: denied servers' tool schemas consume the context window of every agent, and - wasted steps: the model attempts visible-but-denied tools and burns steps on errors (observed repeatedly in a real run). ## Additional Context - Consistent reproduction: two nightly builds (17403, 17430), headless `opencode2 run`, three-server config, agent with namespace-wide denies. - Docs reference: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers ("Use permission actions to hide or deny a server's tools", including the `{ "action": "context7_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }` example) — shipped behavior contradicts this for the Code Mode catalog. - Branch head evidence: `packages/core/src/tool.ts` (v2 branch, head as of 2026-08-14) filters via `whollyDisabled` before assembling the codemode map; the shipped next binaries do not exhibit it. - Workaround for permission-isolated agent setups on shipped builds: scope MCP servers per project (only the servers an agent may use in that project's config), since deny rules cannot currently hide codemode catalog entries.

signal.title: Loop doesn't exit after finish=stop — model re-invoked with no input until the session is quit
signal.text: ### Description When the agent finishes a turn with finish=stop and no tool calls, the session should go idle. Instead the loop keeps running and re-calls the model every ~10-20s with no new user message. The UI shows "busy" the whole time while the model just returns one-line filler ("Standing by", "Ready", "Idle"). From the logs: - Normal cycles end with an exiting loop event. The stuck cycle never emits one — it runs loop step=0..28+ over ~25 minutes. - The repeating pattern is loop step=N -> process (new message) -> stream (new model call), with nothing in between. - Every filler message is finish=stop and its step-finish reason=stop, so the model is correctly signaling "done" and the loop is ignoring it. - Esc fires cancel + error=Aborted (finish=None, 0 parts), then the loop restarts at step=0 and sticks again. Esc doesn't break it; only quitting the session does. Also notable: the model's hidden reasoning in those filler turns literally says "I'm being repeatedly prompted with no user message — this is an artifact", so it's aware it's being re-called with nothing to do. Version 1.17.18, model deepseek-v4-pro (opencode-go), Linux/WSL. Reproduced in one session, then again right after resuming it. Looks related to #42363 and #22329. ### Plugins No plugins ### OpenCode version 1.17.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run opencode (v1.17.18) with deepseek-v4-pro (opencode-go). 2. Do a normal multi-turn agent task — several tool calls, some reasoning, then a finish=stop (e.g. "implement X, run the tests, commit, summarize"). 3. Let it reach a turn that ends with no tool calls. Instead of going idle, it keeps re-calling the model every ~10-20s with no new input — the UI stays "busy" and it appends one-line "Standing by" / "Ready" / "Idle" replies. 4. Press Esc: the current generation aborts, but the loop restarts at step=0 and sticks again. 5. Only quitting the session (Ctrl+C) stops it. Note: not fully deterministic — I only hit it after long sessions with a lot of reasoning/tool history, so it may depend on context length. ### Screenshot and/or share link Recreated using sql db trace by ds4 pro ### Operating System WSL on Windows 11 ### Terminal westerm

signal.title: OpenChamber transcript hides new messages in sessions created before 1.18.16
signal.text: ### Description Environment: opencode 1.18.16 (upgraded from 1.18.15), OpenChamber 1.18.3 web UI (Home Assistant add-on). Symptom: In sessions that existed before the 1.18.16 upgrade, new messages no longer appear at the end of the transcript. The transcript appears to end at the last pre-upgrade message; new questions/answers are effectively invisible. Sessions created after the upgrade work fine. Data is intact — GET /session/{id}/message returns every message including the newest, so this is a client-side ordering problem, not data loss. Root cause (confirmed against real data): opencode's message-ID generation changed in 1.18.16. Through 1.18.15 IDs were a monotonic sequence (msg_f7… → msg_ff…) so string order equalled chronological order. Starting 1.18.16 new IDs are msg_00…-prefixed. OpenChamber's transcript store sorts and merges messages by message-ID string comparison (the J6/Q6 comparators and gb/nL/eL/tL/X6 helpers in the web bundle), with eL/tL doing binary-search insertion keyed on ID. For any session containing both ID namespaces, string order is 00… < f7… < ff…, so new messages sort to the top of the transcript and the visible "end" stays at the last pre-upgrade message. Example: a 314-message session spanning the upgrade — the actual newest message (created the day after the upgrade) sorts to index 50 of 314, and the bottom of the transcript shows content from the day before. Suggested fix: order transcript messages by time.created (falling back to ID for ties) instead of message-ID string order, or keep message IDs monotonic/backward-compatible across releases so ID order remains chronological. ### Plugins Home Assistant add-on ### OpenCode version 1.18.16 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System HAOS ### Terminal _No response_

signal.text: We have scattered reports of memory issues so we are going to tackle them all in a central place. Manual snapshot flow - run opencode (terminal not desktop) - use it until memory has grown (we don't need crazy numbers, once it hits 1-2gb it should help) - press ctrl+p and select heap snapshot - ui will freeze while it is generated - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit Automatic snapshot flow - run opencode with `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1`, for example `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode` - use it until memory grows past around 2gb - opencode checks memory once a minute and automatically writes a heap snapshot when rss is above 2gb - snapshots are written to the log directory as `.heapsnapshot` files - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit and mention that you used the automatic flow If you follow this we can almost always trace the issue and fix it

signal.title: feat(simulation): slim production bridge
signal.text: ## What Production Bun and Node releases retain a thin, version-matched simulation bridge so `opencode-drive` can still launch and control packaged OpenCode instances. Drive owns frame-to-PNG rendering and media output, removing Canvas/Skia and bundled capture fonts from OpenCode artifacts without removing simulation support. Screenshots are now a Drive operation rather than a simulation wire RPC: Drive decodes screenshot params, calls `ui.capture`, preserves the complete RGBA frame, renders locally, and returns the media path. The obsolete `ui.screenshot` request, RPC schema, capability negotiation, frontend branch, and legacy remote path are removed. ## Before / After **Before:** protocol capture alpha was discarded during a full frame conversion, named non-screenshot command batches eagerly required a private media manifest, and scoped WebSocket shutdown could return before socket cleanup or an in-flight send completed. Artifact presence checks relied on strings that did not prove the bridge implementation was bundled. **After:** the shared Drive renderer consumes protocol RGBA frames directly, media is resolved only when a screenshot command executes, and each socket serializes callback-observed sends behind a 64 MiB outbound bound and terminates on rejected sends so disconnect cleanup fails waiting callers. Server finalization terminates clients, awaits listener closure, and awaits every accepted socket's cleanup before scope completion. Build graph verification proves the bridge inputs are bundled while publishable payload scans reject raster/font implementation leakage. ## Impact | Target | Artifact | Before | After | Savings | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | macOS arm64 | executable | 152,957,666 B (145.872 MiB) | 125,547,746 B (119.732 MiB) | 27,409,920 B (26.140 MiB, 17.92%) | | macOS arm64 | npm tgz | 73,677,305 B (70.264 MiB) | 60,772,593 B (57.957 MiB) | 12,904,712 B (12.307 MiB, 17.52%) | | Linux x64 glibc | executable | 239,618,176 B (228.518 MiB) | 175,569,024 B (167.436 MiB) | 64,049,152 B (61.082 MiB, 26.73%) | | Linux x64 glibc | npm tgz | 104,777,803 B (99.924 MiB) | 78,057,738 B (74.442 MiB) | 26,720,065 B (25.482 MiB, 25.50%) | Measurements compare equivalent `--skip-install --skip-web-ui` builds from `origin/v2` and this branch. The final macOS arm64 remeasurement remained exactly `125,547,746 B`. ## How - `packages/simulation` keeps the JSON-RPC bridge and provider/model/tool lifecycle, replaces its Bun-only control server with scoped cross-runtime `ws`, and removes Canvas/Skia, Fontsource assets, and PNG rendering. - `packages/protocol/src/simulation.ts` exposes `ui.capture` only; screenshot naming and validation are Drive-local. - `packages/drive/src/recording` accepts recording RGB or protocol RGBA frames while preserving the recording-specific public frame types and transparency without duplicating each captured line and span. - `packages/drive/src/cli/send.ts` reads the typed private media path only for batches that actually execute a screenshot. - Bun and Node builds verify concrete simulation module graph inputs. Artifact scanning covers each publishable file once per target and rejects Canvas/Skia/font/PNG/source-path leakage. - Host service verification launches the compiled artifact through Drive and requires a real capture-to-PNG result. ## Scope - Release target acquisition and selection are unchanged. - Effect RPC migration is deliberately excluded. - Backend model, provider, and tool lifecycle behavior remains unchanged. - No historical `ui.screenshot` wire compatibility is retained or required. - No generated client update is required because the public Server `HttpApi` is unchanged. ## Testing - `sh .husky/pre-push`: all 34 workspace typecheck tasks passed before commit and on push. - CLI node-asset collection and artifact verification smokes passed after consolidating the three recursive file walkers. - `bun run test:effect` in `packages/drive`: 207 passed. - `bun run test:cli` in `packages/drive`: 58 passed, including the named non-screenshot batch regression. - `bun test --timeout 30000 --only-failures` in `packages/simulation`: 39 passed, including deterministic cleanup, closed-socket continuation, and fail-closed outbound overflow. - Focused screenshot tests verify transparent foreground/background pixels, `⠹` fallback rendering, and continuous `┃`/`╹` geometry. - Rebuilt and scanned host Bun and Node production artifacts; normal version/help and compiled service lifecycle smokes passed. - Bun and Node compiled service smokes performed a real Drive handshake/capture and verified the resulting PNG. - The typed self-host script passed `opencode-drive check` and then passed against both rebuilt artifacts: TUI submit, deterministic LLM/tool flow, semantic snapshot, raw capture, Drive-rendered PNG, and MP4 recording. - The final host Bun payload scan and graph verification passed; the equivalent `--skip-web-ui` size remained unchanged. ## Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Drive participant OpenCode as Packaged OpenCode participant Bridge as Simulation bridge participant Renderer as Drive renderer Drive->>OpenCode: launch with Drive endpoints OpenCode->>Bridge: start scoped UI/backend WebSockets Drive->>Bridge: simulation.handshake Bridge-->>Drive: capabilities include ui.capture Drive->>Bridge: ui.capture Bridge-->>Drive: renderer-neutral RGBA frame Drive->>Renderer: render frame with Drive fonts Renderer-->>Drive: PNG in active media generation ```

signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #13918 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? In its current state, when using OpenCode's GitHub Action for a automatic PR review flow it writes a big, fat comment. This comment is often difficult to read (as it is just a wall of text), different to interpret when it refers to specific licks of code and many developers (myself included) prefer the traditional GitHub reviews flow when working on feedback. This PR introduces a new input parameter to the existing action flow: `review_mode`. This new field has two new valid options: `comment` or `inline` (default to `comment`). The `comment` flow keeps the existing behaviour so existing users will not be affected. When `inline` is used, the prompt given to the chat session is changed slightly and the [structured responses](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs) output is used- falling back to a manual parsing behaviour when not supported by the model- so that a proper review can be given. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added tests for some of the new functions (although, I am not sure if these will run in the CI) Any extra guidance on how to do this would be appreciated :) ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: Bug Report: Message ID generation wraps every ~2.18 years, causing sessions to stop responding silently
signal.text: ### Description ## Summary The ID generator in `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts` only stores 48 bits of a `timestamp_ms * 0x1000 + counter` value. Because `timestamp_ms mod 2^36` is what actually survives, the "time" portion of every ID wraps every `2^36 ms` (≈ 2.18 years). After a wrap, newly generated IDs sort **before** older IDs lexicographically. For sessions that span the boundary, `MessageV2.latest()` then picks the wrong "latest" assistant message and the prompt loop (`runLoop` in `session/prompt.ts`) exits immediately without calling the model — the session silently stops producing responses. This is present in **v1.15.13** and still present on **dev** (verified `2026-08-14`, `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts` is identical). *Discovered with assistance from an AI coding tool (opencode) while debugging a session that stopped responding.* ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`: ```ts let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) now = direction === "descending" ? ~now : now const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // <-- only 48 bits stored for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } return prefix + "_" + timeBytes.toString("hex") + randomBase62(LENGTH - 12) ``` - `now = Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` needs ~53 bits, but only the low **48 bits** are kept. The stored value is effectively `(Date.now() mod 2^36) * 0x1000 + counter`. - `2^36 ms = 68,719,476,736 ms ≈ 795.4 days ≈ 2.18 years`. Whenever `Date.now()` crosses an integer multiple of `2^36`, the ID "clock" resets: IDs go from `...ffff...` back to `...0000...`. - The first wrap since 1970 that users will hit is `k = 26`, i.e. `26 * 2^36 ms ≈ 1,786,706,395,136 ms` (mid-2026). Impact on ordering and logic: 1. **`session/message-v2.ts` → `latest()`** picks the newest user/assistant by max ID string: ```ts if (info.role === "assistant" && (!assistant || info.id > assistant.id)) assistant = info ``` After the wrap, an *old* assistant message (from before the boundary, `msg_ffff…`) has a **larger** ID than a *new* user message (`msg_0003…`). 2. **`session/prompt.ts` → `runLoop()`** stops the loop when the last assistant already finished: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // <-- true after the wrap ) { /* exiting loop */ break } ``` A freshly sent user message has `id < lastAssistant.id` after the wrap, so the loop concludes "the assistant already replied" and **breaks without calling the model**. The user sees: message is saved, but nothing is generated. 3. **`Identifier.timestamp()`** also returns `(t mod 2^36)`, i.e. wrong absolute time for IDs created after the wrap. ## Symptoms - A session that was working stops responding to new messages (message is stored, but no assistant reply is produced). - Log shows the prompt loop exiting immediately without a model call: ``` INFO service=session.prompt session.id=ses_xxx step=0 loop INFO service=session.prompt session.id=ses_xxx exiting loop ``` (no `session.processor`, no `llm` lines in between) - Sessions created entirely after the wrap, or sessions whose history predates it but are not continued across the boundary, are unaffected. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.15.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create/continue a session that has messages with IDs before **and** after the boundary (`26 * 2^36 ms`; mid-2026). Any session whose last pre-boundary message ID starts with a high hex char (e.g. `msg_ffff…`) and that receives a new message after the wrap (ID `msg_0003…`) reproduces it. 2. Send any message. 3. Observe: the prompt loop logs `step=0 loop` then `exiting loop` within ~50 ms; no assistant message is ever produced. A long-running session used daily between ~2024 and 2026 reproduces this exactly once the wrap is crossed. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signal.text: ## Context When OpenCode helps write code that gets committed and pushed, it would be nice to credit it as a co-author via Git's `Co-authored-by` trailer. If no way currently exists, would you consider creating a dedicated GitHub user (e.g. `opencode-agent-bot` or similar) with a noreply email that community members can use in `Co-authored-by` trailers? signal.title: Go plan: $60/month quota exhausted in 6 days while the client recorded only $14.80 of usage — cache-read billing is invisible, undocumented, and the local cost meter is misleading users
signal.text: ### Description I am a paying Go plan subscriber ($10/mo). Within 6 days of my billing cycle (Aug 6 - Aug 12, 2026), both the dashboard and the opencode UI show my **monthly quota ($60) as essentially exhausted** - yet the usage recorded locally by the opencode client itself totals only **$14.80**. That is a **4x discrepancy** between what the product *tells me* I am consuming and what is actually metered against my quota. I find this deeply misleading. ### Reproduction steps 1. Subscribe to the Go plan. 2. Use opencode-go models (deepseek-v4-flash, kimi-k3) for 6 days - 1,791 assistant messages, 5.94M input / 778K output / 371M cache-read tokens (all recorded in the local opencode SQLite database). 3. Compare the locally recorded cost with the Go quota dashboard percentages. ### Expected behavior The local cost field should match what is metered against the Go quota, or the metered figure should be transparent (per-request billing breakdown, published cache-read pricing). ### Actual behavior - Local recorded cost: **$14.80**; dashboard: monthly quota essentially **exhausted**. - deepseek-v4-flash alone accumulated **359M cache-read tokens**, recorded locally at **$0.00**. - No warning before exhaustion; no per-request breakdown available to reconcile the 4x difference. ### Impact I paid for a month of usage and received **6 days** of paid models; the remaining ~24 days of my paid cycle are unusable unless I fall back to free models. ### Additional context Local data from the opencode SQLite database (every assistant message this cycle): | Model | Msgs | Input | Output | Cache read | Locally recorded cost | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | opencode-go/kimi-k3 | 238 | 1.87M | 121K | 12.6M | $13.24 | | opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash | 1550 | 4.04M | 656K | **359M** | $1.52 | | opencode-go/grok-4.5 / glm-5.2 | 3 | 25K | 351 | 16K | $0.05 | | **Total** | **1791** | **5.94M** | **778K** | **371M** | **$14.80** | If cache reads are metered anywhere near full input price, true consumption lands around **$40-$70** - consistent with an exhausted $60 cap. The official Go docs state only the three rolling windows ($12/5h, $30/week, $60/month) and say **nothing about cache token pricing**. Related reports with the same symptom (visible usage far below exhausted quota): - #38255 - ~$34 visible usage, monthly quota 100% blocked - #41206 - ~$11 visible usage, weekly quota 100% - #41391 - maintainer-opened question about Go quota accounting model I paid for $60 of usage across a month. I got 6 days, with a meter that claimed I had spent a quarter of my quota while draining it entirely. Whether this is an accounting bug or intentional opacity, it needs an answer - I expect a written explanation, a per-request audit of my account, and compensation for the unusable remainder of my billing cycle.

signal.title: ID generator wraps after ~795 days, breaking chronological sorting of message IDs
signal.text: ## Summary `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts` (and the client-side replicas in OpenChamber) encodes the timestamp as `Date.now() * 0x1000 + counter` into a **6-byte (48-bit) hex prefix**, which wraps around every 2^36 ms ≈ **795 days**. The latest wrap occurred on **2026-08-14 11:19:55 UTC**. After the wrap, newly created IDs sort **before** all older IDs lexicographically, silently breaking the "ascending ID = chronological order" contract that the format implies. ## Reproduction (real data) Same session, before and after the boundary: ``` msg_fffc192a8001… 2026-08-14 10:11 UTC (prefix near FFFF…) msg_0005afbc2002… 2026-08-14 12:59 UTC (prefix wrapped to 0000…) ``` String comparison orders the 12:59 messages **before** the 10:11 ones. In OpenChamber this rendered the newest messages at the **top** of any conversation that spans the boundary. ## Impact - Any code that derives chronological order from ID string comparison (the documented intent of the `ascending` IDs, and what third-party clients such as OpenChamber relied on) breaks every ~795 days. - `Identifier.timestamp(id)` in `id.ts` returns a wrong (mod-2^36-ms) value for IDs created after a wrap. - opencode's own DB queries (`message-v2.ts` uses `ORDER BY time_created, id`) are unaffected, but the *sortable-ID contract* exposed to clients is broken. - Note this also affects the **same-millisecond counter**: `lastTimestamp`/`counter` are process-global, and client-generated IDs (OpenChamber's optimistic inserts replicate this format) collide in ordering with server IDs generated in the same millisecond. ## Client-side workaround (already shipped) OpenChamber fixed the display-side impact by ordering messages on `time.created` instead of raw IDs: commit `53830952` on `openchamber/openchamber@main` ("fix(chat): keep messages chronological across ID rollover"). That only masks the root cause — the ID generator itself still wraps. ## Suggested fixes 1. **Encode 7 bytes (56 bits) instead of 6** — pushes the wrap to ~3.4M years while keeping a compact ID. 8 bytes (64 bits) is also fine. 2. If the format cannot change, **document the ~795-day wrap** and recommend clients order by `time.created` (already present on every message) rather than by ID. 3. Keep in mind old IDs with the 12-hex prefix will remain in existing stores — a format change alone doesn't reorder existing data, so clients should still prefer time-based ordering.

signal.title: Desktop Home view shows projects but zero sessions (database is correct)
signal.text: # Desktop (GUI) Home view shows projects but zero sessions — database is correct ## Summary The OpenCode Desktop app (macOS) shows the list of projects in the Home / sidebar, but every project displays **"Nothing here yet" / 0 sessions**, even though the SQLite database contains correctly-linked sessions. The terminal `opencode` CLI reads and writes the exact same database without any problem. ## Environment - OpenCode Desktop: **1.17.16** (also reproduced on earlier versions) - `opencode` CLI: **1.17.15** - OS: macOS (darwin, arm64) - Database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (~916 MB, 164 sessions, 5+ projects) ## Observed behavior 1. Open Desktop → Home view. 2. Sidebar lists the 3 projects the user has added (e.g. `opencode-settings-project`, `dockinkz`, `usage-widget`). 3. Selecting any project shows **"Nothing here yet — Create a session to get started"**. No session is listed for ANY project. 4. The terminal `opencode` CLI in the same projects works perfectly and its sessions are persisted to the DB. ## Expected behavior Sessions that exist in the database for a given project should appear in the Desktop Home view for that project. ## Evidence that the data is correct (not a DB/config issue) Verified directly against `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`: - `session.project_id` correctly references `project.id` (FK intact): ``` SELECT s.id, p.worktree, COUNT(*) FROM session s JOIN project p ON p.id = s.project_id GROUP BY p.id; -- /Users/diasmazhenov/vibecode/usage-widget | 3 -- /Users/diasmazhenov/vibecode/dockinkz | 1 -- .../opencode-settings-project | 1 ``` - `session.directory` matches `project.worktree` (fixed a mismatch, but the other projects already matched and still show 0). - `session.time_archived` is NULL for all relevant sessions. - `session.workspace_id` is NULL for all (consistent, not the cause). - `workspace` table is empty for everyone — not the differentiator. - The Desktop process holds the **same** shared DB file (confirmed via `lsof`: `OpenCode … /Users/diasmazhenov/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`). - Other projects (`/`, `open-design`) that are NOT in the Desktop sidebar DO have many sessions in the DB (86 / 73), so the Desktop's project list is a curated subset — but the 3 it shows still render 0 sessions despite valid data. ## Notes - The local Desktop API (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/project/:id/session`) returns `401 Unauthorized` (Basic realm) and the session list endpoint returns empty; the auth token could not be retrieved from local storage / process env, so the failure appears to be server-side session listing within the Desktop-embedded server rather than a pure frontend render issue. - A fresh restart of the Desktop app (which regenerates `opencode.global.dat`) does not resolve it. - `opencode serve` started manually also returns empty session lists for the same DB, suggesting the session-listing query/path used by the server is the failing component. ## Impact The Desktop GUI is effectively unusable for browsing/reopening past sessions; only the terminal CLI can access them. ## Root-cause analysis (from source) The Desktop Home session list pipeline: 1. `packages/app/src/pages/home.tsx` → `sessionLoad` query calls `focusedSync().project.loadSessions(directory, …)` for each `projectDirectories()`. 2. `packages/app/src/context/directory-sync.ts` → `fetch()` calls `client.session.list()` (SDK client scoped to the project directory) and stores results in the sync store. 3. `buildHomeSessionRecords()` (home.tsx:108) reads `sync.child(directory)[0]` and runs `sortedRootSessions()` → `roots()` → `isRootVisibleSession()`. 4. `packages/app/src/pages/layout/helpers.ts:26`: ```ts const isRootVisibleSession = (session, directory) => pathKey(session.directory) === pathKey(directory) && !session.parentID && !session.time?.archived ``` **The bug:** `isRootVisibleSession` reads `session.directory`, but the OpenCode server's `GET /api/session` response does **NOT** include a top-level `directory` field — the directory is only present under `location.directory`: ```json { "id": "ses_xxx", "projectID": "…", "location": { "directory": "/Users/…/project" }, "time": { "created": …, "updated": … } } ``` So `session.directory` is `undefined` → `pathKey(undefined) === pathKey(directory)` is `false` → **every session is filtered out** of the Home list. This matches the reported symptom exactly (projects show, sessions never do, for all projects). `projectForSession()` (helpers.ts:104) has the same problem: its directory fallback `pathKey(project.worktree) === pathKey(session.directory)` also fails when `session.directory` is undefined (only the `projectID` direct match works there). ### Suggested fix Either: - The server should return a top-level `directory` field on sessions (mirroring `location.directory`), or - The SDK/client `Session` type should map `location.directory` → `directory` before the UI consumes it.

signal.title: fix(tui): optimize Mermaid terminal rendering
signal.text: ## What Optimize Mermaid diagrams for terminal Markdown. A six-node vertical flowchart now occupies 28 rows instead of 38 while retaining its node borders, connector stems, and arrowheads. State transitions to offset end markers also remain connected. ## Before / After **Before:** The Markdown renderer forwarded an undefined `compact` option to Merman. Vertical flowcharts therefore used the lower-level library's spacious layout, adding three connector rows between every pair of nodes and making simple diagrams dominate the terminal viewport. **After:** The Markdown renderer resolves `compact` to `true` by default for flowchart and sequence layouts. Callers can still request the spacious layout explicitly with `compact: false`. **Before:** A state transition targeting an end marker on an overlapping vertical row could be classified as a vertical elbow even though no vertical corridor existed. Its route then jumped across the marker, rendering a detached line above it and arrow below it. **After:** Vertically overlapping endpoints use the existing side route, preserving a continuous path into the end marker. ## How - `packages/merman/src/markdown.ts` establishes compact spacing at the terminal Markdown boundary. - `packages/merman/src/test/markdown.test.ts` reproduces the reported six-node flowchart and locks its rendered height to 28 rows. - `packages/merman/src/state/routing.ts` avoids vertical elbows when endpoint bounds leave no vertical corridor. - `packages/merman/src/state/routing.test.ts` verifies route continuity for the state graph used in the demo. ## Scope The lower-level Merman rendering API keeps its existing spacing default. Timeline and GitGraph layout algorithms are unchanged. ## Testing - `bun run test` in `packages/merman` (326 tests) - `bun typecheck` in `packages/merman` - Full workspace typecheck from the pre-push hook (34 tasks) - `opencode-drive check mermaid-diagrams-drive.ts` - Isolated OpenCode Drive run against this worktree, covering flowchart, sequence, state, timeline, and GitGraph Markdown fences ## Demo Real TUI rendering from this worktree with a simulated model response. The walkthrough shows five Mermaid diagram types; the opening flowchart is the reported oversized case using the new compact default. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f212ecd-7203-48ad-a9ba-57e513dee0fe
