signal.title: feat(core): make portable shell scanner authoritative
signal.text: ## What Reintroduce the portable Bash and PowerShell permission scanner behind the disabled-by-default `experimental.portable_shell_scanner` flag. When enabled, the portable scanner is authoritative: tree-sitter is neither loaded nor run. Supported syntax preserves the default scanner's ordered command resources, reusable save patterns, and inferred directories. Unsupported syntax requests normal shell authorization for the untouched command and infers no external directories. ## Before / After **Before** The previous scanner replacement treated a static heredoc as opaque, converted that uncertainty into an unknown directory, and requested `external_directory: "*"`. A scoped external-directory deny then blocked the command even when shell access was allowed. The first guarded version of this PR avoided that regression by always running tree-sitter and using it as a runtime fallback. **After** With the experiment enabled, OpenCode uses only the portable scanner. Opaque input is authorized as the original shell command and never invents an external-directory wildcard. With the experiment disabled, the existing tree-sitter path is unchanged. ## How - `packages/schema` and Core config normalization add the opt-in experimental flag. - `packages/core/src/shell/parse.ts` branches before tree-sitter initialization and adapts portable structural output into legacy-compatible ordered resources, source-shaped save patterns, and directories. - `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/shell.ts` selects the portable path from effective config while preserving the default. - `packages/shell-scan` scans static Bash and PowerShell command positions, marks unsupported syntax opaque, and preserves nested-command discovery order. - `packages/core/test/shell-parse-parity.test.ts` compares 21,863 deterministic supported cases directly against tree-sitter. - Disposable research scripts and their CI steps were removed from the shipped package. ## Scope - Does not remove or change the default tree-sitter scanner. - Does not use tree-sitter as a compatibility check or runtime fallback when the experiment is enabled. - Does not infer directories from opaque commands. - Does not add wildcard authorization for uncertain paths. - Does not change ordered last-match-wins permission evaluation. ## Testing - Bounded differential search: 330,667 Bash and PowerShell programs; 329,803 supported scans; 864 intentionally opaque; 0 supported mismatches. - Real-shell dispatch check: 3,275 generated programs on Bash 5.3, Bash 3.2, and zsh 5.9; 0 missing dispatched commands. - `packages/core`: `bun run test` (1,761 passed, 16 skipped), `bun typecheck`. - `packages/shell-scan`: `bun run test` (274 passed), `bun typecheck`. - Changed files: Prettier check and `git diff --check` pass. - Repository-wide `bun run lint` and `bun run lint:effect-patterns` remain red on pre-existing unrelated diagnostics; targeted Oxlint reports 0 errors. ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Shell invocation] --> B{portable_shell_scanner?} B -- false --> C[Load and run tree-sitter] B -- true --> D[Run portable scanner] D --> E{Supported syntax?} E -- yes --> F[Authorize compatible command resources and directories] E -- no --> G[Authorize untouched shell command] G --> H[Infer no directories] C --> I[Apply ordered permission rules] F --> I H --> I ```

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Show subagent start time and execution duration
signal.text: **Description:** It would be very useful to display timing information for subagent calls in the UI. Currently, when multiple subagents are invoked, it can be difficult to understand **when each subagent was started** and **how long it took to complete**, especially when several agents are running or being delegated in sequence. ### Proposed enhancement For each subagent invocation, display: * **Invocation time** — when the subagent was started. * **Execution duration** — how long the subagent took to complete. * Optionally, **completion time** as well, if it fits naturally into the existing UI. For example, the UI could show something similar to: ```text ▣ Delegators/Workers/Openai-Gpt-5.6-Luna/... 15:02:31 Completed in 42s ▣ General 15:03:14 Completed in 18s ▣ Code-Reviewers/Openai-Gpt-5.6-Luna/... 15:03:35 Completed in 1m 07s ``` This would make it much easier to understand the execution flow, identify slow subagents, and debug or analyze complex multi-agent workflows. ### Why this would be useful This information would help with: * understanding the timeline of agent/subagent execution; * identifying slow or unexpectedly long-running subagents; * debugging delegation and parallel execution; * comparing execution times between different agents; * getting a clearer picture of overall workflow performance. The timestamp could be displayed inline with the subagent call, while the duration could be added once the subagent finishes. ### Example ![Example of the proposed UI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99d97500-f35b-413e-9a44-f5c6cce6e374) I think even a minimal implementation showing the **start time + execution duration** would already provide a lot of value.

signal.title: "Snapshot mechanism stalls on large workspaces: ~1min per git snapshot, permanent index.lock deadlock after a crash"
signal.text: ### Description On a large git workspace (~5,300 tracked files) running opencode 1.18.18 on Windows, the **project snapshot mechanism** becomes pathological: 1. Every agentic iteration triggers a full `git add -A` + `git commit` inside a custom snapshot repository. On a large workspace each of these takes **~1 minute** (`git add -A` ≈ 57s, `git commit` ≈ 19s measured locally), so **every single model interaction is blocked for ~1 minute before anything is sent**. 2. When a snapshot git process crashes (or is killed), it leaves a stale `index.lock` in the snapshot repository. From then on, **every snapshot operation fails with `fatal: Unable to create '...index.lock': File exists`** and opencode retries indefinitely — memory balloons to 6–8 GB, disk reads exceed 10 GB, and no response is ever produced. The only fix is to manually delete the `index.lock` file. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a large repo (several thousand tracked files) in opencode on Windows. 2. Verify the snapshot git repo under `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/<projectID>/...`: - Run `git add -A` in that repo → observe tens of seconds. - Run `git commit` → same. 3. Trigger a snapshot operation and then kill the opencode process mid-operation → a stale `index.lock` is left behind. 4. Restart opencode in the same directory → every interaction now logs: ``` WARN level=WARN message="failed to add snapshot files" exitCode=128 stderr="fatal: Unable to create '.../snapshot/.../index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to be running in this repository..." ``` The session becomes unresponsive: ~6–8 GB RSS, continually increasing disk reads, and no answer is returned, because snapshot never succeeds and opencode retries forever. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System windows ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: feat(tui): refine question form interactions
signal.text: ## What Refines the V2 TUI question form so structured questions remain comfortable for real review and planning workflows: - custom answers edit in place instead of rendering a duplicate row - typing or pasting on the custom option opens the editor directly, including fast multi-word input - multiselect choices support Space as an unadvertised checkbox toggle while Enter remains the documented action - focus and selection use independent colors: focus owns the row treatment, selection owns the green check - Up leaves a custom editor only from its first visual line - confirmation drops the redundant Review heading and sizes wrapped summaries by rendered content - field tabs use the same quiet text hierarchy as adjacent bottom panels, with exact two-cell spacing and no status glyph clutter ## Before / After **Before** 1. Activating a custom answer rendered a second textarea below the original option. 2. Fast typing during the editor mount could lose or reorder input. 3. Committing a custom multiselect answer could produce an additional numbered row. 4. Focused and selected choices used competing blue treatments, making checked state difficult to scan. 5. Confirmation assumed one terminal row per field, clipping wrapped values, always advertising scroll, or expanding to the full terminal height. **After** 1. The custom option itself becomes the editor and remains one stable option after commit. 2. Input is buffered until the inline textarea actually owns renderer focus, including spaces in a fast typing burst. 3. Focus remains the blue row treatment while the checkmark independently communicates selection in success green. 4. Confirmation measures rendered rows, grows only for wrapping, and offers scrolling only after reaching the available viewport cap. ## How - `packages/tui/src/routes/session/form.tsx` owns direct custom typing/paste, inline editing, Space toggling, boundary navigation, orthogonal colors, injected reply/cancel callbacks, and measured review layout. - `packages/tui/test/cli/tui/form.test.tsx` covers paste, burst typing, multi-word custom input, duplicate-row prevention, Space semantics, Up-boundary behavior, compact confirmation, and wrapped review sizing. - `AGENTS.md` records the reusable workflow for future fixture-driven V2 TUI stories without shipping this task's one-off story. ## Scope Image attachments in form responses remain follow-up work tracked by #31791. signal.title: fix(tui): debounce shared storage reloads
signal.text: ## What Make filesystem-backed TUI state converge reliably across concurrent TUI processes, and keep the foreground-only unread-state regression test focused on that behavior. ## Before / After **Before:** an atomic write could notify the directory watcher while its temporary file was being created. The watcher immediately reloaded the old target file, and Linux could coalesce the final rename notification. A second TUI then kept stale tab or unread state indefinitely; increasing the test deadline did not help. **After:** storage reloads are debounced until the short atomic-write event burst settles, so readers observe the committed JSON target. The unread test starts from persisted shared tabs, separating startup tab creation from unread propagation, and reports the exact failed phase. ## How - `packages/tui/src/context/storage.tsx` debounces directory watcher reloads by 50ms and clears the pending reload during cleanup. - `packages/tui/test/context/session-tabs.test.tsx` seeds both tabs before rendering concurrent TUIs, keeps longer deadlines only around cross-process propagation, and labels timeout phases. ## Scope This does not address unrelated `dialog-open` render or CLI service-registration timeouts observed in separate CI attempts. ## Testing - 200/200 targeted runs under 30-way process contention - `bun run test` in `packages/tui` (697 passed, 5 skipped) - `bun typecheck` in `packages/tui` - repository pre-push typecheck (34 tasks passed) ## Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant A as Foreground TUI participant FS as Atomic JSON storage participant B as Background TUI A->>FS: Write temporary file and rename target FS-->>B: Directory event burst B->>B: Debounce reload for 50ms B->>FS: Read committed target FS-->>B: Current shared state ```

signal.title: question tool not broadcast via SSE / GET /api/question/request always empty (V2)
signal.text: ## Bug: question tool not broadcast via SSE / /api/question/request always empty (V2) ### Environment - opencode server version: `0.0.0-next-17403` and `0.0.0-next-17430` (both tested) - Client: Android app (OC Beacon) using the V2 REST + SSE protocol ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start opencode server (V2, any recent next build) 2. Ask the agent to call the `question` tool (e.g. "please use the question tool to ask me a multiple choice question") 3. The agent's tool call appears in the session: `{type: 'tool', name: 'question', executed: false, state: {status: 'running', input: {...}}}` 4. The tool remains `running` forever — waiting for the client to answer ### Expected behavior - When the agent calls the question tool, the server should broadcast a `question.asked` SSE event and/or expose the pending question via `GET /api/question/request` - The client should be able to see and answer the pending question ### Actual behavior - `GET /api/question/request` **always returns empty data** `{"data":[]}` even while the question tool is `running` - **No `question.asked` SSE event is ever broadcast** (captured the SSE stream for 15+ seconds — only `server.connected` and `server.heartbeat` arrive) - The client can never see or answer the question; the tool stays stuck in `running` until aborted ### Notes - Same behavior on both next-17403 and next-17430 - The V1 server (1.18.x) works correctly: `GET /question` returns the pending question and the client can answer it - This blocks any client (mobile/web) that relies on the REST/SSE protocol from handling question cards ### Additional context Client-side impact documented at https://github.com/LeoNardo-LB/oc-beacon (backlog #130): question cards never render on V2 because the server never announces them.

signal.title: catalog: models without declared capabilities default to image input support
signal.text: ## Summary Models without declared capabilities are defaulted to image input support (`capabilities.input: ["text", "image"]`), so text-only models on custom providers are sent image attachments, which their providers reject with HTTP 400. Plugins reading the catalog (e.g. opencode-eyesight) are also misled into treating those models as vision-capable. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-next-17444 - OS: macOS 25.5.0 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64) - Terminal: Apple_Terminal, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: next - Active plugins: `superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git`, `/Users/bankja/projects/opencode-eyesight` (local dev) ## Reproduction 1. Use a V1-format `opencode.json` with a custom provider (`npm: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, e.g. `wd` in the example below) whose model declares **no** `modalities`: ```jsonc { "provider": { "wd": { "name": "MY LOCAL AI", "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "models": { "Deepseek-V4-Flash": { "name": "Deepseek-V4-Flash", "options": { "temperature": 1.0 } } } } } } ``` 2. Start `opencode2` with a session using `wd/Deepseek-V4-Flash`. 3. Attach an image (`@`-mention a file or paste) and send the message. ## Expected Behavior The catalog should report only capabilities the model actually declares. A model with no `modalities`/`tool_call` should not be presented as image-capable, so the runner does not send image parts to it and plugins can rely on `capabilities.input`. ## Actual Behavior - `GET /api/model` reports `caps: {"tools": true, "input": ["text", "image"], "output": ["text"]}` for the model. - The session request includes the image, and the provider rejects it: `Error: Provider request failed with HTTP 400` (finish: `error`), with the error `Provider request failed with HTTP 400` surfaced on the assistant message. ## Additional Context The default comes from `Model.Info.default` in `packages/schema/src/model.ts` (`capabilities: { tools: true, input: ["text", "image"], output: ["text"] }`), which the catalog applies when creating model entries (`packages/core/src/catalog.ts`, model `update`). V1-config migration leaves `capabilities` undefined when the model declares no `tool_call`/`modalities` (`packages/core/src/v1/config/migrate.ts`), after which the default triple kicks in. Explicit declarations are honored — models with `modalities: { input: ["text", "image"] }` normalize to `tools: false` with the declared input. Consequences observed: - Runner forwards the image to a text-only model → provider HTTP 400 on every image message. - Plugins that gate on `catalog.model.list()` capabilities (e.g. opencode-eyesight's vision fallback) skip transcription and pass the image through. Workarounds: - Declare explicit `modalities` (`{ "input": ["text"], "output": ["text"] }`) on text-only models. - (Plugin-side) treat the exact default triple as "unknown" rather than image support. Suggested fix: default models without declared capabilities to text-only (`input: ["text"]`, `tools` unchanged), or leave capabilities empty instead of asserting image support that the provider may not honor.

signal.title: fix(cli): stop `run` from sleeping through an exhausted quota
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #40747 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `opencode run` produces no output and never returns when a model's quota is exhausted. It isn't wedged, it's sleeping. The quota error is classified as retryable, and `delay()` honors the provider's `retry-after`, which for a monthly limit is days. While the schedule sleeps `halt()` never runs, so no `session.error` and no `idle` are published, and `loop()` in `cli/cmd/run.ts` breaks only on `idle` and has no branch for `retry` status. The TUI is unaffected because it shows the retry in its footer; a headless run has nowhere to show it. I left the retry timing alone — honoring long `retry-after` values was deliberate in 0a2d7af17, and waiting out a short rate limit is useful. Only the non-interactive loop changes: - print the retry status, which today prints nothing at all in headless runs - exit non-zero when `action.reason` is `free_tier_limit` / `account_rate_limit`; transient retries (429/5xx) carry no `action.reason` and still wait and retry as before - abort the session before returning, because breaking out of the loop isn't enough to end the process — the sleeping schedule holds the in-process server open, and without the abort the CLI has decided to stop but still has to be killed ### How did you verify your code works? New test in `test/cli/run/run-process.test.ts`: the test provider returns a 429 carrying `GoUsageLimitError` with `retry-after: 345600`, and the run must exit non-zero and mention the limit on stderr. On unmodified `dev` it hangs until the harness kills it at 30 s; with this change it passes in ~2 s. Setting that header needed an optional `headers` argument on `httpError()` / `llm.error()` in the test harness — `retry-after` drives the delay and there was no way to set it before. `bun test test/session/retry.test.ts test/cli/run/` → 250 pass, 5 skip, 0 fail. `tsc --noEmit` → matches the `dev` baseline (12 pre-existing errors in `packages/tui`). ### Screenshots / recordings Not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: Run loop can never exit when message ids are not time-sortable (imported sessions loop until the provider 400s)
signal.text: ### Summary `SessionPrompt.runLoop` decides a turn is finished by comparing message ids as **plain strings**. That is only correct because opencode's own ids embed a timestamp. Any session whose ids do not sort chronologically — e.g. one produced by a third-party importer — can put the loop in a state where it never exits: opencode re-requests indefinitely, each request ending on an assistant message, which providers reject. On Anthropic the user-visible result is a generic `Unexpected server error`, with the real cause (`This model does not support assistant message prefill`) buried. ### Where `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, in `runLoop`: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // <-- lexicographic id comparison ) { yield* Effect.logInfo("exiting loop", { "session.id": sessionID }) break } ``` `MessageV2.latest()` selects the "last" user/assistant the same way. The invariant this relies on comes from `packages/schema/src/identifier.ts`: ids are a 12-hex-char prefix encoding `timestamp_ms * 0x1000 + counter`, plus 14 random chars — so they sort chronologically as strings. Nothing validates that invariant at the `import` boundary, and it is not documented in the `SessionV1` schema. ### Reproduction 1. Import a session whose message ids are random rather than time-sortable (I hit this with [baton](https://github.com/Kaseban/baton), which emitted `msg_<uuid>`; a hand-written JSON with random ids reproduces it too). 2. Resume it and send any prompt. 3. The first request succeeds. opencode then immediately issues a second request with the assistant's own reply appended, and the provider returns 400. Captured with a forwarding proxy in front of the provider: ``` req 1: 1035312B -> 200 OK response: "stop_reason":"end_turn" + "message_stop" req 2: 1035378B -> 400 "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message." ``` The first response is a clean, complete turn — `end_turn`, `message_stop` — and opencode continues anyway. Failure is probabilistic in session length, because ~2.6% of random hex ids sort above a freshly generated native id: | messages | P(at least one imported id outranks the live ones) | observed | |---|---|---| | 3 | ~8% | worked | | 6 | ~15% | worked once, failed once | | 423 | ~100% | failed every attempt | Ruled out by testing, in case they look like suspects: plugins (reproduced with `--pure`), missing `step-start`/`step-finish` parts (synthesised them, no change), unpaired `tool_use`, unsigned thinking blocks, and empty message content. It reproduces with a structurally valid history — I replayed the exact captured payload standalone and it returned 200. ### Suggested fixes Either would resolve it; the first is the smaller change: 1. **Order by `time.created`** (falling back to id) in the loop test and in `MessageV2.latest()`, instead of comparing id strings. 2. **Break on a terminal finish reason regardless of ordering** — if `lastAssistant.finish === "stop"` and there are no pending tool calls, the turn is over; the id comparison is then only a tiebreaker. Worth considering alongside: a continuation request that would end on an assistant message is invalid for providers that disallow prefill, so guarding that at the request-building layer would turn this class of bug into a clear error rather than a loop. ### Related - #38620 — same seam (replay 400 with thinking + tool use) but a different trigger (`message.error !== undefined`); does not cover id ordering. - #21326, #25774 — orphaned/dangling `tool_use`; also this area, different cause. ### Environment opencode 1.18.4 · macOS arm64 (container, linux/arm64) · Anthropic-compatible endpoint (LiteLLM), `claude-opus-4-8`, `thinking: adaptive`. ### Note on the provider side Not an opencode bug, but it made diagnosis much harder: when the upstream rejected the request, the gateway's fallback chain retried on models that do not support `thinking: adaptive`, so both the original and fallback errors were collapsed into one opaque message. Surfacing the provider's `error.message` verbatim in the session log would have saved a lot of time here.
signal.author: dkindlund

signal.title: Scripted-exec endpoint is authorised to every authenticated user
signal.text: `shared/scripted-exec.ts` installs a scripted REST operation that evaluates server-side script. The operation is created with six fields and no authorisation settings, so ServiceNow authenticates the caller and then permits **any** authenticated user on the instance. `GlideEvaluator.evaluateString` does not enforce ACLs, so reaching the endpoint is equivalent to admin. Three things make it worse than a normal permission gap: - The artefact is permanent. It is never removed, and it stays on production instances. - Seven tools plant it, one of them (`snow_create_ui_policy`) unconditionally on every call — so it can appear on an instance where nobody asked for script execution. - `update-set-guard.ts` exempts the `script-execution` subcategory, so there is no update set to back it out with. Because the artefact already exists on instances that ran an older version, the fix has to repair as well as prevent. **Scope of exposure known to us:** only our own PDI. Two orgs ever invoked a planting tool through the platform and both resolve to `dev380262`. Anyone running the CLI over stdio or self-hosted is not visible to us and cannot be counted.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Agent Activity Panel -- sidebar view for monitoring running background agents
signal.text: ## Summary When orchestrating multiple background agents in parallel (e.g., `explore`, `librarian`, `oracle`), there's currently no way to monitor their status without calling `background_output()` manually. A dedicated sidebar/panel showing live agent activity would greatly improve visibility into multi-agent workflows. ## Problem Right now, when agents are spawned with `run_in_background=true`, the user has zero visibility into: - **How many agents** are currently running - **What each agent is doing** (task description / current step) - **Their status** (running / completed / failed) - **Their partial output** (live progress) The only way to check is to wait for a system notification and then call `background_output(task_id="...")` -- which is a pull-based, reactive model with no live visibility. ## Proposed Solution Add an **Agent Activity Panel** in the sidebar (similar to a CI/CD pipeline view) that shows all background agents with their real-time status. ### Mockup ``` +- Agents ──────────────────────────────+ | | | 🟡 explore "Find auth patterns…" | <- click to expand | 🟡 librarian "JWT security docs…" | <- click to expand | ✅ oracle "Architecture review" | <- click to see output | ❌ explore "Find error handlers" | <- click to see error | | +───────────────────────────────────────+ ``` ### Clicking an agent entry expands to show: - Full task description / prompt - Live streaming output (if still running) - Final result (if completed) - Error details (if failed) - Start time + elapsed duration ## User Story > As a power user running complex multi-agent workflows, I want to see all active background agents in the sidebar at a glance, so I can monitor their progress and click into any agent to view real-time output -- without having to wait for completion notifications. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Sidebar panel lists all background agents spawned in the current session - [ ] Each entry shows: agent type, task description snippet, status icon (running / done / failed) - [ ] Clicking an entry opens a detail view with full output - [ ] Running agents show live/streaming output as it arrives - [ ] Panel updates in real-time (no manual refresh needed) - [ ] Completed/failed agents remain visible (dismissible) ## Context This is especially valuable for workflows where 3-5 agents run in parallel (e.g., parallel codebase exploration + external docs research + architecture consultation). Currently the UX feels like "fire and forget" with no control panel. Related to the overall goal of making multi-agent orchestration more transparent and manageable from the UI.

signal.title: [BUG] Desktop: conversation freezes mid-"thinking", no error, must abort and resend — missing watchdog/retry UX
signal.text: ## Description On the **Windows desktop app**, quite often — especially with models that do long/reasoning "thinking" (e.g. OpenAI/DeepSeek-style reasoning dumps) — the conversation **freezes mid-thinking**: the agent is stuck in "thinking" state, spinner/tool call never resolves, and no output arrives. The only workaround is to **abort/terminate the conversation and resend the message** (losing the reasoning context), which is disruptive for long debugging tasks. ## Details of the bug 1. User sends a prompt (sometimes after long thinking, sometimes right at start). 2. Client shows "thinking…" (or the thinking block dumps) indefinitely; the stream silently stops; no error toast. 3. UI (desktop) is stuck; user must hit the abort/stop button and resent the exact same prompt; then it usually works — pointing to a **transient stream/connection race**, not the model being slow. ## Associated issues (other symptoms, same "thinking stuck" family) - #36370 (Desktop stuck in "thinking" - sidecar stream never completes, Windows) - #37609 (Plan/Build mode sometimes hangs after long reasoning, never emits final response) - #38951 (API 404 silently hangs in thinking state, no error recovery) - #32366 (UI stuck on thinking indefinitely after stream error, no error displayed) - #38644 (provider 500 drops response without showing error) - #41069 (previously closed as duplicate of #37617 — free-tier model network blips treated as normal; user on this session reported similar) ## Suggested improvements 1. **Watchdog / timeout on the thinking phase**: if no chunks received for N seconds (e.g. 60s), surface an explicit error/info banner ("model hasn't responded; retry?") and offer "retry with cached thinking". 2. **Recover stuck turn automatically**: detect stuck state and prompt user "Retry / discard and re-ask" instead of silently dangling. 3. **Show provider error in the UI** (many of these are provider 5xx/empty chunk cases): single toast for "provider error, auto-retried". 4. **Non-lossy retry**: when user aborts+resends, keep the previous reasoning/tool output as context so the retry isn't blind. This is a frequent occurrence (dozens of similar reports) and the UX cost is high for long sessions.

signal.title: [FEATURE]:Frontend UI extensibility for plugins (Custom Settings & Dialogs)
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Currently, the @opencode-ai/plugin architecture is exclusively backend-focused (Node/Bun). While it provides excellent support for intercepting lifecycle hooks, registering commands/tools, and modifying configurations, it completely lacks mechanisms for frontend UI extensibility. A concrete example of this limitation arises when attempting to refactor the built-in experimental war agent into a standalone plugin to clean up the core codebase. The backend logic and prompts can be successfully migrated via the config hook. However, the plugin loses its dedicated settings UI (dialog-war-config.tsx) and specific trigger buttons (prompt-input.tsx) because plugins cannot currently inject custom SolidJS components or HTML into the frontend. The only workaround right now is hardcoding agent-specific UI logic directly into the core packages/app repository. This tightly couples the code and defeats the purpose of having a modular plugin system. Furthermore, while MCP (Model Context Protocol) is fantastic for exposing tools and context, it does not address these client-side UI rendering limitations. ### Describe the solution you'd like I would love to see a frontend extensibility mechanism introduced into the plugin architecture. Here are a few potential approaches, ranging from highly flexible to highly secure: Micro-frontend / Dynamic Component Loading: Allow plugins to bundle a ui.js module that exports standard SolidJS components or Web Components. The core app could dynamically import() these and provide specific mounting points (e.g., registerSettingsTab, registerAgentConfigDialog). Iframe / WebView Injection (Safest & Simplest): Allow plugins to expose an endpoint or a static HTML file. The frontend could provide a hook like registerWebviewPanel(id, url) and render an <iframe> within the settings dialog or side panel. This ensures complete decoupling and sandbox security. Schema-driven UI Generation: If running arbitrary third-party code on the frontend is a security concern, plugins could return a JSON Schema describing their required configuration fields (e.g., dropdowns for commanderModel, editModel). The frontend could then dynamically render a generic, native-looking form based on this schema. ### Describe alternatives you've considered Modifying .opencode.json directly: Users have to manually edit the JSON file to change plugin-specific settings. This offers a significantly poorer user experience compared to native UI dropdowns and toggles. Tool-based configuration: Exposing a configure_agent tool and asking the AI to change the settings for the user. While functional, it is much slower and less deterministic than a simple UI interaction. Forking the repository: Maintaining a hardcoded fork of packages/app strictly to preserve custom UI components for proprietary or experimental agents. ### Additional context Frontend UI extensibility is the missing piece for a truly modular Opencode ecosystem. Implementing this would empower developers to build rich, interactive plugins—such as custom agent dashboards, specialized workflow visualizations, and seamless third-party integrations—without perpetually bloating the core application repository.

signal.title: fix(tui): preserve background hint timing
signal.text: ## What Keep the `ctrl+b` background-tool hint tied to how long the tool has been running, rather than how long the current tab view has been mounted. ## Before / After **Before:** A shell or subagent showed the hint after one second, but switching away from its tab unmounted the hint state. Returning to the tab restarted the full delay and temporarily hid the hint even when the tool had already been running for much longer. **After:** The hint waits only for the remainder of the tool's first second. Returning to a tab after that threshold shows it immediately. ## How - `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx` derives the running tool's start time from `time.ran`, falling back to `time.created`, and computes the remaining delay from its age. - `packages/tui/src/util/delayed-presence.ts` accepts either a fixed delay or a per-value delay while preserving cancellation when the source changes or disappears. - Equivalent running-tool updates retain the original timer; a different tool starts a delay based on its own age. ## Scope This only changes hint timing. The shortcut, eligible tool types, text, and background action are unchanged. ## Testing - `cd packages/tui && bun run test` (699 passed, 5 skipped) - `cd packages/tui && bun typecheck` - Pre-push `bun turbo typecheck --concurrency=3` (34 packages passed) - `bunx prettier --check src/routes/session/index.tsx src/util/delayed-presence.ts test/util/delayed-presence.test.ts` ## Demo No visual artifact: the rendered hint is unchanged; this fixes its remount timing and is covered by deterministic delayed-presence regression tests.

signal.title: refactor(cli): replace updater semver dependency
signal.text: ## What Replace the CLI updater’s general-purpose `semver` runtime dependency with a 50-line release-version action module tailored to the updater’s actual decisions: strict validity, equality, and major extraction. The update behavior remains unchanged: invalid or equal versions do nothing, major changes do nothing, and every other same-major difference upgrades, including rollbacks and prerelease transitions. ## Impact | Measurement | Before | After | Impact | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Bun macOS arm64 CLI binary | 150,530,402 B | 150,464,354 B | -66,048 B | | Node CLI bundle | 26,134,396 B | 26,100,903 B | -33,493 B | | Node CLI bundle, gzip | 10,502,124 B | 10,492,634 B | -9,490 B | | CLI direct `semver` runtime edge | `semver@7.7.4` | none | removed | | CLI direct `@types/semver` edge | `@types/semver@7.7.1` | none | removed | | `--version` startup median, 20 runs | 513.3 ms | 516.9 ms | no measurable change within noise | Artifact measurements use paired builds from untouched `origin/v2` and this branch with fixed `OPENCODE_VERSION=1.18.18` and `OPENCODE_CHANNEL=next`. `semver` remains in the workspace for unrelated packages and root release tooling; this removes only the CLI’s direct dependency and bundled updater usage. ## How - Add `packages/cli/src/services/updater-action.ts` with the updater policy and a narrow strict release-version parser. - Preserve `semver.valid` limits: 256 input characters, strict SemVer identifiers, and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` bounds for major/minor/patch. - Keep major values as decimal strings, avoiding precision loss during extraction and comparison. - Normalize optional lowercase `v`, surrounding whitespace, and build metadata exactly as the existing updater action does. - Preserve `semver.eq`’s existing oversized numeric prerelease behavior, including IEEE-754 collisions such as `9007199254740992` and `9007199254740993` comparing equal. - Remove the CLI package’s direct `semver` and `@types/semver` declarations and update `bun.lock`. Release producers were checked: stable builds emit plain `x.y.z`; preview builds emit `0.0.0-<channel>-<build>[.<attempt>]`. The update service accepts a broader opaque version token, so the parser intentionally preserves the full strict `semver@7.7.4` validity surface rather than narrowing to only currently produced strings. ## Scope This does not change update policy, rollback behavior, release ordering, polling, installation-method detection, upgrade commands, the update API, or non-CLI `semver` dependencies. This supersedes #42470 by removing the updater dependency instead of loading it lazily. ## Differential Evidence A temporary deterministic oracle test compared the proposed action directly with exact `semver@7.7.4` for 328,869 assertions. It covered standard releases, `v` and whitespace handling, rejected `=`/uppercase prefixes, generated core/prerelease/build products, OpenCode `next` versions, dotted identifiers, build-insensitive equality, leading zeros, safe-integer boundaries, oversized numeric prereleases, malformed strings, rollback pairs, adjacent corpus pairs, and 100,000 seeded random strings up to 279 characters. The oracle test was removed after verification so `semver` is not retained as a CLI dependency. ## Testing - `bun run test src/services/updater.test.ts` (11 passed) - Temporary differential corpus against exact `semver@7.7.4` (328,869 assertions passed) - `bun run typecheck` - `OPENCODE_VERSION=1.18.18 OPENCODE_CHANNEL=next bun run build --skip-web-ui` (all 12 native targets) - `OPENCODE_VERSION=1.18.18 OPENCODE_CHANNEL=next bun run build:node --bundle-only --skip-install` (`--version` and `--help` smoke checks passed) - `bunx prettier --check src/services/updater-action.ts src/services/updater.ts src/services/updater.test.ts package.json` - `.husky/pre-push` (35 workspace typechecks passed) - Full CLI suite: 188 passed; the same three unrelated process/service tests fail on untouched `origin/v2` and this branch (`test/service.test.ts`, `test/standalone.test.ts`, `test/acp/command.test.ts`)

signal.title: fix(provider): fix Vertex AI multi-region location producing invalid hostname
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #37006 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Fixes the Vertex AI provider building an invalid hostname (`us-aiplatform.googleapis.com`) when `location` is set to a continental multi-region value like `us` or `eu`. Only `global` was treated as not needing a region prefix; `us`/`eu` need the same treatment. Two separate places had this bug and both needed fixing: 1. The endpoint-template helper used for the OpenAI-compatible Vertex path (in both the legacy provider loader and the newer plugin system) only special-cased `global`. 2. opencode also calls `@ai-sdk/google-vertex`'s `createVertex()` directly for the native SDK path, and that package has the identical bug in its own default `baseURL` computation. Since we can't fix the dependency here, we pass `baseURL` explicitly to override its broken default. The legacy `provider.ts` fix had to be scoped carefully in `resolveSDK` (only for `npm === "@ai-sdk/google-vertex"`, not the `/anthropic` variant) because the existing Claude-on-Vertex code path already relies on `options.baseURL` being unset to trigger its own REP-endpoint override — setting a `baseURL` unconditionally there would have broken that. I did generate this code using AI, but I did review. I am not normally writing typescript so it certainly is not my forte, but nothing stuck out to me as incorrect in the code generation. The above summary text was AI generated, but it does seem to accurately reflect the changes and the issue based on my review. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added/updated unit tests in both `packages/core` and `packages/opencode` asserting the exact constructed `baseURL`/endpoint string for `us`, `eu`, and regular single-region locations (e.g. `us-central1`), for both the OpenAI-compatible and native SDK paths. - Ran the full test suites: `packages/core` (1077 passing) and `packages/opencode` (3168 passing), no regressions. - I manually reproduced the original error against a real Vertex-backed project with `location: "us"` and confirmed the request now succeeds with the updated code using bun dev with the same configuration that failed on the released 1.18.1 OpenCode I'm a little unsure about the version in the uri, the sdk shows v1beta1. Additionally the path now includes ../publishers/google. I'm unable to test other models at the moment other than Gemini and Anthropic models, but those models did work after these changes. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: refactor(tui): rebuild tab pulse on gated envelopes
signal.text: ## What Behavior-preserving refactor of the tab pulse animation core, follow-up to #42487. The tab pulse is, structurally, a small synthesizer voice: each visual stage is a temporal envelope times a spatial profile times a color, mixed in a fixed order. This PR names that structure instead of hand-coordinating envelopes. | before | after (synthesis vocabulary) | |---|---| | `runAttack` + `runFade` + manual clock, coordinated in `setActive` | one `GatedEnvelope`: trigger → attack → sustain, release fades from the note-off level | | `ignition` + `glowOff` + `release`, coordinated in `setGlow` | one `GatedEnvelope`: ignition is the attack, the 200ms drain is the release shape, the diffusion swell rides `releaseProgress` | | `glowLevel` / `running` branching getters | `.level` (phase-aware) | | `edgeFlash`, `completionPulse` | unchanged one-shot `Envelope`s (drum hits, not gated voices) | ## How `packages/tui/src/component/tab-pulse.tsx` only: - `GatedEnvelope` — a gated stage with `trigger()` / `release()` / `settle()`, phase-aware `level`, `releaseProgress`, and `noteOffLevel`. Sustain is motionless, so only attack and release count as `animating`; a held glow stays non-live exactly as before. - `PulseState` shrinks from six coordinated envelopes to two gated voices (`runEnvelope`, `glowEnvelope`) plus two one-shots. `setActive` / `setGlow` become gate edges; the completion-pending handshake keeps its bespoke sequencing. The sweep clock stays in `PulseState` (it is a spatial concern, not an envelope one) and its `fronts` tuple is reused scratch, so the steady-state render allocates nothing. - The glow release unifies the old drain + diffusion pair: `glowEnvelope.level` carries the draining residue (same 200ms shape via `GLOW_RELEASE_DRAIN_FRACTION`), and `PulseState.glowReleaseSwell` yields the diffusion amplitude that `renderSelf` pairs with `glowReleaseSpread`, computed per row only while releasing. ## Behavior notes One deliberate, invisible-in-practice detail preserved from before: with animations disabled, glow changes settle instantly to their static level via `settle()`. Re-enabling animations restarts the run attack but resumes the sweep from its prior position, exactly as the old code did. ## Scope - No prop or consumer changes; `session-tabs.tsx` untouched. - The `unit (linux)` CI failure ("only the foreground TUI mutates unread state", a 2s wait timeout) is preexisting on `v2` and fails there identically; it passes locally on every run. ## Testing - `bun typecheck` in `packages/tui` - `bun run test test/component/tab-pulse.test.tsx test/context/session-tabs.test.tsx` — 17 pass, including the held-glow liveness and disabled-pulse invariants - End-to-end in the tabs story: sweep, prompt flash, glow ignition, held glow, diffuse resolve, completion pulse, and error/activity hues all verified against the pre-refactor recordings - Post-review simplification pass (three parallel reviewers: reuse, quality, efficiency); fixes folded in and re-verified ## Demo Real story run on this branch: run sweep, unread glow, diffuse resolve on select, completion pulse. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0bcf3e6-058a-4eb0-a62a-379eefebfd1a

signal.title: [FEATURE]: allow user to inject custom instruction when compacting a session
signal.text:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Problem When a session is compacted, the LLM generates a structured summary of the conversation. However, the user has no way to provide per-compaction guidance — e.g., what to prioritize in the summary, what information is no longer relevant, or what the next work focus should be. The existing `experimental.session.compacting` plugin hook can inject context into the compaction prompt, but: - It only receives `{ sessionID }` — no per-invocation dynamic input - The injected content is static (determined by plugin code), not changeable per compaction Additionally, the recent conversation that the user might use to convey such guidance is often excluded from the compaction scope (it falls into the "recent" portion that is preserved verbatim), so the compaction LLM never sees it. ## Proposal Allow the user to pass an optional `instruction` string when triggering a compaction, which gets appended to the compaction LLM prompt. ### Suggested changes 1. **API layer** — Add `instruction?: string` to `SummarizePayload` (`packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/session.ts`) 2. **Handler** — Pass `instruction` through `compactSvc.create()` → `compaction.process()` (`packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts`) 3. **Compaction prompt** — Append the user instruction to the summary prompt in `processCompaction`: ```ts if (input.instruction) { nextPrompt += `

Additional user instruction for this compaction:
${input.instruction}` } 4. TUI — When the user triggers /compact (or <leader>c), show a DialogPrompt input box (already available at packages/tui/src/ui/dialog-prompt.tsx) with a placeholder like "Optional: guide the compaction (what to prioritize, what to drop)…". The user can type a one-liner or leave it empty and press Enter to proceed. Why - Per-compaction guidance is a common pattern in agent frameworks (e.g., Claude Code's /compact with optional instructions) - The change is minimal — one field threaded through 4 layers, each just passing it along - No breaking changes — instruction is optional; existing behavior is preserved when it's absent Context - Current compaction implementation: packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts (V1 path, actively used) - V2 core compaction (packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts) does not yet support plugin hooks; this proposal should be considered for both paths - DialogPrompt component already exists and is used by other commands (e.g., session rename, provider config)

signal.title: opencode session list hangs for ~2 minutes due to unnecessary full InstanceBootstrap
signal.text: ## Summary Running `opencode session list` blocks the terminal for approximately 2 minutes before showing results, even though the underlying SQL query completes in ~0.007 seconds. The root cause is that the command triggers a full `InstanceBootstrap` (config loading, plugin init, LSP startup, VCS init, file watchers, snapshot system, etc.) — all of which are unnecessary for a simple read-only database query. ## Environment - opencode version: 1.18.x (current `dev` branch) - Database: 94 sessions, SQLite WAL mode, 131 MB after VACUUM ## Steps to reproduce ```bash time opencode session list # Blocks for ~2 minutes before printing the session table ``` ## Root cause ### 1. `SessionListCommand` does not set `instance: false` `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/session.ts:70-86`: ```typescript export const SessionListCommand = effectCmd({ command: "list", describe: "list sessions", // ← missing `instance: false` builder: (yargs) => ... handler: Effect.fn("Cli.session.list")(function* (args) { const sessions = yield* Session.Service.use((svc) => svc.list(...)) ... }), }) ``` The `instance` option in `effectCmd` defaults to `true` (`packages/opencode/src/cli/effect-cmd.ts:46`): ```typescript /** * Whether the command needs a project InstanceContext. Defaults to true. * * `true` (default): ... Runs InstanceBootstrap (config + plugin * init + LSP/File/etc forks) eagerly. * * `false`: skip the instance entirely. ... Use `false` for commands * that don't read project state (e.g. `models`, `serve`, `web`, `account`, `db`, `upgrade`). */ instance?: boolean | ((args: Args) => boolean) ``` When `instance: true` (the default), `effectCmd` loads the full `InstanceStore`, which triggers `InstanceBootstrap.run`: `packages/opencode/src/project/bootstrap.ts:32-46`: ```typescript const run = Effect.gen(function* () { yield* config.get() // load configuration yield* plugin.init() // initialize plugins (can mutate config) yield* Effect.forEach( [lsp, shareNext, format, vcs, snapshot, project], (s) => s.init() // start LSP, file watchers, VCS, snapshot, etc. ... ) }) ``` This boots the entire opencode runtime — including starting language servers, file watchers, git monitors, snapshot system, share service, and formatting service — just to run a single `SELECT` query on the `session` table that takes **0.007 seconds**. ### 2. `Session.list()` requires `InstanceState.context` `packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:548-555`: ```typescript const list = Effect.fn("Session.list")(function* (input?: ListInput) { const ctx = yield* InstanceState.context // ← requires full instance return yield* listByProject(db, { projectID: ctx.project.id, // ← used for WHERE filter ... }) }) ``` Because `list()` yields `InstanceState.context` to get `ctx.project.id`, simply setting `instance: false` would cause a defect (the `InstanceRef` would be undefined). ### 3. Other commands already skip InstanceBootstrap Multiple commands correctly set `instance: false` and work fine: | Command | File | `instance` | |---------|------|-----------| | `db` | `db.ts:11` | `false` | | `account` (all subcommands) | `account.ts:180,195,210,220,230` | `false` | | `providers` | `providers.ts:253,500` | `false` | | `serve` | `serve.ts:12` | `false` | | `web` | `web.ts:37` | `false` | | **`session list`** | **`session.ts:70`** | **not set → defaults to `true`** ❌ | ### 4. Evidence that SQL is not the bottleneck ```sql -- Query plan shows indexed scan + temp sort (expected for ORDER BY without covering index) EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT * FROM session WHERE project_id=? AND parent_id IS NULL ORDER BY time_updated DESC LIMIT 100; -- |--SEARCH session USING INDEX session_project_idx (project_id=?) -- `--USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY -- Actual execution time: ~0.007 seconds ``` The database has 94 sessions, 3,806 messages, and 16,449 parts. The `session` table scan is trivially fast even without a covering index on `time_updated`. ## Proposed fix Two possible approaches: **Option A (simpler): Bypass `InstanceState` in the CLI handler** Modify `SessionListCommand` to set `instance: false` and query sessions directly via `Database.Service` + `directory` filter (instead of `project_id`), following the same pattern used by the `db` command: ```typescript export const SessionListCommand = effectCmd({ command: "list", instance: false, // ← ADD THIS ... handler: Effect.fn("Cli.session.list")(function* (args) { const { db } = yield* Database.Service const rows = yield* db .select() .from(SessionTable) .where(and( eq(SessionTable.directory, process.cwd()), isNull(SessionTable.parent_id) )) .orderBy(desc(SessionTable.time_updated)) .limit(args.maxCount ?? 100) .all() // ... format and output }), }) ``` **Option B: Add a lightweight `listByDirectory` method to the session service** Create a new method that doesn't require `InstanceState.context`, using `directory` as the filter key instead of `project_id`. ## Additional note The same issue likely affects `session delete` (same file, same missing `instance: false`), as well as the `stats` command which also queries sessions via the full InstanceBootstrap.

signal.title: OpenAI WebSocket 1009 retries the same oversized response.create five times before HTTP fallback
signal.text: ### Description With the OpenAI Responses WebSocket enabled, an oversized request containing base64 image tool outputs is deterministically rejected with: ``` ProviderResponseStreamError: WebSocket closed before response.completed (code 1009: message too big) ``` OpenCode retries the same oversized WebSocket request five times with backoff before falling back to HTTP. The session therefore appears stuck for about a minute and repeats a request that cannot succeed over that transport. Cancelling or restarting before fallback starts the cycle again. The session eventually recovered over HTTP and then compacted, so this report is about delayed recovery and unnecessary retries, not permanent data loss. In the observed session, one tool round read six 1920x1080 PNG files. Their base64 data URLs totaled 17,390,364 bytes. Including an image from the immediately preceding round, the request history contained 19,895,594 bytes of image data before JSON overhead. The next model request produced five consecutive code 1009 failures. In v1.18.18, the complete `response.create` payload is sent as one WebSocket message: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.18/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts#L289-L295 Code 1009 is currently only annotated as `message too big`: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.18/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts#L350-L354 Expected behavior: code 1009 should immediately bypass WebSocket and retry once over HTTP, or OpenCode should preflight the serialized payload size and use HTTP for oversized requests. It should not replay the same known-too-large WebSocket message five times. Related issues: - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/14562 covers the same base64-image root cause through HTTP 413 and compaction, but not WebSocket code 1009 or delayed HTTP fallback. - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29646 covers generic early WebSocket disconnects (for example transient code 1006). Code 1009 is deterministic and should trigger immediate transport fallback. ### Plugins `telegram-notify.js` (not involved in request construction) ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start OpenCode with `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WEBSOCKETS=true`. 2. Use the OpenAI provider with `gpt-5.6-sol`. 3. In one tool round, read enough PNG images for the base64 tool-result attachments to exceed the WebSocket message-size limit (six 1920x1080 PNGs totaling about 17.4 MB reproduced it here). 4. Continue the turn so OpenCode sends the next `response.create`. 5. Observe five consecutive code 1009 errors before HTTP fallback succeeds. ### Screenshot and/or share link No public share link. The raw error and measured payload sizes are included above. ### Operating System Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 host; Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2) ### Terminal PowerShell 7 launcher; headless `opencode serve` running in WSL2

signal.title: [Bug] Agent loop produces duplicate responses due to non-monotonic MessageID comparison
signal.text: ## Description Agent loop fails to exit after `finish=stop` when the assistant message ID is lexicographically smaller than the user message ID, causing a duplicate LLM call and a second assistant response. In `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, the `runLoop` function uses a **string comparison** to decide whether to break the loop: ```typescript if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // string lexicographic comparison ) { break } ``` `MessageID.ascending()` generates IDs like `msg_f93b221d1...`. These IDs are **not guaranteed to be lexicographically monotonic**. When the assistant message ID happens to sort before the user message ID, the condition `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` evaluates to `false`, the loop does not break, and a second LLM call is made — producing a duplicate assistant response. This only affects agents that return `finish=stop` without tool calls (e.g. a plan-mode / discussion agent). Agents that use `finish=tool-calls` follow a different code path and are unaffected. ## Concrete evidence Session with 5 consecutive duplicate pairs. Each pair: same `parentID`, two `finish=stop` assistant messages, gap of 2–32ms between them. | User message ID | First assistant ID | `user.id < asst1.id` | Second assistant ID | `user.id < asst2.id` | |---|---|---|---|---| | `msg_f93b221d1...` | `msg_f93b221b9...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93b2853f...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93b7b78b...` | `msg_f93b7b748...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93b7efa2...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93bb731c...` | `msg_f93bb72da...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93bbd637...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93c03ac5...` | `msg_f93c03a9e...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93c0b842...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93c23126...` | `msg_f93c230ef...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93c26a5d...` | `true` ← loop breaks | In all 5 cases, the first assistant message's ID is lexicographically **smaller** than the user's, so the loop runs one extra iteration and produces a second response. ## Plugins oh-my-openagent@latest ## OpenCode version 1.18.5 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use an agent that responds with text only (no tool calls), returning `finish=stop` directly. 2. Send a message. In ~some cases (when `MessageID.ascending()` produces an assistant ID that sorts before the user ID), the agent will respond twice with similar but slightly different content. 3. The issue is intermittent because it depends on ID generation, but happens frequently in sessions with many turns. ## Suggested fix Replace the string ID comparison with a more reliable ordering check. Options: - Compare by `time.created` timestamps instead of ID strings - Use a numeric counter that is guaranteed monotonic - Or at minimum, don't use the ID comparison as the loop exit gate — `finish=stop` (when not `tool-calls` and no pending tool calls) should be sufficient to break ## Operating System macOS 15.7.7 (x64) ## Terminal OpenChamber (Electron app, opencode v1.18.5)

signal.title: Desktop 1.18.12: sessions spanning the 2026-08-14 message-ID wrap stop accepting messages (loop exits at step=0)
signal.text: ### OpenCode Desktop 1.18.12: sessions spanning the 2026-08-14 message-ID wrap stop accepting messages (agent loop exits at step=0) **Environment**: Windows 11 · OpenCode Desktop 1.18.12 (embedded sidecar server) · SQLite storage. ## Symptom Since `2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`, sessions whose last assistant message was created *before* that moment can no longer receive messages: - Sending a message writes the user text to the DB, but the agent loop exits immediately (`loop ... step=0` → `exiting loop` in the log) and never calls the LLM — the conversation "ends" instantly with no reply. - After reloading the session, the sent message appears out of order / missing, because the UI renders messages sorted by ID. - New sessions created after the wrap work normally, which made it look like a single broken conversation. ## Root cause (问题原因) Message/part IDs are generated by the `ascending()` helper: ```ts const current = BigInt(timestamp) * 0x1000n + BigInt(counter); // ID = 48-bit hex of (timestamp << 12 | counter) + 14 random base62 chars ``` The embedded time field is only 36 bits: `Date.now() mod 2^36`, which wraps every `2^36` ms ≈ **2.18 years**. The wrap occurred at `Date.now() = 26 × 2^36 = 1,786,706,395,136 ms = 2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`: - IDs generated just before the wrap start with `msg_ffff...` (high lexicographic value) - IDs generated just after the wrap start with `msg_0001...` (low value) In the run loop the "nothing to do" check is roughly: ```ts if (lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasPendingToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id) { log("exiting loop"); break; } ``` For an affected session, the pre-wrap assistant message (`msg_ffff...`) sorts *after* the freshly sent user message (`msg_0001...`), so `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` evaluates true and the loop concludes the newest message was already answered — it never runs. ## Reproduction 1. In a session, exchange at least one assistant reply before `2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`. 2. After that time, send a new message in that same session. 3. Observed: the message row is persisted, the loop logs `step=0` then `exiting loop`, no assistant reply is produced, and the rendered order is broken after refresh. This affects (a) sessions with messages on both sides of the wrap, and (b) sessions whose last message is a pre-wrap assistant reply when the user sends after the wrap. Any long-lived session will hit it again at the next wrap. ## Workaround applied (解决办法) Because restarting/updating cannot fix the stored ordering, I rewrote the affected sessions' message/part IDs in SQLite to a monotonic scheme (backup taken via `VACUUM INTO` first, IDs regenerated in `time_created` order, `parentID`/JSON references and event data remapped, foreign keys verified). After that, the loop proceeds normally again. ## Suggested fix - Stop encoding the time modulo 2^36 — use a full-width timestamp (or a wider ID), so IDs stay monotonic across the wrap boundary; and/or - Make the loop-completion check and UI ordering compare `time_created` (with ID only as a tiebreaker) instead of lexicographic ID order. --- *This issue was automatically created by an AI assistant on behalf of a user (auto-generated report: root cause analysis, workaround, and suggested fix were compiled by the assistant; reproduction steps verified against the local database).*

signal.title: Remote MCP server using Streamable HTTP (Supabase) fails on Linux with SSE 405 in runtime — persists in v1.17.11
signal.text: ## Description Remote MCP servers that migrated to Streamable HTTP (POST-only) fail on Linux at runtime with `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)`, even though the initial handshake succeeds. Reproduced with Supabase's hosted MCP (`mcp.supabase.com/mcp`, server v0.8.1). - `opencode mcp list` reports the server as `✓ connected` - `opencode mcp debug supabase-DEV` returns `HTTP response: 200 OK` and `Server info: supabase v0.8.1` - But in the TUI, the server keeps emitting `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)` This looks like the same root cause as #24946 (closed without a fix commit) and the open feature #28567. Filing a fresh report because it still reproduces on the latest release (v1.17.11) with a widely-used server. Note: #5636 (Figma 405) appears to be a different issue (client_name whitelist in dynamic OAuth), not a transport problem. ## Plugins None. ## OpenCode version v1.17.11 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure the Supabase remote MCP with a Bearer PAT (CI pattern from Supabase's own docs): ```json { "mcp": { "supabase-DEV": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=<project-ref>", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <personal-access-token>" }, "enabled": true } } } ``` 2. Start opencode and open the TUI → the server shows `SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)`. 3. `opencode mcp list` says `✓ connected`; `opencode mcp debug supabase-DEV` says `200 OK`. Direct curl against the endpoint with the same token: - `GET /mcp` → `405 Method Not Allowed` - `POST /mcp` with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` → `200 OK` So the server only speaks Streamable HTTP (POST); the handshake succeeds, but opencode's runtime transport keeps attempting GET/SSE. There's no way to force Streamable HTTP from config: the remote MCP `type` enum in `https://opencode.ai/config.json` is only `["remote"]` (no `"http"`/`"sse"` toggle). Supabase's docs show `"type": "http"` for clients that expose that field (Claude Code, Cursor, AI SDK), but opencode doesn't expose it. ## Screenshot and/or share link N/A (curl + `mcp debug` output above). ## Operating System Linux ## Terminal Alacritty

signal.title: TUI SIGILL (ud2) in OpenTUI drawTextBuffer when compositor scale jumps to 4
signal.text: ## Summary An idle OpenCode TUI aborts with `SIGILL` (`ud2`) the instant the compositor scales the monitor up to 4. This has happened twice, weeks apart, on two OpenCode versions, at the **same instruction pointer** and on the **same second** as the scale-to-4 event. This is **not** a missing-CPU-feature SIGILL. The faulting instruction is a deliberate `ud2` abort in the bundled Bun runtime, reached from OpenTUI's text-buffer draw path. Same abort site as #41483 (`opencode+0x2407064` / `libopentui.so+0x1d061d`), but a different trigger: a healthy local `foot` session that had already been running for ~56 minutes, not a partial capability handshake at startup. ## What happened 1. Started `opencode --auto` in foot on Hyprland (18:38). 2. Worked in a session, then left the TUI idle (last session write 18:56:40). 3. Scaled the external display **DP-1 from 3.13 → 4**. 4. Kernel recorded the abort on that same second: ``` Aug 12 19:34:41 traps: opencode[3769384] trap invalid opcode ip:2607064 ``` The process dumped core (`si_code: ILL_ILLOPN`). No OOM, 37 GiB free. ## Reproduction Reliable on this machine whenever OpenCode's TUI is open and the monitor is scaled **to 4**. 1. Hyprland + foot, OpenCode TUI running (`opencode --auto` is enough; session can be idle). 2. External display: Apple Pro Display XDR, `6016x3384@60`. 3. Scale DP-1 up through 2 → ~3.13 → **4**. 4. OpenCode dies immediately with `SIGILL`. Logical resolution at those scales: | scale | logical size | |------:|--------------| | 2 | 3008×1692 | | 3.13 | 1920×1080 | | **4** | **1504×846** | Going 2 → 3.13 did **not** kill it. The abort is on the step to 4. ## Two hits, same abort, same trigger | when | version | command | scale event (same second) | |------|---------|---------|---------------------------| | 2026-08-04 19:27:23 CEST | 1.18.11 | `opencode --auto` | DP-1 3.20 → 4 | | 2026-08-12 19:34:41 CEST | 1.18.16 | `opencode --auto` | DP-1 3.13 → 4 | Both cores have **identical offsets**: ``` #0 opencode + 0x2407064 ; ud2 #1 opencode + 0x2405266 #2 opencode + 0x32dd8bf ; napi_internal_suppress_crash_on_abort_if_desired #3 opencode + 0x44e35ad #4 libc.so.6 + 0x3e6f0 ; __restore_rt #5 libopentui.so + 0x1d061d ``` That is the same `#0`/`#5` pair reported in #41483. ## Symbolized OpenTUI frame `libopentui.so` is still on disk (`/tmp/.9adb5cbffaf2ed8f-00000000.so`, not stripped, has DWARF). `addr2line` on frame #5: ``` buffer.OptimizedBuffer.trySetTransparentTextCellFast packages/core/src/zig/buffer.zig:896 called from: OptimizedBuffer.drawTextBufferInternal buffer.zig:1659 OptimizedBuffer.drawTextBuffer buffer.zig:1274 lib.bufferDrawTextBufferView lib.zig:2521 ``` The instruction at that offset is a cell-buffer load inside the fast path (`cmpl $0xff, (%rsi,%rcx,4)`), not a SIMD op. Faulting bytes in the main binary: ``` 260705f: call 0x2634e80 ; noreturn abort helper 2607064: ud2 ; <- RIP 2607066: int3 int3 int3 ... ``` Classic Zig/Bun "noreturn returned" / panic abort, which the kernel reports as `trap invalid opcode`. ## Inference (not proven) Scale 3.13 → 4 shrinks the logical viewport by ~22% and delivers a SIGWINCH / `TIOCSWINSZ` to foot. OpenTUI then redraws. `trySetTransparentTextCellFast` indexes `self.buffer.char[index]` with no bounds check; `OptimizedBuffer.resize` reallocs those arrays. A draw that still holds an index computed against the pre-resize width/height would trip a Zig safety panic, which becomes this `ud2`. I have not single-stepped the panic reason (no panic string in the journal). The timestamp match + the symbolized draw path is the evidence. ## Ruled out - OOM / resource exhaustion - AVX / "baseline binary on old CPU" (Intel Core Ultra X7 358H, avx2+; the opcode is `ud2`, not EVEX) - A crash in the herdr OpenCode plugin — it is installed, but it is not on the crashing stack - `--auto` itself (that is just how the agent is launched; the abort is in the renderer) ## Environment - **opencode** 1.18.16 (previous hit: 1.18.11), installed via mise - **Bun** v1.3.14 (Linux x64 baseline), bundled - **OpenTUI** native `libopentui.so` extracted to `/tmp/.9adb5cbffaf2ed8f-00000000.so` - **OS** Arch Linux, kernel `7.1.5-arch1-1-ptl`, glibc 2.44 - **compositor** Hyprland 0.56.2 - **terminal** foot 1.27.0, JetBrainsMono Nerd Font 9 - **display** Apple Pro Display XDR `DP-1` 6016×3384@60 - **CPU** Intel Core Ultra X7 358H ## Expected A compositor scale change (or any SIGWINCH / resize) should reflow the TUI. It should not abort the process. ## Workaround Do not scale the monitor to 4 while OpenCode is open, or close OpenCode first. Session data in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` survived; the crash was during an idle redraw. ## Related - #41483 — identical `ud2` / `libopentui+0x1d061d`, trigger is a partial capability handshake at **startup** - #38199 — TUI crash on extreme shrink (~2×1); Bun segfault, different stack - anomalyco/opentui#971 — OpenTUI `bufferDrawBox` panic on grapheme / clip

signal.title: fix(llm): handle truncated OpenAI tool arguments
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #36766 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? A truncated OpenAI Responses stream can cut a `function_call` mid-JSON inside its streamed arguments. Previously the parser failed the whole stream at `response.output_item.done` (and later again at the terminal event), losing the provider's `truncated` / `max_output_tokens` diagnosis. The fix defers the failure decision until the terminal response event, because truncation is only diagnosable there: - Streamed `function_call` arguments that fail to parse no longer abort the stream at `output_item.done`. The call is recorded as an `UnparsedTool` — only its id, name, and UTF-8 byte count are kept, never the argument contents — and settled when the terminal response event arrives. - `response.completed` with `truncated: true`, or `response.incomplete` with `incomplete_details.reason === "max_output_tokens"`, classify the tool as truncated and emit a `provider-error` with `classification: "truncated"` (new literal added to `ProviderFailureClassification`). - A clean terminal event with malformed JSON reports `Invalid JSON input for openai-responses tool call <name>` instead. - `response.failed`, `error`, and a stream that ends without a terminal event (`onHalt`) append the pending unparsed-tool diagnostics to the errors they already emit. An unparsed tool is never dispatched: no `tool-call` event is emitted for it. The parser never buffers argument contents, so provider-sent data is not leaked into diagnostics. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added a `truncated tool arguments` test group in `packages/llm/test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts` covering all five paths: `response.completed` + `truncated`, `response.incomplete` + `max_output_tokens`, clean completion with malformed JSON, `response.failed`, and stream end without a terminal event. Tests use deterministic scripted SSE, no live provider. - `bun test test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts` passes (5/5 in the new group). - `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/llm`. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR ### Related work Truncated tool arguments are addressed by several open PRs. This PR is the protocol-level detection half of #36766; #37220 covers the recovery half in the core session runner (fail the pending local tool call and ask the model to re-emit, capped at three) and explicitly defers adapter-level detection — the part this PR implements. Because an unparsed tool call emits no `tool-call` event, a runner-level recovery keyed off the parse failure of a dispatched call does not engage here; instead the classified `provider-error` surfaces at the terminal response event. #42303 improves the user-facing diagnostic for the same failure in the opencode session layer, and #39473 retries truncated AI SDK streams at the stream level (#37852). The file sets are disjoint, so the four PRs compose without merge conflicts.

signal.title: Client stalls at single-core 100% CPU during long sessions with many rapid tool-calling turns — unrecoverable except via SIGINT
signal.text: Title: Client stalls at single-core 100% CPU during long sessions with many rapid tool-calling turns — unrecoverable except via SIGINT ## Summary During a long-running session involving a background job monitored via repeated short tool-calling turns, the OpenCode client stalls completely — no partial output, no tool call, nothing — for 20+ minutes. `Escape` does not cancel the stalled turn. Only killing the process from the terminal (`Ctrl+C`) recovers, requiring the session to be resumed afterward. Confirmed reproducible twice in the same day, same workflow signature. ## Environment - Provider: `github-copilot`, model: `claude-sonnet-5` - Platform: Linux (see full env details on request) - Session was long-running (~1.5h+) at the time of the stall, with substantial accumulated context (`cache.read` ~248,000 tokens by the time of the incident) ## Reproduction pattern 1. Start a long-running background job (in this case via `tmux new -d -s NAME '<command> | tee log'`). 2. Poll it repeatedly from the agent in short tool-calling turns (in this case: ~12-13 turns of `sleep 115; tmux list-sessions; cat log`, each turn ~2 minutes apart). 3. After the background job actually completes (~20-25 min in), the *next* agent turn — which should be cheap (just reading a finished log / detecting the tmux session ended) — instead stalls completely for 20+ minutes before producing any output at all. ## Evidence gathered (from `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) Querying the local SQLite session DB (`message`, `part`, `event` tables) for the stalled turn showed: - The stalled message's own `time.created` timestamp was ~23.5 minutes **before** its own first `part` (not even a `step-start` part) appeared. This rules out "a tool/bash call took a long time to execute" — the stall happened before the turn even began producing anything. - The eventual token/cost breakdown for that same message (once it finally completed) was: `input: 2, output: 426, reasoning: 0, cache.read: 247987, cache.write: 597`, `finish: "tool-calls"`. This is a **cheap**, almost entirely cache-hit request — model inference for 426 output tokens should take seconds, not 23+ minutes. - This rules out a slow/expensive model generation as the cause of the wall-clock delay. ## Key additional fact: CPU was pinned at 100% on a SINGLE core during the stall (both occurrences) This is the detail that rules out "waiting on a slow/stalled network response" (which would show near-zero CPU, blocked on I/O) and instead points to **a synchronous, non-yielding operation blocking the client's single-threaded main/event-loop**. Single-core saturation + a completely unresponsive UI (Escape doesn't register at all) is consistent with the JS/Bun main thread being busy in a tight loop or an O(n²)-or-worse computation, not legitimate parallel work and not I/O wait. `Escape` failing to cancel is consistent with this: if the main event loop is blocked synchronously, it cannot process the keypress event that would trigger a cancel action. `Ctrl+C` works because the terminal's line discipline delivers `SIGINT` to the process at the OS level, independent of whether the app's own event loop is currently responsive — the process then dies (unhandled/stuck signal → default termination), which matches needing to "resume the session" afterward rather than a graceful cancel. ## Hypothesis (unconfirmed — I don't have access to the OpenCode source to verify) Given the correlation with (a) a large accumulated context (`cache.read` ~248k tokens) and (b) many rapid successive short tool-calling turns in the same session, I suspect some client-side bookkeeping step that runs synchronously on the main thread and scales with conversation/context size (e.g. serialization, token/cache accounting, or persistence to the local SQLite DB) has worse-than-linear complexity, and becomes a multi-minute main-thread stall once a session crosses some size/turn-count threshold. I have not been able to locate the specific code path causing this. ## Request - Any pointers to where in the codebase a per-turn synchronous operation might scale with session size would help narrow this down further. - In the meantime, is there a supported way to reliably interrupt a stalled turn without killing the whole client process? (`Escape` did not work in either occurrence.) ## Diagnostic method for anyone else hitting this Query `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` directly: ```sql -- find message.time_created (turn issued) vs its parts' time_created (turn actually starts producing output) SELECT m.id, m.time_created, (SELECT MIN(p.time_created) FROM part p WHERE p.message_id = m.id) as min_part, (SELECT MAX(p.time_created) FROM part p WHERE p.message_id = m.id) as max_part FROM message m WHERE m.session_id = '<session_id>' ORDER BY m.time_created; -- pull full token/cost breakdown for a specific stalled message from the event log SELECT data FROM event WHERE aggregate_id = '<session_id>' AND type = 'message.updated.1' AND data LIKE '%<message_id>%' ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1; ``` Happy to provide the exact (anonymized) query outputs from both occurrences if useful.
